records.title: Arc<Mutex<T>>
records.summary: Combine atomic shared ownership with exclusive guarded access to mutable state across threads.

records.title: async and await
records.summary: Language syntax that constructs futures and yields at explicit await points while preserving sequential-looking control flow.

records.title: Enums and pattern matching
records.summary: Nominal variant types paired with pattern-based control flow over their possible shapes.

records.title: Expression-oriented evaluation
records.summary: Most Rust evaluation forms are expressions that produce values; statements primarily sequence expression evaluation.

records.title: Future
records.summary: A lazy computation that an executor polls toward an eventual output.

records.title: Generic parameters
records.summary: Parameterize functions, types, and impls over types while preserving compile-time checking at every concrete use.

records.title: HashMap<K, V>
records.summary: Key/value collection supporting keyed lookup, insertion, ownership-aware access, and entry-based updates.

records.title: Option<T>
records.summary: Represent a value that may be absent without carrying an error cause.

records.title: Question-mark propagation
records.summary: Extract success or return early with a compatible converted failure through the enclosing residual contract.

records.title: Result<T, E>
records.summary: Represent either a successful value or a recoverable failure value that callers must handle or propagate.

records.title: Send and Sync
records.summary: Marker contracts for safely transferring ownership between threads and sharing references between threads.

records.title: Slices
records.summary: Non-owning views over contiguous elements, represented by a reference plus range/length semantics.

records.title: String and &str
records.summary: Owned growable UTF-8 text and borrowed UTF-8 string slices with byte-aware traversal boundaries.

records.title: Struct types
records.summary: Custom nominal types that package related typed fields as a meaningful domain value.

records.title: Rust test harness
records.summary: Discover #[test] functions, execute them as a test binary, capture outcomes, and report failures.

records.title: Native threads
records.summary: Spawn operating-system threads with closures and coordinate their completion through join handles or scoped lifetimes.

records.title: Traits
records.summary: Declare shared method behavior that types implement and generic APIs can require.

records.title: Unsafe Rust
records.summary: Language constructs that declare or discharge safety obligations the compiler cannot verify.

records.title: Vec<T>
records.summary: Growable contiguous same-typed sequence with explicit panicking or optional access choices.

nodes.title: Bounded-pass Bellman-Ford
nodes.summary: Relax every edge for at most V-1 passes, optionally stop when unchanged, then test for a source-reachable negative cycle.
nodes.invariant: After pass i, every shortest source path with at most i edges has its correct distance; all finite estimates remain witnessed path upper bounds.
selectionCues: negative edges are permitted
source-reachable negative-cycle detection is required
O(VE) fits the workload

complexityBounds.time: O(VE), with safe early exit when a full pass changes nothing

nodes.title: FIFO layered graph traversal
nodes.summary: Use VecDeque and discover-on-enqueue to compute reachability, minimum edge counts, and parent paths from a source.
nodes.invariant: Before dequeuing distance d, all queued vertices have distance d or d+1; each discovered vertex has one valid parent path of its assigned distance and no undiscovered shorter path exists.
selectionCues: minimum number of unweighted edges is required
level-by-level discovery matters
all edges have equal traversal cost

complexityBounds.time: O(V+E) with adjacency lists and discover-on-enqueue

nodes.title: Bounded priority frontier
nodes.summary: Maintain only the best k candidates using a heap whose root is the current eviction boundary.
nodes.invariant: After processing prefix [0,i), the heap contains exactly the best min(k,i) candidates under the full deterministic rank, and its root is the worst retained candidate.
selectionCues: only top/bottom k rather than total order is needed
k is materially smaller than n
each new candidate can be compared with the retained boundary

complexityBounds.time: O(n log k) with O(log k) replacement

nodes.title: BST ordered descent and pruning
nodes.summary: Follow only the child subtree whose inherited key interval can contain the target or ordered neighbor.
nodes.invariant: If a valid answer exists, it lies within the current subtree or recorded predecessor/successor candidate under inherited bounds; the discarded subtree cannot improve it.
selectionCues: global BST order is established
one key or ordered neighbor/range boundary is requested
cost is stated in h

nodes.title: Constraint-guided backtracking
nodes.summary: Enumerate choices depth-first, reject impossible partial states, emit complete solutions, and restore mutable state.
nodes.invariant: On entry, state is exactly the chosen prefix and satisfies all checked constraints; on return, caller-visible mutable state equals its entry state.
selectionCues: the answer is one or all assignments/sequences
choices form a finite search tree
partial violations can be detected soundly

complexityBounds.time: O(number of visited search states × transition/check cost), output-sensitive
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(search depth + mutable path/state), excluding output

nodes.title: Converging two pointers
nodes.summary: Move one of two monotone endpoints according to sorted/dominance information until all relevant pairs or merge choices are resolved.
nodes.invariant: Before each step, every candidate excluded outside the active endpoints has been evaluated or proven unable to beat/satisfy the current answer; at least one endpoint strictly advances.
selectionCues: ordered values make one endpoint move logically dominant
the candidate space can be discarded by row/column-like monotonicity
both endpoints move at most n times

nodes.title: DFS cycle-certified topological traversal
nodes.summary: Explore directed dependencies depth-first with active/finished state, returning either a cycle witness or reverse finish order.
nodes.invariant: Active vertices equal the current directed DFS path; a vertex finishes only after all outgoing neighbors finish, so reverse finish order respects every edge if no active-edge cycle was found.
selectionCues: directed dependency validation is required
a cycle witness or topological order is the result
whole-graph outer-loop coverage is explicit

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(V) state/parents/output plus O(depth) call or explicit stack

nodes.title: Lazy-heap Dijkstra
nodes.summary: Relax nonnegative weighted edges from the current minimum distance and skip obsolete heap records.
nodes.invariant: Every finite estimate is a real path upper bound; after a non-stale minimum entry is settled under nonnegative weights, its distance is final.
selectionCues: single-source weighted shortest paths
all edges are validated nonnegative
adjacency plus priority queue fits the input size

complexityBounds.time: O((V+E) log E) with lazy BinaryHeap entries
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(V+E) worst-case adjacency, tables, and duplicate heap records

nodes.title: Earliest-finish compatible interval selection
nodes.summary: Sort by finish time and repeatedly take the next interval compatible with the last selected one to maximize unweighted count.
nodes.invariant: After each selection, there exists an optimal completion containing the chosen prefix, and its last selected finish is no later than the aligned optimum's finish.
selectionCues: objective is maximum number of compatible intervals
all selected intervals have equal unit value
endpoint compatibility and ties are explicit

complexityBounds.time: O(n log n) sort plus O(n) scan

nodes.title: Exact binary lookup
nodes.summary: Use ordered random access to find any exact match or its insertion point while preserving a shrinking candidate interval.
nodes.invariant: Before each iteration, every element equal to the target lies within [lo, hi), and every eliminated index is provably less or greater under the same order.
selectionCues: input is already sorted or preprocessing is justified
the query needs any exact match or insertion point
random-access comparisons are available

nodes.title: FIFO frontier
nodes.summary: Enqueue discovered work at the back and process the earliest waiting item from the front.
nodes.invariant: The deque front-to-back contains exactly pending items in eligibility order, and removal always selects the earliest eligible live item.
selectionCues: arrival/discovery order must be preserved
new work joins after existing work
front removals are frequent

complexityBounds.time: O(items + allowed reenqueues) with amortized O(1) end operations

nodes.title: Fractional value-density fill
nodes.summary: Sort divisible supplies by value per capacity unit and exhaust higher density before lower density until capacity is filled.
nodes.invariant: After each prefix, all used capacity comes from available material of no lower density than any unused material, so an exchange cannot improve the allocation.
selectionCues: items are continuously divisible
objective and constraints are linear in amount
density comparison avoids unsafe floating ordering

complexityBounds.time: O(n log n) sort plus O(n) fill

nodes.title: Frequency map
nodes.summary: Associate each canonical key with its occurrence count or other accumulated per-key state.
nodes.invariant: After processing prefix [0, i), map[key] equals the exact number of occurrences of key in that prefix.
selectionCues: output or decision needs counts/per-key aggregates
expected hashing is acceptable
stable order is stored by a separate sequence when required

nodes.title: Incremental contiguous window
nodes.summary: Enumerate fixed windows or expand/shrink a feasible interval while adding and removing endpoint contributions exactly once.
nodes.invariant: State equals the exact aggregate of [left, right); every recorded answer is correct for previously completed windows, and endpoint movement preserves the problem's fixed-size or monotone-feasibility contract.
selectionCues: the answer concerns contiguous regions
fixed k permits rolling updates or the constraint changes monotonically
removing the left contribution is well-defined

complexityBounds.time: O(n) when each endpoint advances at most n and updates are O(1)

nodes.title: LIFO frontier
nodes.summary: Push unresolved nested/deferred state and resolve the most recent item first.
nodes.invariant: The stack from bottom to top contains exactly the live unresolved items in creation order, so the top is the only valid next nested/deferred item to resolve.
selectionCues: nested scopes or reverse undo order
the newest unresolved state must complete first
tail operations suffice

complexityBounds.time: O(n) when each item is pushed/popped at most once

nodes.title: Membership set
nodes.summary: Track whether a key has appeared when no associated count/value is required.
nodes.invariant: After processing prefix [0, i), the set contains exactly the distinct canonical keys from that prefix.
selectionCues: only presence/absence or uniqueness matters
expected hash cost is acceptable
output order is maintained separately if required

nodes.title: Monotone boundary search
nodes.summary: Find the transition between a true prefix and false suffix, such as a lower or upper duplicate bound.
nodes.invariant: All indices before lo are confirmed in the first partition, all indices at or after hi are confirmed in the second, and the transition lies in [lo, hi].
selectionCues: the predicate is monotone over indexed input
the answer is the first index entering or leaving a region
empty and all-one-side partitions have specified answers

nodes.title: Prefix range aggregate
nodes.summary: Precompute cumulative states once so many static half-open range sums use two boundary values.
nodes.invariant: prefix[i] equals the overflow-safe aggregate of input[0..i] under the declared operation; every valid query l..r is recovered by the operation's proven cancellation rule.
selectionCues: the sequence is static across many queries
the aggregate has required identity/cancellation behavior
O(n) preprocessing and storage are acceptable

complexityBounds.time: O(n) build and O(1) per range sum

nodes.title: Explicit-unit prefix trie
nodes.summary: Traverse one declared key unit per edge for exact membership and prefix enumeration under measured memory constraints.
nodes.invariant: After consuming i key units, the current node represents exactly the prefix of length i; terminal state is checked only after all units are consumed.
selectionCues: common-prefix lookup/enumeration is central
key unit and normalization contract are fixed
measured memory beats simpler sorted/hash alternatives

complexityBounds.time: O(L × child-lookup cost) for a key of L declared units, plus output
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(total stored key units) nodes/edges with representation-dependent constants

nodes.title: One-dimensional sequence DP
nodes.summary: Order positions and choose the best predecessor transition into each suffix/prefix state, with explicit unreachable/base state.
nodes.invariant: When state i is finalized in dependency order, its value/witness is optimal over all legal last transitions from already-correct predecessor states.
selectionCues: history is summarized by one position/index
overlapping predecessor subproblems recur
transitions form an acyclic order

complexityBounds.time: O(number of states × predecessors/choices per state)
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(number of states) or dependency-window compressed, plus witness

nodes.title: Single-pass prefix-state invariant
nodes.summary: Scan once while retaining only the state needed to summarize the processed prefix and update the best/current answer.
nodes.invariant: Before processing item i, state exactly summarizes items [0, i) and the recorded answer is correct for every candidate wholly contained in that prefix.
selectionCues: answer can be updated from prior prefix summary and current item
past raw items are unnecessary once summarized
order is processed left-to-right

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(1) or O(state size), excluding output

nodes.title: Sorted interval coalescing sweep
nodes.summary: Sort validated intervals by start and merge overlap or policy-defined adjacency in one pass.
nodes.invariant: Emitted ranges equal the canonical union of all completed components in the processed prefix; current equals the union of the final not-yet-emitted component.
selectionCues: output is a canonical union/coalescing
endpoint/touch policy is explicit
sorting mutation/allocation is acceptable

complexityBounds.time: O(n log n) sorting plus O(n) sweep

nodes.title: Structural recursive decomposition
nodes.summary: Solve a base structure directly and combine results from strictly smaller children or suffixes.
nodes.invariant: Every active call owns one well-formed subproblem; child calls receive strictly smaller subproblems and their contracts compose to the parent result.
selectionCues: input is recursively shaped
the proof follows subproblem structure
maximum depth is safely bounded or made explicit

complexityBounds.time: sum of per-call work over the call tree
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(maximum depth × live per-frame state), excluding output

nodes.title: Semantics-first tree traversal
nodes.summary: Visit every node in preorder, inorder, postorder, or level order according to when the node result becomes valid.
nodes.invariant: For each active/completed subtree, nodes already emitted or folded exactly match the selected traversal prefix, and each completed subtree result satisfies its local postcondition.
selectionCues: every node must be visited
parent/child result timing determines order
O(n) traversal is expected

complexityBounds.time: O(n) with O(1) local work per node
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(h) recursive/explicit DFS stack or O(width) level queue

nodes.title: Two-sequence prefix/suffix DP
nodes.summary: Use one index per sequence and transitions for aligned/substituted/deleted/inserted next units under an explicit string-unit/cost contract.
nodes.invariant: Each cell is the optimal cost for exactly its two declared prefixes/suffixes, derived from all legal final/next edit operations and correct neighboring states.
selectionCues: two ordered sequences must be aligned/compared
both remaining positions affect future choices
operation costs and units are explicit

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(nm) with witness, or O(min(n,m)) for value-only rolling rows

nodes.title: Incremental equivalence connectivity
nodes.summary: Map stable item IDs to parent/size arrays and answer connectivity while processing irreversible unions.
nodes.invariant: Items are connected exactly when compressed finds return the same valid root; each successful union reduces component count by one and preserves a forest.
selectionCues: operations add equivalence edges
queries ask same-component rather than route
deletions/direction/weights are absent

complexityBounds.time: O((n+m) alpha(n)) amortized for initialization plus m operations with rank/size and compression

nodes.title: 0/1 item-capacity DP
nodes.summary: Index by item boundary and remaining/used integral capacity; choose skip or take once when it fits.
nodes.invariant: After processing the declared item prefix, each capacity cell is the best value achievable by a subset of only those items; descending 1D updates preserve single use.
selectionCues: items are indivisible and usable at most once
capacity is a bounded nonnegative integer
pseudo-polynomial O(nC) is acceptable

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(nC) with direct witness or O(C) value-only with descending updates

nodes.title: Accumulator width and overflow policy
nodes.summary: Bound prefix/window totals independently of elements and use checked arithmetic or a justified wider representation.
nodes.definition: The numeric representation and failure behavior selected for intermediate and final aggregates under worst-case valid input.
nodes.nonExample: Summing many i64 values into i64 solely because every individual value fits.

nodes.title: Adjacency-list size and traversal cost
nodes.summary: Count V plus stored adjacency entries E under the declared direction/duplicate policy, including isolated vertices.
nodes.definition: A sparse graph representation whose traversal time is proportional to initialized vertices and scanned adjacency entries.
nodes.nonExample: Reporting O(E) while omitting isolated vertices or counting each undirected edge inconsistently.

nodes.title: Abstract behavior versus representation
nodes.summary: Specify access/removal order first, then choose a concrete Rust container from required operations and costs.
nodes.definition: The separation between an abstract data-type contract such as LIFO/FIFO and a storage implementation such as Vec, ring buffer, or linked nodes.
nodes.nonExample: Saying a queue must be a linked list.

nodes.title: Amortized cost
nodes.summary: Bound total cost across an operation sequence so occasional expensive operations have a justified average per operation.
nodes.definition: A deterministic sequence-level analysis assigning the total worst-case cost across operations, independent of an input probability distribution.
nodes.nonExample: Calling Vec push always O(1) while ignoring reallocation and the amortized marker.

nodes.title: Analysis and measurement
nodes.summary: Use asymptotic reasoning for scalable bounds and controlled measurements for constants, allocation, cache, and actual distributions.
nodes.definition: Complementary evidence where mathematical analysis predicts growth and reproducible experiments characterize a specified implementation/workload.
nodes.nonExample: Using one fast sample to claim a better asymptotic bound.

nodes.title: Asymptotic growth bound
nodes.summary: Describe resource growth for large inputs while separating upper, lower, and tight claims.
nodes.definition: A mathematical relation between an algorithm's resource function and a comparison function after constants and lower-order behavior are bounded appropriately.
nodes.nonExample: Claiming O(n) means the function executes exactly n operations.

nodes.title: Auxiliary space
nodes.summary: Count additional memory used by the algorithm separately from input and required output storage.
nodes.definition: Peak extra working storage as a function of input size under an explicitly stated treatment of recursion, copies, and output.
nodes.nonExample: Calling a cloned input in-place because the mutation happens on the clone.

nodes.title: Sound partial-state pruning
nodes.summary: Reject a partial state only when every possible completion violates a stated constraint.
nodes.definition: A necessary impossibility proof that removes a subtree without removing a valid answer.
nodes.nonExample: Discarding a branch because a heuristic score looks unfavorable when the contract asks for all solutions.

nodes.title: Choose-explore-undo restoration
nodes.summary: Each mutable choice has a paired undo so every sibling begins from the same parent state, including early exits.
nodes.definition: An observational-equivalence invariant over a depth-first choice search.
nodes.nonExample: Popping a path only on normal return while a found/error branch returns early.

nodes.title: Bellman-Ford pass and cycle invariant
nodes.summary: After i full edge passes, shortest paths using at most i edges are represented; a further improvement after V-1 passes proves a reachable negative cycle.
nodes.definition: A bounded repeated-relaxation proof for negative edges and source-reachable negative-cycle detection.
nodes.nonExample: Declaring a cycle because any negative edge exists.

nodes.title: BFS layer and parent invariant
nodes.summary: The queue processes nondecreasing unweighted distance and every discovered non-source parent proves a path one edge shorter.
nodes.definition: A FIFO frontier invariant establishing minimum edge count from the source and reconstructible parent paths.
nodes.nonExample: Using BFS distance as a minimum weighted cost.

nodes.title: Half-open binary-search invariant
nodes.summary: Maintain a shrinking [lo, hi) interval that contains every index still capable of satisfying the target predicate.
nodes.definition: A loop invariant over ordered random-access input where eliminated prefixes/suffixes provably cannot contain the desired exact match or boundary.
nodes.nonExample: Updating lo = mid on a nonempty interval and allowing the loop to stop shrinking.

nodes.title: Global BST ordering invariant
nodes.summary: Every key in a left/right subtree obeys inherited bounds, with duplicates handled by one declared policy.
nodes.definition: A recursive order constraint over all descendants, equivalent under a consistent policy to sorted inorder traversal.
nodes.nonExample: A root 10 with left child 5 whose right descendant is 12: local parent-child checks pass at 5 but the root bound fails.

nodes.title: Worst, best, average, and expected cases
nodes.summary: Tie a resource claim to maximum/minimum inputs, an explicit input distribution, or algorithmic randomness.
nodes.definition: The quantification or probability model over inputs/random choices used to interpret a cost function.
nodes.nonExample: Calling a typical hand-picked example the average case.

nodes.title: Operation cost model
nodes.summary: Name which primitive operations are counted and which representation/library assumptions make them constant, logarithmic, or linear.
nodes.definition: An explicit abstraction for the cost of comparisons, indexing, hashing, allocation, copying, arithmetic, or other operations used in an analysis.
nodes.nonExample: Counting source-code lines as time complexity.

nodes.title: DFS undiscovered-active-finished state
nodes.summary: Track whether a vertex is unseen, on the current recursion/explicit stack, or completely explored.
nodes.definition: A three-state traversal contract that distinguishes a directed back edge from an edge to a finished vertex.
nodes.nonExample: Using one visited boolean to claim which directed edge closes the active path.

nodes.title: Dijkstra settled-distance invariant
nodes.summary: With nonnegative edges, the minimum unsettled finite estimate removed from the priority queue equals its final shortest distance.
nodes.definition: The greedy finalization fact that fails when a later negative edge can improve a settled vertex.
nodes.nonExample: Finalizing a vertex in a graph containing an unvalidated negative edge.

nodes.title: Directed cycle witness
nodes.summary: An edge to an active ancestor plus parent/stack state reconstructs a concrete directed cycle.
nodes.definition: A verifiable failure artifact proving a directed graph is not acyclic.
nodes.nonExample: Reporting cycle because DFS sees any already visited neighbor.

nodes.title: DP state-transition cost model
nodes.summary: Total time is reachable state count times transition work per state plus setup/reconstruction; space counts live table/witness state.
nodes.definition: A cost derivation from exact state dimensions/domains and choices, not from nested-loop appearance alone.
nodes.nonExample: Calling a two-index table O(n) because one loop is hidden in recursion.

nodes.title: DP dependency DAG and evaluation order
nodes.summary: Every transition points to a strictly smaller/earlier state; memoization follows demand while tabulation follows a topological order.
nodes.definition: The acyclic graph of state dependencies that proves termination and legal table read order.
nodes.nonExample: Filling a table left-to-right while a transition reads an uncomputed right neighbor.

nodes.title: Memoization versus tabulation
nodes.summary: Top-down memoization evaluates reachable states once; bottom-up tabulation evaluates a declared order and can expose compression opportunities.
nodes.definition: Two evaluation strategies for the same proven recurrence and state graph, with different recursion/reachability/initialization tradeoffs.
nodes.nonExample: Using a mutable cache as a substitute for defining base states and dependencies.

nodes.title: Pseudo-polynomial numeric state
nodes.summary: A table dimension proportional to numeric capacity C is polynomial in C but may be exponential in the bit length used to encode C.
nodes.definition: A complexity boundary requiring both item count and numeric range/resource limits.
nodes.nonExample: Calling O(nC) strongly polynomial in the ordinary binary input length.

nodes.title: Deterministic DP witness reconstruction
nodes.summary: Store or recompute an optimal predecessor/choice under a total tie policy, then validate the produced witness against the table value.
nodes.definition: A path through optimal state transitions that materializes one feasible solution, not only its objective.
nodes.nonExample: Greedily reconstructing from final values without checking which transition achieved equality.

nodes.title: Base cases and exhaustive recurrence
nodes.summary: Define terminal states and minimize/maximize over every legal first/last decision, with checked unreachable sentinels.
nodes.definition: An equation whose alternatives partition or exhaust all feasible solutions and compose optimal subproblem values.
nodes.nonExample: A transition that skips one valid action or adds cost to an unreachable sentinel.

nodes.title: Dependency-safe space compression
nodes.summary: Retain only state layers still needed by future transitions, respecting in-place update direction and witness requirements.
nodes.definition: A liveness transformation of the dependency DAG that preserves recurrence semantics.
nodes.nonExample: Updating 0/1 capacity left-to-right and thereby reusing the same item multiple times.

nodes.title: Sufficient DP state
nodes.summary: A state stores exactly the context needed to determine legal future choices and the optimal continuation value.
nodes.definition: A quotient of partial histories whose members have identical remaining subproblem semantics.
nodes.nonExample: Knapsack state containing only item index while remaining capacity affects feasibility.

nodes.title: Union by size/rank plus path compression
nodes.summary: Attach the shallower/smaller root and compress find paths, analyzing the whole operation sequence amortized.
nodes.definition: The paired heuristics that keep forest paths extremely shallow with O(alpha(n)) amortized operation cost.
nodes.nonExample: Claiming worst-case constant time for each find solely because one call compresses its path.

nodes.title: Parent-forest representative invariant
nodes.summary: Each item follows parent links to one root representative; roots parent themselves and sets are exactly equal-root classes.
nodes.definition: A forest representation in an indexed parent vector with valid IDs and no non-root cycles.
nodes.nonExample: Linking arbitrary nodes in both directions and creating a parent cycle.

nodes.title: Disjoint-set partition contract
nodes.summary: Maintain a partition of known items under make, representative lookup, and irreversible set merge.
nodes.definition: An equivalence-relation data structure for insertion/merge connectivity, not path retrieval or deletion.
nodes.nonExample: Using find representatives as a route between two vertices.

nodes.title: Safe edge relaxation
nodes.summary: If u is reachable and d[u]+w(u,v) is checked and smaller, update d[v] and parent[v] to a real path witness.
nodes.definition: A monotone upper-bound improvement preserving that every finite estimate is the weight of a discovered source path.
nodes.nonExample: Adding a weight to infinity or updating only the distance without its parent witness.

nodes.title: Exact-match and insertion-point result
nodes.summary: An exact search returns one matching index or a valid insertion position, not a promised first duplicate.
nodes.definition: Rust binary_search Result semantics under a slice sorted consistently with the query comparator.
nodes.nonExample: Treating Ok(i) as the lower bound when multiple equal values exist.

nodes.title: Exchange and cut-and-paste proof
nodes.summary: Transform an arbitrary optimum to include the greedy choice without reducing objective or violating feasibility, then recurse on the remainder.
nodes.definition: A constructive comparison between greedy and optimal solutions that establishes a safe first choice.
nodes.nonExample: Replacing an optimal item without checking capacity, compatibility, or objective preservation.

nodes.title: FIFO order
nodes.summary: The next removal returns the earliest enqueued live item.
nodes.definition: A first-in, first-out access contract adding at a logical tail and removing from a logical head.
nodes.nonExample: Retrying the newest job before earlier waiting jobs.

nodes.title: Fixed-size overlapping window
nodes.summary: Visit every contiguous region of one positive length and update or recompute its value under an explicit short-input contract.
nodes.definition: The n-k+1 overlapping half-open subranges [i, i+k) for 0 < k <= n, with no windows when k exceeds n.
nodes.nonExample: Using chunks(k), whose regions do not overlap, to enumerate every length-k window.

nodes.title: Fractional versus indivisible choice boundary
nodes.summary: Divisibility permits proportional exchange by density; indivisible choices can strand capacity and invalidate that proof.
nodes.definition: The structural assumption that makes density-order exchange valid for fractional capacity allocation.
nodes.nonExample: Taking highest density whole items and claiming exact 0/1 optimality.

nodes.title: Frontier invariant
nodes.summary: The container holds exactly discovered or pending work not yet completed, ordered by the selected policy.
nodes.definition: A loop-boundary predicate relating pushed/enqueued items, removed items, remaining pending work, and processing order.
nodes.nonExample: Enqueueing the same retry twice without the invariant accounting for duplicates.

nodes.title: Graph direction and identity contract
nodes.summary: Declare vertex identity, directedness, self/parallel-edge behavior, missing references, and observable ordering.
nodes.definition: The domain-to-graph mapping that makes every adjacency and traversal claim unambiguous.
nodes.nonExample: Treating a prerequisite edge as bidirectional because both endpoint IDs appear.

nodes.title: Traversal determinism policy
nodes.summary: Specify start and neighbor order only when result order is observable; otherwise validate semantic properties across any valid order.
nodes.definition: A separation between algorithmic correctness and stable presentation/testing order.
nodes.nonExample: Snapshot-testing one DFS order while iterating an unordered map.

nodes.title: Discover-on-frontier insertion
nodes.summary: Mark a vertex and assign its parent/distance the first time it enters the frontier, not after duplicate work.
nodes.definition: The visited-state transition that ensures each vertex enters BFS once and owns one discovery witness.
nodes.nonExample: Marking on dequeue so converging predecessors enqueue the same vertex repeatedly.

nodes.title: Greedy choice property
nodes.summary: There exists an optimal solution compatible with the locally selected feasible choice at every step.
nodes.definition: A problem-specific theorem, not a generic consequence of selecting an extreme key.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming the largest immediate gain is globally optimal because it worked on one input.

nodes.title: Minimal greedy counterexample
nodes.summary: Exhaust small valid instances to falsify an unproved local rule and shrink the first failure to its essential constraints.
nodes.definition: A diagnostic artifact showing exactly which exchange or dominance premise fails, without pretending tests prove success universally.
nodes.nonExample: Concluding a rule is correct because exhaustive search passed only up to size five.

nodes.title: Validated half-open interval
nodes.summary: Represent [start,end) with start <= end and specify empty, overlap, containment, adjacency, and coalescing behavior.
nodes.definition: A range including its start and excluding its end, whose domain policy determines whether adjacent ranges are combined.
nodes.nonExample: Comparing end == next.start inconsistently between overlap tests and output merging.

nodes.title: Hash cost and arbitrary order
nodes.summary: Treat lookup as expected, include hashing/key/capacity costs, and never infer insertion or sorted order from standard hash iteration.
nodes.definition: The performance/order contract of hash-backed storage under its hasher, collision, capacity, and iteration implementation assumptions.
nodes.nonExample: Returning HashMap keys directly when the output contract requires first-seen order.

nodes.title: Hash and equality invariant
nodes.summary: Equal keys must hash equally and key equality/hash-relevant state must remain stable while stored.
nodes.definition: The logical contract connecting Eq and Hash so a key's bucket/probe identity is consistent for insertion and lookup.
nodes.nonExample: Changing a key field that participates in Eq/Hash while it remains in the map.

nodes.title: Binary-heap partial order
nodes.summary: Every parent is at least as extreme as its children, placing one extreme at the root without sorting siblings or iteration.
nodes.definition: A local order invariant over an implicit complete tree that supports path-local repair after extreme insertion/removal.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming the backing array or iterator is globally descending.

nodes.title: Heap operation and build costs
nodes.summary: Distinguish peek, pop, push assumptions, capacity growth, repeated extraction, and linear bulk heap construction.
nodes.definition: A method-specific cost model for the concrete priority workload, including heap size k rather than only input size n.
nodes.nonExample: Calling repeated sorted pops O(n) because peek is O(1).

nodes.title: In-place transformation and ownership
nodes.summary: Separate mutation of permitted input storage from clones, collected iterators, auxiliary state, and required output.
nodes.definition: An implementation/contract choice where the algorithm updates existing sequence storage while preserving required input/output and borrowing rules.
nodes.nonExample: Cloning the whole Vec and calling mutation of the clone O(1) auxiliary space.

nodes.title: Algorithm input size
nodes.summary: Define the variable or variables that measure the growing input before stating a bound.
nodes.definition: A problem-relevant measure such as element count, vertices/edges, digits, or multiple dimensions against which resource growth is expressed.
nodes.nonExample: Writing O(n) without saying what n measures.

nodes.title: Interval problem boundary
nodes.summary: Distinguish union/coalescing, maximum unweighted compatible subset, weighted scheduling, and resource-counting objectives.
nodes.definition: The exact objective and compatibility/weight/resource semantics that determine which interval algorithm and proof apply.
nodes.nonExample: Applying earliest finish to maximize arbitrary interval weights.

nodes.title: Sorted interval sweep invariant
nodes.summary: After processing a start-sorted prefix, output intervals are canonical/disjoint and current holds exactly the unfinished final union component.
nodes.definition: A one-pass correctness predicate maintained by extending the current range on overlap/policy adjacency or emitting it before a later disjoint range.
nodes.nonExample: Merging unsorted intervals while assuming no later range can bridge components.

nodes.title: Initialization, maintenance, termination proof
nodes.summary: Prove the invariant initially, prove one iteration preserves it, and combine it with termination to derive correctness.
nodes.definition: The inductive correctness argument connecting precondition, loop transitions, stopping condition, and postcondition.
nodes.nonExample: Checking the invariant on three test inputs.

nodes.title: LIFO order
nodes.summary: The next removal returns the most recently pushed live item.
nodes.definition: A last-in, first-out access contract with explicit empty behavior.
nodes.nonExample: Removing the oldest unmatched delimiter.

nodes.title: Sequential list access and full operation cost
nodes.summary: Count traversal, allocation, links, cache locality, and position discovery rather than quoting pointer rewiring alone.
nodes.definition: The end-to-end cost model for an ordered head-to-tail representation whose elements are not necessarily contiguous or randomly accessible.
nodes.nonExample: Calling insertion at an unknown middle position O(1) while omitting O(n) traversal.

nodes.title: Loop invariant
nodes.summary: State a property true before and after every iteration that connects processed state to the final specification.
nodes.definition: A predicate established before the loop, preserved by one arbitrary iteration, and strong enough with termination to imply the postcondition.
nodes.nonExample: A comment that merely restates what the loop body does.

nodes.title: Sorted multi-input merge invariant
nodes.summary: Maintain one frontier per sorted input and emit the least eligible next key while preserving global order and multiplicity/version policy.
nodes.definition: Before each emission, every unconsumed input suffix is sorted and no value behind any frontier can precede the chosen next output.
nodes.nonExample: Concatenating sorted runs without comparing their frontiers.

nodes.title: Monotone predicate partition
nodes.summary: All true elements precede all false elements, making their transition index searchable as a boundary.
nodes.definition: A sequence partitioned by predicate p into [true...] followed by [false...], including all-true, all-false, and empty cases.
nodes.nonExample: Searching a predicate whose truth values alternate across the input.

nodes.title: Optimization feasibility and objective contract
nodes.summary: Define candidate set, feasibility, maximize/minimize objective, tie/output semantics, and infeasible/empty behavior before selecting a rule.
nodes.definition: The mathematical comparison target against which local choices and proofs are judged.
nodes.nonExample: Saying choose best next without defining best final solution.

nodes.title: Total ordering contract
nodes.summary: Define a comparator or key whose equality and ordering are consistent for every value the algorithm may compare.
nodes.definition: A reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive, total comparison policy used consistently by sorting and searching, including an explicit policy for values such as floating-point NaN.
nodes.nonExample: Sorting with one key and searching with a comparator that orders the same records differently.

nodes.title: Owned recursive link
nodes.summary: Represent a single-owner acyclic next link as Option<Box<Node<T>>> with moves governing insertion/removal and automatic drop governing reclamation.
nodes.definition: A finite-sized recursive node topology where each heap node has one owning Box predecessor or root and an optional boxed successor.
nodes.nonExample: Adding Rc<RefCell<_>> to a singly owned chain with no alias requirement.

nodes.title: Monotone endpoint progress
nodes.summary: Give each pointer a precise boundary meaning and prove each update discards only states that cannot improve or satisfy the answer.
nodes.definition: An invariant/progress argument where one or more indices move in one direction over a sequence and the total number of moves is bounded by sequence length.
nodes.nonExample: Resetting the left pointer for every right pointer while claiming a linear scan.

nodes.title: Prefix aggregate algebra
nodes.summary: Constant-time range recovery needs an associative prefix operation and a valid way to remove the earlier prefix.
nodes.definition: The identity, associativity, and inverse/cancellation properties required by a chosen cumulative representation and range query.
nodes.nonExample: Subtracting two prefix maxima to obtain a range maximum.

nodes.title: Half-open prefix-sum identity
nodes.summary: Store prefix[0] = 0 and prefix[i+1] = prefix[i] + value[i], so sum(l..r) = prefix[r] - prefix[l].
nodes.definition: A cumulative array with one extra identity entry that converts a valid half-open range sum into the difference of two prefix states.
nodes.nonExample: Using prefix[r] - prefix[l] after defining prefix[i] as the sum through i inclusive.

nodes.title: Priority-queue access contract
nodes.summary: Insert candidates and repeatedly inspect/remove the item with the most extreme declared priority.
nodes.definition: An abstract container ordered by a priority relation rather than solely by insertion time or sequence index.
nodes.nonExample: Processing the earliest arrival regardless of its priority key.

nodes.title: Recursion depth and branching cost
nodes.summary: Analyze call-tree work, maximum live depth, per-frame state, output size, and overflow risk separately.
nodes.definition: A recursion cost model based on the number of calls/branches and maximum simultaneous frames rather than syntax.
nodes.nonExample: Calling a recursive solution O(n) solely because its input measure decreases by one.

nodes.title: Recursive progress contract
nodes.summary: Define base cases, a strictly decreasing measure, recursive subproblems, and return/combination semantics.
nodes.definition: A termination and correctness contract for calls over smaller structural or numeric state.
nodes.nonExample: Calling again after changing state without proving the measure decreased.

nodes.title: Recursive frame ownership
nodes.summary: Separate per-call parameters/locals from shared input, output, and mutable search state.
nodes.definition: The state visible to one activation and the ownership/borrowing boundary across child calls.
nodes.nonExample: Treating a shared mutable accumulator as if each call owned an independent copy.

nodes.title: Rooted tree and subtree
nodes.summary: Model one root, parent-child edges, leaves, depth, height, and recursively complete subtrees with an explicit empty case.
nodes.definition: A finite hierarchical structure where each non-root node has one parent and each node roots a disjoint recursive subtree.
nodes.nonExample: Treating a cyclic graph as a tree without visited-state handling.

nodes.title: Rust BTreeMap ordered-map contract
nodes.summary: Prefer the standard ordered map for total-order keys, ordered iteration, and ranges while keeping key order stable in storage.
nodes.definition: The stable standard-library ordered key/value map abstraction, distinct from an instructional binary-node implementation.
nodes.nonExample: Mutating an Ord-relevant interior field of a stored key and expecting the map to reorder itself.

nodes.title: Rust collection operation cost
nodes.summary: Read the exact standard-library operation, capacity, ownership, expected, and amortized semantics before importing a textbook bound.
nodes.definition: The resource and ownership behavior of a concrete Rust collection method, including shifts, resizing, hashing, iteration over capacity, and allocation.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming HashMap iteration is O(len) without checking the current API's capacity behavior.

nodes.title: Minimal Rust sequence-container choice
nodes.summary: Default to Vec, choose VecDeque for frequent front operations, and choose linked storage only from an evidenced contract.
nodes.definition: A workload-based decision using operation mix, ordering, contiguity, allocation, and ownership with the least sufficient standard container.
nodes.nonExample: Implementing a generic unsafe linked list for a FIFO exercise.

nodes.title: Rust BinaryHeap ordering contract
nodes.summary: Use max order by default, Reverse for min order, stable Ord-relevant state, and explicit deterministic ties.
nodes.definition: The standard-library priority semantics for Ord items, including arbitrary iteration and encapsulated logic errors if stored order changes.
nodes.nonExample: Mutating an interior priority field while an item remains in the heap.

nodes.title: Rust lazy priority updates
nodes.summary: Use Reverse over a deterministic distance/vertex key, push improvements, and discard popped entries stale against the distance table.
nodes.definition: A standard-library Dijkstra implementation strategy without mutable heap handles.
nodes.nonExample: Relaxing neighbors from every popped duplicate even after a better distance was recorded.

nodes.title: Rust owned binary tree
nodes.summary: Use Option<Box<Node<T>>> child links for a single-owner educational tree and borrow nodes during read-only traversal.
nodes.definition: A finite-sized recursive representation whose root owns every descendant through unique optional boxed links.
nodes.nonExample: Adding parent Rc<RefCell<_>> links when the exercise only needs downward traversal.

nodes.title: Finite Rust recursive type
nodes.summary: Break recursive size with pointer indirection and select Box for single ownership unless sharing is required.
nodes.definition: A nominal recursive type whose recursive fields have known-size pointer representation.
nodes.nonExample: An enum variant containing the same enum directly by value.

nodes.title: Rust slice sort contract
nodes.summary: Choose sort or sort_unstable from stability, allocation, mutation, comparator, and key-extraction requirements rather than habit.
nodes.definition: The observable standard-library guarantees for a selected Rust slice sorting method, separated from non-contractual implementation details.
nodes.nonExample: Using sort_unstable_by_key when equal-key input order is part of the result specification.

nodes.title: Rust string unit
nodes.summary: Choose bytes, Unicode scalar values, or user-perceived graphemes from the problem contract before indexing or counting.
nodes.definition: The semantic element used by a string algorithm, mapped explicitly to Rust bytes/byte offsets, chars/scalar values, or an external grapheme segmentation model.
nodes.nonExample: Calling str::len the number of visible characters.

nodes.title: Rust Vec stack
nodes.summary: Use push, pop, and last at the end of Vec for amortized constant LIFO operations.
nodes.definition: The standard contiguous growable sequence used through its efficient tail as a stack.
nodes.nonExample: Pushing at index zero and removing from index zero to emulate a stack.

nodes.title: Rust VecDeque queue/deque
nodes.summary: Use push_back/pop_front for FIFO or explicit end operations for a deque while respecting possible wrapped storage.
nodes.definition: A growable ring buffer providing logical front/back order and amortized constant operations at both ends.
nodes.nonExample: Taking only the first as_slices result and silently dropping wrapped elements.

nodes.title: Rust window indexing and borrowing
nodes.summary: Prefer shared slice windows or checked indices, validate zero-size semantics, and separate read-only views from mutation needs.
nodes.definition: The standard slice API and borrow/index behavior used to enumerate overlapping shared regions without allocation or invalid ranges.
nodes.nonExample: Calling windows(0) or expecting overlapping mutable windows from safe iteration.

nodes.title: Contiguous sequence indexing
nodes.summary: Use integer offsets over a fixed logical element unit and account for shifts, copies, and boundary conditions.
nodes.definition: Random access into an ordered contiguous sequence whose index range and element representation are explicit.
nodes.nonExample: Treating a HashMap as an array because integer keys are used.

nodes.title: Sort-versus-scan query trade-off
nodes.summary: Compare one-time ordering cost and mutation/allocation with query count, update rate, and per-query scan/search cost.
nodes.definition: A workload-level decision between direct linear work and preprocessing/indexing that enables cheaper repeated ordered queries.
nodes.nonExample: Sorting an unsorted vector solely to answer one membership query and claiming the query is O(log n) overall.

nodes.title: Sort stability
nodes.summary: Equal-key elements retain their relative input order only when the selected sorting contract guarantees stability.
nodes.definition: A tie-order guarantee over distinct records whose comparison keys are equal.
nodes.nonExample: Calling output stable merely because one run happened to preserve the ties.

nodes.title: Sorted permutation
nodes.summary: The output contains exactly the input elements and adjacent keys are nondecreasing under the chosen order.
nodes.definition: A sequence preserving input multiplicities while satisfying order(key[i - 1], key[i]) for every adjacent pair.
nodes.nonExample: Returning a sorted set when duplicate input elements must be retained.

nodes.title: Stays-ahead prefix proof
nodes.summary: Compare aligned greedy and optimal prefixes and prove the greedy partial state is never worse under a measure that yields final optimality.
nodes.definition: An inductive dominance proof whose prefix measure must imply the declared final objective.
nodes.nonExample: Comparing incomparable prefixes or a measure unrelated to final feasibility/value.

nodes.title: Subtree induction and fold
nodes.summary: Prove the base empty/leaf case and combine correct child results to establish the parent result.
nodes.definition: A recursive correctness argument where the postcondition for each subtree follows from recursively established child postconditions and local work.
nodes.nonExample: Saying recursion works because it visits everything without proving the combined result.

nodes.title: DAG topological-order contract
nodes.summary: Every directed edge u→v places u before v; a valid API rejects cyclic input rather than returning a partial/invalid order silently.
nodes.definition: A linear extension of dependency precedence defined only for directed acyclic graphs.
nodes.nonExample: Sorting vertex labels and calling the result topological without checking edges.

nodes.title: Maintained balance guarantee
nodes.summary: A separate structural invariant bounds height after updates; rotations/implementations are deferred.
nodes.definition: An update-preserved relationship between subtree sizes/heights that establishes h = O(log n) for the chosen tree family.
nodes.nonExample: Calling a tree balanced because one drawn example is symmetric.

nodes.title: Height-dependent tree cost
nodes.summary: Navigation/search follows at most one root-to-leaf path in O(h), where h may be linear without balance.
nodes.definition: A resource bound parameterized by the longest relevant descendant path rather than automatically by log node count.
nodes.nonExample: Calling lookup in an insertion-ordered chain O(log n).

nodes.title: Traversal processing order
nodes.summary: Choose whether a node is processed before, between, after its children, or by level from the result semantics.
nodes.definition: A deterministic visit/processing order over every node of a rooted tree, with child order specified when observable.
nodes.nonExample: Using preorder for an expression whose parent result requires both evaluated children.

nodes.title: Trie key-unit and child-layout cost
nodes.summary: Choose bytes or scalar values and dense/sparse children from the workload; count nodes, edges, terminal data, and allocation overhead.
nodes.definition: The representation contract that makes prefix operations correct and their time/space claims conditional.
nodes.nonExample: Allocating 256 children per node for a sparse Unicode vocabulary without measuring memory.

nodes.title: Trie prefix and terminal identity
nodes.summary: Edges encode key units and a terminal marker distinguishes an exact stored key from a merely traversable prefix.
nodes.definition: An uncompressed prefix tree in which common key prefixes share nodes while membership remains explicit.
nodes.nonExample: Returning exact-key success whenever traversal reaches the end of the query prefix.

nodes.title: Weighted shortest-path contract
nodes.summary: Declare direction, source, weight domain/sign, unreachable/overflow/negative-cycle states, path ties, and whether paths or distances are returned.
nodes.definition: The exact optimization and failure semantics that select a shortest-path method.
nodes.nonExample: Returning zero for unreachable and silently wrapping a path sum.

nodes.title: Window feasibility monotonicity
nodes.summary: Expanding or shrinking must change the constraint predictably enough to discard windows without revisiting endpoints.
nodes.definition: A problem property such as nonnegative additive contributions where endpoint movement has a one-directional effect on feasibility.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming removing the left value always reduces a sum when values may be negative.

nodes.title: Contiguous window state
nodes.summary: Represent exactly the elements in a half-open interval [left, right) and update aggregate state when either endpoint moves.
nodes.definition: A contiguous sequence region with explicit inclusivity and maintained state equal to the aggregate of precisely that region.
nodes.nonExample: Removing a left element from the aggregate after incrementing left twice.

nodes.title: Build-script execution boundary
nodes.summary: Review pre-build executable code, its rerun inputs, native prerequisites, and generated OUT_DIR outputs.
nodes.definition: The supply-chain and reproducibility boundary created when Cargo compiles and executes build.rs before the package build.
nodes.nonExample: Writing generated source into tracked src files on every build.

nodes.title: Feature resolution
nodes.summary: Trace additive feature activation across workspace, target, normal, dev, and build dependency edges.
nodes.definition: Cargo's selection and unification of named conditional capabilities and optional dependencies for a concrete command and resolver context.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming two features are mutually exclusive because the application treats them as modes.

nodes.title: Manifest requirement and lock resolution
nodes.summary: Separate authored dependency ranges and package metadata from Cargo's exact resolved dependency graph.
nodes.definition: Cargo.toml declares acceptable inputs; Cargo.lock records the selected versions/sources/checksums used until an intentional update.
nodes.nonExample: Manually editing Cargo.lock as the dependency policy source.

nodes.title: Versioned Cargo metadata automation
nodes.summary: Inspect workspace and resolution through cargo metadata JSON with an explicit format version.
nodes.definition: Machine-readable workspace interrogation that treats documented opaque fields as opaque and tolerates compatible additive fields.
nodes.nonExample: Parsing human cargo build output to discover workspace members.

nodes.title: Cargo build profiles
nodes.summary: Choose dev, test, release, or custom compiler settings from build purpose and measured operational needs.
nodes.definition: A workspace-root compiler configuration controlling optimization, debug information, assertions, overflow checks, and related build behavior.
nodes.nonExample: Copying maximum optimization settings before measuring build or runtime trade-offs.

nodes.title: Workspace ownership
nodes.summary: Centralize shared resolution, metadata, dependencies, lints, and profiles while keeping package boundaries explicit.
nodes.definition: The root/member contract that determines workspace membership, inheritance, default command scope, shared lockfile, and shared target output.
nodes.nonExample: A directory containing unrelated Cargo.toml files with no declared workspace.

nodes.title: Arrow typed physical array
nodes.summary: An array has one data type, logical length, null count, type-specific buffers, and optional child arrays or dictionary.
nodes.definition: A homogeneous logical sequence realized by a specified columnar memory layout.
nodes.nonExample: Reading arbitrary buffer bytes without the array's type, length, and offset.

nodes.title: Bounded Arrow batch execution
nodes.summary: Process repeated batches under explicit row/byte targets and account for variable-width and retained-buffer memory.
nodes.definition: A finite work and memory unit rather than an unbounded monolithic array.
nodes.nonExample: Collecting an entire stream into one RecordBatch because columnar storage is compact.

nodes.title: Checked Arrow typed access
nodes.summary: Resolve a field, verify its DataType, downcast the dynamic array safely, and propagate mismatch instead of panicking.
nodes.definition: The boundary from schema-erased Array to the concrete type a kernel requires.
nodes.nonExample: Calling unwrap on as_any().downcast_ref after checking only a column name.

nodes.title: Arrow offset-based values
nodes.summary: UTF-8, binary, and list layouts locate each logical value through checked adjacent offsets into a data buffer or child array.
nodes.definition: A length-plus-one monotonic offset sequence using the width declared by the Arrow type.
nodes.nonExample: Indexing Unicode strings by character count or using 32-bit offsets for data beyond their representable range.

nodes.title: Arrow RecordBatch invariants
nodes.summary: All columns match the ordered schema and share one row count; zero-column/empty behavior is handled deliberately.
nodes.definition: A rectangular schema-bound columnar execution unit.
nodes.nonExample: Combining a ten-row ID array and nine-row value array under a declared ten-row schema.

nodes.title: Arrow ordered schema contract
nodes.summary: Bind each ordered field name to its exact DataType, nullability, and metadata before constructing or consuming columns.
nodes.definition: The semantic contract that gives physical arrays column identity and compatibility.
nodes.nonExample: Treating matching column names as enough while integer width or nullability differs.

nodes.title: Arrow slice and retained-buffer cost
nodes.summary: A slice changes logical offset/length while sharing backing storage, so small views can retain much larger allocations.
nodes.definition: A zero-copy logical view whose memory lifetime follows shared buffers.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming slicing copies selected bytes and immediately frees the parent buffer.

nodes.title: Arrow validity and null semantics
nodes.summary: Validity bits, not masked value bytes, decide whether a slot is logically present; null storage may be unspecified.
nodes.definition: The per-slot presence contract independent of the values buffer.
nodes.nonExample: Reading zero from a null numeric slot and aggregating it as real data.

nodes.title: Bounded admission and overload policy
nodes.summary: Cap concurrent/in-flight items and choose wait, reject, sample/drop, coalesce, or spill semantics before capacity is exhausted.
nodes.definition: The boundary that prevents producer demand from becoming unbounded memory/work.
nodes.nonExample: Calling a channel unbounded and relying on the OOM killer as overload control.

nodes.title: End-to-end backpressure propagation
nodes.summary: A slow sink eventually delays or limits upstream admission across every bounded queue/state/output boundary.
nodes.definition: Demand/capacity feedback spanning the whole pipeline rather than one local queue.
nodes.nonExample: Bounding one queue while an upstream task accumulates an unbounded retry Vec.

nodes.title: Byte versus UTF-8 text boundary
nodes.summary: Choose Vec<u8> or String from the format contract; text decode is fallible and line delimiters are bytes with declared semantics.
nodes.definition: The first ingestion type decision separating arbitrary octets from valid UTF-8 content.
nodes.nonExample: Using read_to_string for a binary or unspecified-encoding file.

nodes.title: CAP behavior during network partition
nodes.summary: When a partition prevents required communication, document whether an operation refuses/times out to preserve atomic consistency or responds while risking a conflicting/stale history.
nodes.definition: The concrete degraded-mode decision induced by the theorem's consistency, availability, and partition model.
nodes.nonExample: Selecting consistency and availability on a slide while omitting what either side does after communication is cut.

nodes.title: Arrival, service, capacity, and queue latency
nodes.summary: Measure item/byte arrival and service distributions, burst size, utilization, queue occupancy/age, and sustained deficit.
nodes.definition: The workload model distinguishing finite burst absorption from unstable sustained overload.
nodes.nonExample: Doubling queue length and claiming throughput increased without changing consumer service rate.

nodes.title: Graceful bounded-channel termination
nodes.summary: Stop admission, close senders, drain or explicitly discard under policy, flush/commit effects, and make receiver disconnection visible.
nodes.definition: A finite shutdown state machine preserving or explicitly rejecting accepted work.
nodes.nonExample: Aborting workers while queued accepted items are silently lost.

nodes.title: Consistent state and source-position checkpoint
nodes.summary: Durably publish one recovery point pairing replay positions with all operator/window/timer/dedupe state that reflects exactly those positions.
nodes.definition: A globally usable recovery image, not a collection of unrelated local snapshots.
nodes.nonExample: Saving counters after record 100 with a source offset that resumes at record 90.

nodes.title: Client-observable consistency guarantee
nodes.summary: State guarantees as permitted histories—stale reads, read-your-writes, monotonic reads, causal visibility, or linearizability—under named timing and failure assumptions.
nodes.definition: A falsifiable constraint on values and operation order visible to clients, separate from replica count or marketing labels.
nodes.nonExample: Calling a store strongly consistent without a history-level claim or partition/timeout behavior.

nodes.title: CSV byte or UTF-8 field representation
nodes.summary: Use StringRecord for valid UTF-8 text contracts and ByteRecord when arbitrary bytes are legitimate, without lossy conversion by default.
nodes.definition: The encoding boundary for field access, trimming, Serde types, diagnostics, and downstream validity.
nodes.nonExample: Replacing invalid bytes with U+FFFD and calling the result an unchanged identifier.

nodes.title: Explicit CSV dialect
nodes.summary: Fix header, delimiter, quote/escape, terminator, comment, trim, and width behavior as source metadata.
nodes.definition: The syntactic configuration needed to turn bytes into logical CSV records without guesswork.
nodes.nonExample: Calling every comma-delimited-looking file RFC CSV while accepting semicolons and arbitrary escapes implicitly.

nodes.title: Header-to-schema mapping
nodes.summary: Validate normalized names for duplicates, required/missing/unexpected fields and map columns deterministically independent of order when allowed.
nodes.definition: The structural contract linking source column identity to wire DTO fields before row conversion.
nodes.nonExample: Zip expected fields to positions after silently dropping a duplicate header.

nodes.title: Logical record versus physical line
nodes.summary: Quoted fields may span physical lines; errors and replay identify the parser's logical record plus byte/line position.
nodes.definition: A parser-complete row boundary under dialect rules, not a raw newline split.
nodes.nonExample: Reporting embedded-newline row fragments as two independent failed records.

nodes.title: Missing, empty, whitespace, and null semantics
nodes.summary: Define per-column whether absent, zero-length, whitespace-only, or sentinel text maps to error, None, default, or real string.
nodes.definition: A schema-level distinction applied after syntactic parsing and before domain validation.
nodes.nonExample: Mapping every empty string and absent field to the same default zero.

nodes.title: Bounded row quarantine policy
nodes.summary: Emit redacted source/record/field/class metadata and stop or continue under explicit maximum rejected count/rate and replay semantics.
nodes.definition: A deterministic data-quality containment contract, not unconditional skip-bad-row behavior.
nodes.nonExample: Continue forever while dropping most rows and reporting only a final success count.

nodes.title: CSV structural, typed, and domain validation
nodes.summary: Separate dialect/width/header, UTF-8/typed conversion, and semantic/cross-row domain rules with stable error classes.
nodes.definition: A staged boundary that prevents a syntactically parsed row from masquerading as accepted domain data.
nodes.nonExample: Counting successful record iteration as proof all required numeric ranges and uniqueness rules passed.

nodes.title: Bounded RecordBatch stream consumption
nodes.summary: Pull and process output batches/partitions incrementally under memory, cancellation, limit, and error contracts.
nodes.definition: Execution whose live result memory is bounded independently of total rows.
nodes.nonExample: Calling collect on an unbounded or unproven query and only then applying a limit.

nodes.title: EXPLAIN structure and analyzed metrics
nodes.summary: Use EXPLAIN for planned operators and EXPLAIN ANALYZE for executed operator metrics, normalizing version/config-dependent presentation.
nodes.definition: Observable structural/runtime evidence for a query plan, separate from the result oracle.
nodes.nonExample: Snapshot-testing the entire formatted plan string as the only correctness assertion.

nodes.title: DataFusion schema-aware logical plan DAG
nodes.summary: Represent relational operations and expressions independently of concrete files, partitions, and executable algorithms.
nodes.definition: A schema-aware DAG of relational intent derived from SQL/DataFrame input.
nodes.nonExample: Treating the logical Filter node as proof a Parquet reader skipped row groups.

nodes.title: Semantics-preserving plan rewrite
nodes.summary: An optimizer may change operators/expressions only while preserving output schema, names, values, multiplicity, null behavior, and required order.
nodes.definition: A transformation from one query plan to a potentially cheaper equivalent plan.
nodes.nonExample: Pushing a nullable predicate across an outer join without proving equivalence.

nodes.title: Partitions and exchange cost
nodes.summary: Parallel partitions run independently until repartition/coalesce/merge operators move or synchronize data; more partitions are not automatically faster.
nodes.definition: The execution topology and data movement required by distribution/order constraints.
nodes.nonExample: Counting RepartitionExec as free parallelism without rows/bytes/time or skew evidence.

nodes.title: DataFusion physical execution plan
nodes.summary: Select concrete scan, filter, aggregate, join, sort, repartition, and merge operators for the data and runtime configuration.
nodes.definition: The executable partitioned operator DAG produced from an optimized logical plan.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming identical physical plans across machines, file layouts, and target-partition settings.

nodes.title: DataFusion query and output contract
nodes.summary: Fix input schemas, SQL/null semantics, output fields/order, cardinality expectations, error policy, and resource limits before tuning.
nodes.definition: The observable meaning every valid logical/physical alternative must preserve.
nodes.nonExample: Changing an outer join to an inner join because the sample output happens to match.

nodes.title: Projection and filter pushdown evidence
nodes.summary: Locate requested columns/predicates at the data-source boundary and confirm reduced selected work rather than inferring from SQL text.
nodes.definition: Moving safe work toward a scan so irrelevant columns/regions/rows avoid later operators.
nodes.nonExample: Dropping columns after DataSourceExec decoded all of them and calling it projection pushdown.

nodes.title: Event time versus processing time
nodes.summary: Event time is declared by the event; processing time is local execution time and cannot substitute without changing semantics.
nodes.definition: Two distinct clocks for data meaning and system observation.
nodes.nonExample: Assigning replayed historical events to today's windows because they arrived now.

nodes.title: Record framing and EOF contract
nodes.summary: Define how a record ends, whether a final unterminated/blank record exists, and how partial/error bytes affect record numbering and recovery.
nodes.definition: The syntax boundary that turns a byte stream into independently attributable records.
nodes.nonExample: Calling repeated JSON values a stream without a separator/length or deserializer framing rule.

nodes.title: Optimistic metadata commit and validation
nodes.summary: Build files/metadata from a base version, validate operation assumptions against the refreshed current table, then atomically swap the catalog pointer or retry/reject.
nodes.definition: The concurrency boundary making a complete new snapshot visible without partial file publication.
nodes.nonExample: Overwriting the metadata pointer unconditionally after another writer committed.

nodes.title: Field-ID and partition-spec evolution
nodes.summary: Track logical fields by ID and every file/manifest by spec ID so schema renames/reorders and old/new physical layouts remain correctly readable.
nodes.definition: Metadata identity that separates logical columns/predicates from names, positions, and one fixed partition layout.
nodes.nonExample: Reading an old column as a newly added column merely because it occupies the same ordinal.

nodes.title: Measured data and metadata rewrite maintenance
nodes.summary: Compact small data files or regroup manifests only when observed planning/open/scan overhead justifies rewrite cost, then commit an equivalent table state.
nodes.definition: A semantics-preserving optimization lifecycle with before/after file, byte, manifest, plan, and scan evidence.
nodes.nonExample: Running daily full rewrites without file-size, query, cost, or conflict evidence.

nodes.title: Manifest tree and conservative pruning
nodes.summary: Snapshot manifest-list summaries and manifest file metrics prune impossible files, while residual row predicates preserve truth.
nodes.definition: The metadata index from a snapshot to immutable data/delete files with partition and column statistics.
nodes.nonExample: Dropping a file because a truncated upper bound appears outside a filter without applying its specified semantics.

nodes.title: Snapshot retention and safe reachability deletion
nodes.summary: Expire only policy-eligible snapshots and delete a file only after complete reference/in-progress checks show no retained snapshot can reach it.
nodes.definition: The time-travel/rollback/storage contract governing metadata and data garbage collection.
nodes.nonExample: Deleting all files older than one day while a retained snapshot still references them.

nodes.title: Catalog-selected snapshot truth
nodes.summary: One atomically selected table-metadata version names schemas/specs and a current snapshot; its manifest tree defines visible files.
nodes.definition: The committed root and immutable reference graph representing one table state.
nodes.nonExample: Unioning every Parquet file found below the table directory.

nodes.title: Safe ingest error provenance
nodes.summary: Classify open/read/decode/parse/schema/domain/limit errors with source and record location while redacting untrusted sensitive payloads.
nodes.definition: A stable diagnostic envelope that preserves actionable cause and location without leaking content.
nodes.nonExample: Logging the full rejected credentials/config record inside a generic parse error.

nodes.title: Ingestion resource envelope
nodes.summary: Set maximum total bytes, record bytes/count, nesting, and processing/rejection policy before allocating or waiting for EOF/delimiter.
nodes.definition: A memory/time/availability contract that selects whole-file versus incremental processing and prevents unbounded input growth.
nodes.nonExample: Calling read_line repeatedly on an attacker-controlled never-delimited stream without take/limit logic.

nodes.title: Aggregatable latency distribution
nodes.summary: Preserve count/sum and suitable histogram buckets or equivalent distribution so threshold ratios and cross-instance quantiles have explicit error bounds.
nodes.definition: Telemetry that retains tail shape instead of reducing observations to an average or unmergeable precomputed quantile.
nodes.nonExample: Averaging each worker's p99 to claim a global p99.

nodes.title: Allowed lateness, too-late routing, and cleanup
nodes.summary: Retain window state through end+lateness, admit/update within that horizon, then clean state and route later events with provenance.
nodes.definition: The bounded correction and state-lifetime contract after the main firing.
nodes.nonExample: Keeping every window forever so no late event is ever dropped.

nodes.title: Lifecycle-aware provenance claim
nodes.summary: Record producer/time/event type and run/job/input/output facets as claims; deduplicate and order them, retain failures/partials, and grade confidence when evidence is missing or conflicting.
nodes.definition: Evidence that an activity used/generated/derived an entity, distinct from assumed scheduler topology.
nodes.nonExample: Inferring that task B consumed A's exact output version only because B was downstream.

nodes.title: Dataset, job, run, and artifact version identity
nodes.summary: Use canonical namespace+name and stable run IDs, with version/snapshot/partition/schema/code facets sufficient to distinguish the exact entities used and generated.
nodes.definition: The collision-resistant identity layer for connecting provenance claims across producers.
nodes.nonExample: Merging prod.sales and test.sales because both are named sales.

nodes.title: LSM amplification and compaction debt
nodes.summary: Measure logical versus physical reads/writes/live space and slow input when pending flush/compaction exceeds bounded resources.
nodes.definition: The resource tradeoff and feedback loop behind LSM throughput, latency, and capacity.
nodes.nonExample: Accepting writes until disk exhaustion because background compaction will eventually catch up.

nodes.title: Flush installation and WAL retirement
nodes.summary: Write/verify a complete sorted run, install it in authoritative metadata, then retire only WAL coverage made redundant by installed state.
nodes.definition: The crash-safe handoff from replayable volatile state to immutable durable state.
nodes.nonExample: Deleting the WAL before the run is complete and discoverable after restart.

nodes.title: Mutable and immutable memtable lifecycle
nodes.summary: Apply WAL-backed writes to a bounded mutable sorted structure, seal it under pressure, and flush immutable state while a new table accepts writes.
nodes.definition: The memory-resident newest LSM component and its handoff to durable sorted runs.
nodes.nonExample: Allowing one memtable to grow without a flush or write-pressure policy.

nodes.title: Newest-visible read precedence
nodes.summary: Search newer memory/runs before older candidates or merge candidates by key/version, returning the newest visible value or tombstone.
nodes.definition: The reconciliation rule making overlapping immutable histories appear as one keyspace.
nodes.nonExample: Returning an old SST value after a newer memtable delete.

nodes.title: LSM sequence and visibility order
nodes.summary: Order versions monotonically and select the newest version not newer than the read/snapshot horizon.
nodes.definition: The total update order used to reconcile duplicates across storage components.
nodes.nonExample: Choosing the first file visited when two runs contain the same key.

nodes.title: Immutable sorted run contract
nodes.summary: Persist key/version ordered entries plus verified metadata as an immutable file installed atomically into the read set.
nodes.definition: A durable sorted LSM component produced by flush or compaction.
nodes.nonExample: Mutating an installed run in place while readers may observe it.

nodes.title: LSM tombstone semantics
nodes.summary: Represent deletion as an ordered version that hides older values until it is safe to elide during compaction.
nodes.definition: A delete marker participating in the same version order as values.
nodes.nonExample: Dropping a delete at flush and resurrecting an older lower-level value.

nodes.title: WAL-before-ack durability boundary
nodes.summary: Append a checksummed sequenced operation and satisfy the declared sync boundary before acknowledging it as recoverable.
nodes.definition: The persistence ordering that lets recovery reconstruct acknowledged volatile state.
nodes.nonExample: Returning success after only mutating a process-local map.

nodes.title: Metric quantity, unit, temporality, and bounded dimensions
nodes.summary: Choose counter/gauge/histogram semantics, one base unit, reset/aggregation behavior, and a finite reviewed label set whose product fits the series budget.
nodes.definition: The stable metric-stream identity and resource-cost contract.
