nodes.nonExample: Labeling request latency by user ID, trace ID, raw URL, and error message.

nodes.title: Backfill coverage, reprocessing, and concurrency policy
nodes.summary: Enumerate target intervals, existing/running outcomes, code/input version intent, missing/failed/completed policy, dependency order, max active work, and reconciliation.
nodes.definition: A bounded historical re-execution plan rather than an unqualified date loop.
nodes.nonExample: Launching every past interval concurrently while sharing one mutable output path.

nodes.title: Acyclic task and data dependency contract
nodes.summary: Define tasks, required artifacts/data, success/skip/failure conditions, and acyclic execution edges separately from mere grouping or control-only order.
nodes.definition: The static dependency plan from which eligible task instances are derived.
nodes.nonExample: A cycle where A waits for B's artifact and B waits for A's success.

nodes.title: Retry-idempotent atomic artifact publication
nodes.summary: Read pinned interval inputs, write attempt-local output, validate it, then atomically publish one stable artifact/version key so retries cannot expose partial or duplicate results.
nodes.definition: The task effect contract across crash, retry, duplicate scheduling, and overlapping attempts.
nodes.nonExample: Appending directly to a shared daily file before task success.

nodes.title: Versioned run and half-open data interval
nodes.summary: Identify workflow/job/task/run/attempt plus [start,end), code/config/input versions and separate logical coverage from trigger and wall-clock execution.
nodes.definition: The reproducibility key for one intended processing interval and implementation state.
nodes.nonExample: Calling now() in a historical run to choose input rows.

nodes.title: Arrow–Parquet schema compatibility
nodes.summary: Map Arrow fields to supported Parquet physical/logical types with explicit nullability and reject unsupported or semantically lossy conversion.
nodes.definition: The checked representation boundary between in-memory arrays and durable columns.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming every Arrow extension or interval type round-trips unchanged.

nodes.title: Bounded Parquet-to-Arrow reading
nodes.summary: Apply projection/selection before build and stream finite output RecordBatches under explicit batch/limit/error contracts.
nodes.definition: A controlled scan that separates selected storage regions from output batch sizing.
nodes.nonExample: Collecting every selected row group into one in-memory batch before processing.

nodes.title: Parquet file hierarchy and footer
nodes.summary: A finalized file maps row groups to per-column chunks/pages and ends with metadata offsets, metadata length, and trailing magic.
nodes.definition: The durable navigation structure readers inspect before selecting data regions.
nodes.nonExample: Considering a file valid because it starts with PAR1 while its footer is missing.

nodes.title: Parquet page encoding and compression
nodes.summary: Pages store levels and encoded values; page metadata declares encoding and optional compression for their column chunk.
nodes.definition: Physical byte-reduction/representation choices within a leaf column chunk.
nodes.nonExample: Claiming dictionary encoding alone prevents irrelevant row groups from being read.

nodes.title: Parquet column projection
nodes.summary: Select only required schema leaves before decoding and preserve deterministic output identity/order.
nodes.definition: Avoiding I/O and decode work for unrequested column chunks independently of row filtering.
nodes.nonExample: Reading every column into Arrow and dropping unused arrays afterward.

nodes.title: Parquet row-group boundary
nodes.summary: A row group is a horizontal record partition containing one column chunk per leaf column and a unit for statistics and skipping.
nodes.definition: The shared row interval across column chunks in a Parquet file.
nodes.nonExample: Writing each input row as its own row group without measuring metadata or compression cost.

nodes.title: Conservative Parquet statistics pruning
nodes.summary: Use available trusted min/max/null and optional indexes only to eliminate regions that cannot match, then evaluate survivors.
nodes.definition: A metadata-based negative proof for row-group/page reads, not a row-level correctness oracle.
nodes.nonExample: Returning all rows from a min/max-overlapping page without applying the predicate.

nodes.title: Parquet writer finalization and publication
nodes.summary: Bound in-progress row-group memory, finish the footer, reopen/verify the artifact, and publish only the finalized output.
nodes.definition: The transition from buffered encoding to a readable committed file.
nodes.nonExample: Renaming a partially written temporary file after write(batch) without close or verification.

nodes.title: Partition key, locality, and skew contract
nodes.summary: Select a key from required query locality while bounding partition item/byte/rate growth and exposing hot-key or correlated skew.
nodes.definition: The workload-facing contract that maps records and access paths to a bounded unit of placement and failure.
nodes.nonExample: Hashing tenant ID despite one tenant carrying most bytes and requests, then claiming the ring is balanced.

nodes.title: Deterministic ownership and movement
nodes.summary: Map the full key/token space to one primary owner and an ordered replica set, with deterministic add/remove movement and no gaps or duplicate physical replicas.
nodes.definition: A reproducible routing plan whose coverage and topology-change movement can be independently checked.
nodes.nonExample: Using process-random hash iteration to choose owners differently on each node.

nodes.title: Purpose-bound minimized data lifecycle
nodes.summary: For every data element/copy record subject/category, purpose, source, flows, stores, recipients, quality, access, retention, deletion/backup behavior, audit and owner; collect/keep only what is necessary.
nodes.definition: The privacy-risk and manageability contract from collection through derived copies and policy-driven destruction.
nodes.nonExample: Keeping full raw requests forever because storage is cheap and they might help later.

nodes.title: Protocol deadline and cancellation state
nodes.summary: Apply connect/read/frame/write/response deadlines and specify whether cancellation leaves no progress, buffered input, partial output, or a connection that must close.
nodes.definition: A time bound plus a safe state transition, not merely a timer error.
nodes.nonExample: Restarting write_all after timeout without knowing how many bytes reached the stream.

nodes.title: Versioned request/response envelope
nodes.summary: Validate version/type/request identity and define unknown-field/type and error-response behavior before dispatch.
nodes.definition: The stable application metadata separating framing from command semantics and correlation.
nodes.nonExample: Dispatching an unknown opcode as the closest known command.

nodes.title: Bounded application frame contract
nodes.summary: Define header/version/type/flags/request ID/length/body encoding, maximum sizes, and clean/truncated EOF behavior independently of reads.
nodes.definition: A self-delimiting application data unit reconstructed from stream bytes or carried by one datagram.
nodes.nonExample: Allocating the peer-declared length before checking it against a maximum.

nodes.title: Incremental bounded frame decoder
nodes.summary: Retain partial header/body bytes, emit zero or more complete frames, and preserve unused suffix bytes under a fixed buffer/connection limit.
nodes.definition: A state machine invariant to arbitrary transport chunking.
nodes.nonExample: Calling read once per frame and parsing whatever count arrived.

nodes.title: Partial read/write progress
nodes.summary: Loop or maintain explicit offsets until required bytes are transferred, propagating errors and never duplicating a partially sent frame.
nodes.definition: Byte-oriented I/O progress whose operation boundary need not match the supplied buffer.
nodes.nonExample: Discarding a short-write count and resending the entire frame on the same connection.

nodes.title: Transport semantics versus application messages
nodes.summary: TCP supplies ordered bytes without boundaries/liveness; UDP supplies bounded datagrams without delivery/order/retry guarantees required by many applications.
nodes.definition: The guarantees and omissions the application protocol must accept or supply.
nodes.nonExample: Using TCP packet boundaries or UDP send success as an application acknowledgment.

nodes.title: UDP loss, duplicate, size, and congestion discipline
nodes.summary: Bound datagrams/rates/retries, correlate responses, make repeated operations safe or detect duplicates, and tolerate loss/reorder without assuming the path.
nodes.definition: Application responsibilities added when choosing unreliable datagram transport.
nodes.nonExample: Retrying a non-idempotent UDP mutation forever at a fixed high rate.

nodes.title: Quorum overlap and response contract
nodes.summary: Relate N, R, W, available responders, acknowledged versions, read reconciliation, concurrency, and timeouts before naming an observed guarantee.
nodes.definition: The responder-set and version-selection contract behind tunable read/write availability and freshness.
nodes.nonExample: Writing to any two of three and reading any two, then returning the first response without version comparison while claiming latest-value reads.

nodes.title: Client deduplication and majority liveness bound
nodes.summary: Use stable client/request sequence IDs and cached results across retry, while distinguishing unconditional non-Byzantine safety from progress requiring a reachable majority and eventual timing stability.
nodes.definition: The client-effect and availability contract surrounding the replicated log.
nodes.nonExample: Claiming exactly-once effects and continued writes after isolating the leader from every majority.

nodes.title: Raft commit and ordered apply rule
nodes.summary: Advance commit by majority counting only for current-term entries, indirectly commit their prefix, and apply committed entries once in increasing index order.
nodes.definition: The rule connecting replication evidence to irreversible deterministic state-machine effects.
nodes.nonExample: Applying an uncommitted prior-term entry because it happens to exist on two of three nodes.

nodes.title: Raft log matching and suffix repair
nodes.summary: Accept AppendEntries only when the previous index/term matches, then delete a conflicting suffix and append leader entries so equal index/term implies an equal prefix.
nodes.definition: The consistency check and repair rule for divergent uncommitted logs.
nodes.nonExample: Appending after a missing or different previous entry and retaining two meanings for one index.

nodes.title: Raft term, vote, and election safety
nodes.summary: Persist monotonically increasing term and one vote per term, reject stale authority, and grant votes only to candidates whose last log is at least as up-to-date.
nodes.definition: The logical-clock and majority-vote rules yielding at most one elected leader per term and preserving committed history.
nodes.nonExample: Voting again after restart because votedFor was kept only in memory.

nodes.title: Recovery point and catch-up capacity
nodes.summary: Bound checkpoint age/restore time/replay volume and provision enough post-restart service rate to catch up while new input continues.
nodes.definition: The RPO/RTO and capacity contract determining whether recovery converges.
nodes.nonExample: Restoring successfully into a pipeline whose service rate remains below current arrival rate.

nodes.title: Replay and processing-effect guarantees
nodes.summary: Define at-most/at-least/exactly-once managed-state effects and distinguish them from physical executions and external side effects.
nodes.definition: The loss/duplication contract across crash restoration and replay.
nodes.nonExample: Claiming exactly-once because a checkpoint flag is enabled while an HTTP sink double-charges.

nodes.title: Replication and failure-domain placement
nodes.summary: Define N distinct replicas across the intended host/rack/zone domains and state which correlated failures and responder counts remain tolerable.
nodes.definition: The physical placement contract behind a logical replication factor.
nodes.nonExample: Three copies on one machine presented as tolerance of a machine failure.

nodes.title: Hints, anti-entropy, and repair debt
nodes.summary: Track divergent ranges/versions and retained hints, then perform measurable read/full/incremental repair before deletion/version retention makes recovery unsafe.
nodes.definition: The convergence lifecycle after replicas miss, reorder, or independently accept updates.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming an expired or lost hint will somehow update a replica without comparison and repair.

nodes.title: Versioned concurrency and conflict policy
nodes.summary: Distinguish causally ordered from concurrent versions and specify retain, reject, last-write-wins, or deterministic domain-merge behavior with its loss assumptions.
nodes.definition: The evidence and policy used when replicas observe writes in different orders or at different times.
nodes.nonExample: Picking the largest wall-clock timestamp and calling it causally correct despite clock skew and concurrent writes.

nodes.title: Missing and unknown field policy
nodes.summary: Version required/default/deprecated fields and deliberately reject, capture, or ignore unknown fields for the producer/consumer compatibility contract.
nodes.definition: An explicit evolution rule encoded and tested rather than inherited accidentally from derive defaults.
nodes.nonExample: Adding serde(default) to every field to make all malformed old/new documents pass.

nodes.title: Deny-default per-request authorization
nodes.summary: Evaluate current subject, tenant/object, action, attributes and policy on every server-side path; grant only explicit least privilege and audit allow/deny without sensitive payloads.
nodes.definition: The reference-monitor decision after identity and canonical resource resolution.
nodes.nonExample: Allowing any authenticated user to fetch /documents/{id} because the UI only links their own IDs.

nodes.title: Threat-scoped authenticated encryption and key lifecycle
nodes.summary: Minimize first, then use reviewed standard authenticated encryption/strong transport at the layer matching the threat; generate/store/separate/version/rotate/revoke/destroy keys under least privilege and recovery tests.
nodes.definition: Confidentiality/integrity protection whose algorithm, nonce/key management and attacker limits are explicit.
nodes.nonExample: Base64-encoding records with a key hard-coded next to the ciphertext and calling them encrypted.

nodes.title: Authentication, session, and sensitive-action evidence
nodes.summary: Verify a claimed service-scoped identity through approved authenticators, protect/rotate/expire unpredictable session evidence over strong transport, and reauthenticate high-risk actions.
nodes.definition: The time-bounded evidence of who/what is making a request, distinct from what it may do.
nodes.nonExample: Treating a user ID request parameter as authenticated identity or accepting an old session after credential recovery.

nodes.title: Untrusted-input to sensitive-sink boundary
nodes.summary: Canonicalize once, enforce server-side type/schema/length/range/allowlist and business semantics, and use structured parameterization or context-safe encoding at the sink.
nodes.definition: The fail-closed transformation from adversary-controlled bytes to a validated domain value that never becomes command syntax accidentally.
nodes.nonExample: Blocking apostrophes while concatenating the remaining text into SQL or a shell command.

nodes.title: Secret lifecycle and redacted security audit
nodes.summary: Give each secret owner/purpose/consumer/scope/version/expiry, provision with least privilege, rotate/revoke/test recovery, and audit use/denial/admin events while excluding secret and sensitive contents.
nodes.definition: Operational evidence for credentials/keys without turning logs, code, config, or telemetry into another secret store.
nodes.nonExample: Printing an API token on authentication failure so debugging can reproduce the request.

nodes.title: Asset, flow, trust-boundary, and threat contract
nodes.summary: Inventory actors/assets/data/stores/processes/flows/boundaries, enumerate abuse/failure cases, rank likelihood/impact, select prevent/detect/respond controls, and record residual risk plus review trigger.
nodes.definition: A maintained adversarial model tying each control and test to a concrete asset/path/threat.
nodes.nonExample: Listing generic OWASP categories without a system flow, attacker capability, control owner, or validation.

nodes.title: Serde representation model
nodes.summary: Map Rust wire types to the format through explicit scalar/string/bytes/sequence/map/struct/enum semantics.
nodes.definition: The typed mediation boundary between a data format and Rust values, not a domain-schema validator by itself.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming OsString or arbitrary bytes serialize portably as a normal UTF-8 string.

nodes.title: Stable idempotent or transactional sink effect
nodes.summary: Use deterministic effect IDs/upsert keys or coordinated commit so replay produces one logical external result.
nodes.definition: The external collaboration needed to extend recovery guarantees beyond managed state.
nodes.nonExample: Appending an unkeyed notification again after every replay.

nodes.title: User journey and good-event SLI contract
nodes.summary: Name the user-visible operation, service boundary, valid-event population, good criterion, exclusions, observation point, and data-completeness policy.
nodes.definition: A reproducible numerator/denominator or distribution measuring a behavior users care about.
nodes.nonExample: Using host CPU below 80 percent as the availability SLI for completed searches.

nodes.title: SLO window, error budget, and burn contract
nodes.summary: Set target and calendar/rolling window, compute allowed bad events/time, consumed/remaining budget and burn rate, and attach an explicit decision policy.
nodes.definition: The arithmetic and operational agreement around acceptable service misses.
nodes.nonExample: Reporting 99.9 percent without the event population, window, exclusions, or consequence.

nodes.title: Deterministic event-time replay
nodes.summary: Given the same event multiset, timestamps, keys, watermark/idleness trace, and policy, produce the same ordered change log independent of wall clock.
nodes.definition: A reproducible oracle for out-of-order streaming semantics.
nodes.nonExample: Using SystemTime::now inside event-time aggregation results.

nodes.title: Resource and execution-context correlation
nodes.summary: Propagate and validate resource, trace, span, request, and job/run identifiers so signals can be joined to the same operation without putting unique IDs in metric dimensions.
nodes.definition: The identity bridge between aggregate symptoms and sampled per-operation evidence.
nodes.nonExample: Joining two log lines solely because their timestamps are within one second.

nodes.title: Sampled, redacted, retained telemetry evidence
nodes.summary: Collect only fields needed for stated diagnostic questions, redact/drop secrets and sensitive identifiers, define sampling bias/coverage, access and retention, and preserve missing/conflicting evidence.
nodes.definition: The utility, privacy, cost, and uncertainty contract for logs, traces, exemplars, and events.
nodes.nonExample: Recording authorization headers and full payloads in every span for possible future debugging.

nodes.title: Isolation anomaly taxonomy
nodes.summary: Distinguish dirty write/read, nonrepeatable read, phantom, lost update, read skew, write skew, and the broader absence of any equivalent serial order.
nodes.definition: Named counterexample shapes over full histories, not a universal total ordering of vendor level names.
nodes.nonExample: Declaring no anomaly because no single row was read twice while a cross-row invariant is violated.

nodes.title: Transaction and external-effect boundary
nodes.summary: Bundle database reads/writes into one commit/rollback unit and keep nontransactional effects deferred, idempotently keyed, or explicitly compensated.
nodes.definition: The exact resources and observations covered by atomic commit and durable acknowledgement.
nodes.nonExample: Sending an email inside a transaction and assuming database rollback unsends it.

nodes.title: Transaction history and dependency graph
nodes.summary: Record each transaction's reads-from versions, predicate reads, writes, commit/abort, and real-time constraints, then compare dependencies with possible serial orders.
nodes.definition: A complete observable execution used to diagnose isolation rather than relying on a level label.
nodes.nonExample: Listing final row values without the versions each transaction read or whether it committed.

nodes.title: Whole-transaction retry and effect identity
nodes.summary: After serialization/deadlock abort, discard the aborted view and rerun all reads/decisions under a bounded policy while preserving stable external operation identity.
nodes.definition: The application control loop required when concurrency control rejects an execution.
nodes.nonExample: Retrying only UPDATE with a decision computed from a stale aborted snapshot.

nodes.title: Monotonic event-time watermark
nodes.summary: Advance an explicit source progress estimate without regression; timestamps behind it are late by definition, not necessarily invalid.
nodes.definition: A lower-bound/progress signal used to trigger event-time work under a stated source assumption.
nodes.nonExample: Setting watermark to each observed timestamp and allowing it to move backward.

nodes.title: Minimum active watermark and idleness
nodes.summary: Combine inputs by their minimum watermark and exclude a source only after an explicit idle rule, restoring it without watermark regression.
nodes.definition: The multi-source progress rule preventing faster partitions from closing slower partitions' windows.
nodes.nonExample: Using the maximum watermark and dropping valid events from a lagging active partition.

nodes.title: Keyed half-open window assignment
nodes.summary: Map each valid timestamp/key deterministically into explicit [start,end) tumbling/sliding/session windows using checked units/offsets.
nodes.definition: The pure function from event identity/time to one or more state namespaces.
nodes.nonExample: Counting an event exactly at 12:05 in both [12:00,12:05] and [12:05,12:10].

nodes.title: Trigger, firing, and result-update semantics
nodes.summary: Define when windows emit and whether each emission is final append, keyed replacement, or explicit retraction/update.
nodes.definition: The contract connecting mutable window state to downstream-visible revisions.
nodes.nonExample: Emitting two totals for one key/window to an append-only sink without revision identity.

nodes.title: Bounded keyed window state
nodes.summary: Account for active keys×windows×aggregate/revision metadata and enforce timestamp/key/cardinality/lateness limits plus cleanup.
nodes.definition: The finite resource contract for an otherwise unbounded stream.
nodes.nonExample: Accepting arbitrary future timestamps that create millions of never-closing windows.

nodes.title: Wire DTO to validated domain conversion
nodes.summary: Keep compatibility-shaped optional/raw fields at the boundary and construct invariant-bearing domain values through TryFrom/validation.
nodes.definition: A two-stage parse then semantic-validation boundary with distinct syntax/schema/domain errors.
nodes.nonExample: Letting an optional raw string circulate internally where the domain requires a nonempty normalized identifier.

nodes.title: Readiness-gated attempt and consolidation
nodes.summary: When prerequisites exist, elicit one bounded plan/solution attempt before instruction, preserve generated representations/errors, then compare and consolidate; route blocked learners directly to guidance.
nodes.definition: An attempt-first sequence whose purpose is preparation and diagnosis, not endurance or discovery without teaching.
nodes.nonExample: Hiding all instruction for twenty minutes regardless of missing prerequisites or frustration.

nodes.title: Append-only attempt-event envelope
nodes.summary: Require stable event/attempt IDs, monotone sequence, type, occurred/recorded UTC times, schema/content/item versions, support mode, idempotency key and validated payload; never update/delete raw rows.
nodes.definition: The minimal transactional fact log needed to reproduce learner evidence and projections.
nodes.nonExample: Overwriting the attempt's final status and discarding the hint/test sequence that produced it.

nodes.title: Attempt before help
nodes.summary: Commit a prediction, plan, explanation, or code attempt before support is revealed.
nodes.definition: An observable commitment that makes retrieval and reasoning inspectable before feedback.
nodes.nonExample: Opening the full solution before describing the problem.

nodes.title: Initial blocked or faded acquisition
nodes.summary: Establish the target strategy's invariant, execution and feedback with coherent examples/practice before requiring discrimination among siblings.
nodes.definition: A bounded acquisition phase centered on one outcome, not permanent same-type repetition.
nodes.nonExample: Mixing binary search, DFS and joins before the learner can execute any one of them.

nodes.title: Descriptive confidence–accuracy calibration
nodes.summary: For comparable scored responses, show raw count/correct by confidence band, observed accuracy, gap, immediate/delayed horizon and support mix; say insufficient data rather than invent precision.
nodes.definition: A transparent comparison between expressed probability bands and observed binary rubric outcomes over a stated sample.
nodes.nonExample: Converting one 90%-confident error into a permanent overconfident learner label.

nodes.title: Compiler feedback loop
nodes.summary: Read diagnostics as structured evidence, form a hypothesis, and run the smallest discriminating change.
nodes.definition: A debugging loop grounded in compiler observations rather than random edits.
nodes.nonExample: Applying every compiler suggestion without explaining the cause.

nodes.title: Completion-step and feedback evidence
nodes.summary: Choose omitted steps by dependency and diagnostic value, require the learner's prediction/explanation/implementation, and evaluate against an independent state/behavior oracle before revealing.
nodes.definition: Evidence that a learner supplied a missing consequential step rather than copied surrounding syntax.
nodes.nonExample: A blank whose answer is visible unchanged two lines above.

nodes.title: Pre-feedback item-bound confidence judgment
nodes.summary: Record a 0–100 confidence value before correctness feedback, bound to committed response, item/outcome/version, target horizon and timestamp; never edit it afterward.
nodes.definition: A learner's contemporaneous judgment about the correctness or future retrievability of one answer, not evidence of competence.
nodes.nonExample: Asking confidence after revealing the test result or storing a general 'I know Rust' rating.

nodes.title: Reviewed confusable sibling and contrast contract
nodes.summary: Name a small sibling set, shared surface cues, distinguishing structural cues, non-examples, source/reviewer/confidence and learner-error evidence.
nodes.definition: An auditable claim that strategies are plausible alternatives whose discrimination is instructionally useful.
nodes.nonExample: Marking two unrelated roadmap topics confusable merely to increase variety.

nodes.title: Immediate performance versus delayed evidence
nodes.summary: Classify evidence by actual lag, freshness, support and outcome alignment so fluent restudy or immediate success cannot masquerade as retention.
nodes.definition: Evidence from a fresh probe after a declared delay, interpreted separately from acquisition performance.
nodes.nonExample: Marking an outcome retained because the learner copied a just-seen example correctly.

nodes.title: Compiler, test, and official-document evidence packet
nodes.summary: Capture command/toolchain, structured diagnostic/test result, exact span/failure, learner hypothesis, official source/query, chosen change and verification outcome.
nodes.definition: A reproducible self-help trail grounded in the program and primary documentation rather than answer lookup.
nodes.nonExample: Accepting the first compiler suggestion without reading the span or running the relevant tests.

nodes.title: Reviewable cause, correction, and future cue
nodes.summary: Classify error, distinguish learner hypothesis from reviewed finding, record the minimal correction, independent verification, a short cue for future recognition, and linked remediation.
nodes.definition: An actionable explanation/correction record whose status can be tested and superseded.
nodes.nonExample: Copying the correct answer and writing 'read more carefully next time.'

nodes.title: Error symptom, artifact, and evidence contract
nodes.summary: Bind stable error ID to attempt/outcome/item/version, response/artifact checksum, evaluator evidence, observed-versus-expected symptom, support and timestamps.
nodes.definition: The reproducible facts that an error interpretation must explain.
nodes.nonExample: 'I am bad at lifetimes' with no code, diagnostic, expected behavior or item version.

nodes.title: Append-only error recurrence and supersession lifecycle
nodes.summary: Track open, corrected, needs-confirmation and resolved states; link same-cause recurrence, changed-cause supersession and fresh proof without mutating old artifacts.
nodes.definition: A rebuildable history of how an error hypothesis responds to correction and later evidence.
nodes.nonExample: Deleting a compiler error entry after one passing rerun or adding a permanent penalty for every recurrence.

nodes.title: Curriculum, immutable event, and derived-state separation
nodes.summary: Keep teachable definitions/rubrics, what happened, and current learner interpretation in separate versioned layers joined by stable IDs.
nodes.definition: An ownership boundary preventing learner state from silently changing curriculum truth or raw history.
nodes.nonExample: Writing `mastered: true` into a concept Markdown file after visiting its page.

nodes.title: Rubric-scoped evidence observation
nodes.summary: Interpret exact event/artifact IDs for one outcome using rubric/evaluator/content versions, score/criteria, freshness/delay/variant, support and reviewer status; preserve supersession.
nodes.definition: A versioned claim about what an immutable attempt demonstrates, distinct from the attempt facts and mastery snapshot.
nodes.nonExample: Counting `completed` as proof without a rubric, artifact, score or support history.

nodes.title: Outcome-aligned worked-example anatomy
nodes.summary: State the goal, prerequisites, inputs/constraints, intermediate state, each solution step and rationale, observable result, verification, likely errors, and analogy limits.
nodes.definition: A complete but concise expert solution whose decisions and state transitions are inspectable rather than merely copyable.
nodes.nonExample: A code listing with no stated invariant, ownership/data-flow explanation, or verification.

nodes.title: Declared external/AI help and independence boundary
nodes.summary: Record learner-declared source/type/depth, tutor hint/reveal events and affected artifact; classify assisted practice without moral labels and require a fresh no-tutor variant for durable independence.
nodes.definition: Honest support provenance used to interpret evidence, not to surveil or punish tool use.
nodes.nonExample: Inferring ChatGPT use from typing cadence and marking the learner a cheater.

nodes.title: Explicit responsibility-fading stages
nodes.summary: Version the sequence full example → completion → isomorphic independent problem → mixed selection → transfer, including entry/exit evidence and revealed/omitted steps.
nodes.definition: A controlled handoff of consequential decisions from worked solution to learner.
nodes.nonExample: Randomly deleting tokens until the learner writes most of the file.

nodes.title: Freshness and support provenance
nodes.summary: Version item/variant, record hints/resources/reveals/external help, and require a materially fresh probe for evidence intended to establish durable independence.
nodes.definition: The evidence needed to distinguish recall from recognition, repetition, copied structure, or assisted completion.
nodes.nonExample: Calling the same unchanged prompt fresh because it appeared on another day.

nodes.title: Intervening learner-action evidence
nodes.summary: For levels 2–6, require and persist a new observation, official-doc search/query, prediction, plan, code/query edit, compiler/test run, or consequential explanation tied to the current blocker.
nodes.definition: Observable engagement with the current evidence before more information is revealed.
nodes.nonExample: Pressing Next Hint repeatedly with no changed artifact or observation.

nodes.title: Accessibility and frustration bypass
nodes.summary: Permit immediate requested escalation or reveal, record the actual support neutrally, avoid traps/timers, and schedule a fresh variant rather than denying access.
nodes.definition: A safe escape from the normal ladder that preserves autonomy and honest evidence provenance.
nodes.nonExample: Forcing a dyslexic or frustrated learner to type an explanation before seeing a needed scaffold.

nodes.title: Versioned help-level and reveal contract
nodes.summary: Define levels 0 independent, 1 restate, 2 docs-search cue, 3 concept hint, 4 stronger hint, 5 pseudocode/partial scaffold, 6 near-complete scaffold, and 7 explicit full reveal with stable IDs and solution flag.
nodes.definition: An inspectable escalation policy that distinguishes information amount and evidence consequences.
nodes.nonExample: A single Hint button that may silently reveal the complete implementation.

nodes.title: Isomorphic, mixed, and transfer distinction
nodes.summary: Define what structural relation is preserved, which surface/context features change, which sibling strategies are confusable, and what counts as near versus far transfer.
nodes.definition: A freshness contract that progressively tests execution, selection and application beyond example memory.
nodes.nonExample: Renaming variables in the identical prompt and calling it far transfer.

nodes.title: Transparent reversible mastery-state contract
nodes.summary: Derive not_started, exposed, practicing, provisional, retained or needs_confirmation from qualifying observations, unresolved critical misconceptions and exact model/evidence versions.
nodes.definition: A reproducible categorical summary whose rules and evidence can be inspected and changed by rebuilding.
nodes.nonExample: An opaque 0.83 mastery probability with no supporting attempts or transition rule.

nodes.title: Committed mixed strategy-selection evidence
nodes.summary: Before feedback, record candidate set, chosen strategy, cues/rationale and plan; score both selection and execution with item/support/version provenance.
nodes.definition: Evidence that the learner discriminated among plausible strategies rather than merely executed a named one.
nodes.nonExample: A problem titled Sliding Window that asks only for its implementation.

nodes.title: Outcome-specific prior-evidence gate
nodes.summary: Use a fresh diagnostic artifact with score, errors, support and version to enter full-example, completion, independent, mixed, or transfer stages; reopen support after failure.
nodes.definition: A deterministic guidance-placement decision grounded in demonstrated outcome performance.
nodes.nonExample: Skipping ownership examples because the learner is an experienced data engineer.

nodes.title: Fresh retrieval
nodes.summary: Reconstruct knowledge or a solution after delay in a context that does not expose the prior answer.
nodes.definition: A memory-based attempt that can provide delayed evidence beyond immediate performance.
nodes.nonExample: Rereading a completed solution and marking it retained.

nodes.title: Committed retrieval before feedback
nodes.summary: Capture a prediction, plan, explanation, query, answer, or code attempt before corrective feedback or solution reveal, with immutable timing and item version.
nodes.definition: An observable attempt to produce target knowledge or strategy from memory before seeing the answer.
nodes.nonExample: Reading a solution and then typing its conclusion as the first recorded response.

nodes.title: Review due-state and recommendation reason
nodes.summary: Store policy/model version, interval index, qualifying last evidence, due time, reason, candidate item constraints and outcome state separately from mastery; missed/early/late and failure remain explicit.
nodes.definition: A rebuildable scheduling projection that chooses the next evidence opportunity without awarding competence.
nodes.nonExample: Promoting provisional to retained automatically when 21 calendar days pass.

nodes.title: Actual review timing and due-state evidence
nodes.summary: Store scheduled, presented, committed, feedback and completion times; classify early/on-time/late/missed without deleting history or fabricating a success.
nodes.definition: An auditable event timeline from which review eligibility and actual lag can be rebuilt.
nodes.nonExample: Overwriting the due date when a review is missed so it appears on time.

nodes.title: Transparent distributed-review policy
nodes.summary: Start with visible interval indices at 1, 3, 7 and 21 days, record the policy version and reason, and treat the sequence as a revisable baseline rather than an optimum.
nodes.definition: A deterministic rule that distributes retrieval opportunities across time and exposes every due-date calculation.
nodes.nonExample: Claiming a proprietary score has discovered the learner's exact forgetting curve.

nodes.title: Explicit transfer transformation matrix
nodes.summary: Record preserved invariant and changes to surface, representation, constraints, scale, domain, interface, failure mode, evaluator and support; review the isomorphic/near/far label.
nodes.definition: The evidence for how a fresh item differs from acquisition while targeting the same outcome.
nodes.nonExample: Calling a variable rename far transfer without any structural or contextual change.

nodes.title: Evidence-based advanced feature activation
nodes.summary: Require a concrete unmet constraint, rejected safe alternatives, bounded scope, and new verification plan before advanced Rust enters a project.
nodes.definition: A review gate that compares the smallest safe/native solution with the proposed advanced mechanism and approves it only when the benefit and invariant burden are observable.
nodes.nonExample: Adding unsafe or a procedural macro because it looks more advanced.

nodes.title: Arrow arrays and RecordBatch
nodes.summary: Represent equal-length typed column arrays under one schema in immutable row chunks.
nodes.definition: A schema-conforming collection of equal-length Arrow arrays forming a bounded horizontal table slice.
nodes.nonExample: A mutable vector of unrelated columns with different row counts.

nodes.title: Async backpressure
nodes.summary: Make producers wait, shed, or fail explicitly when bounded downstream capacity is exhausted.
nodes.definition: A protocol that propagates finite consumer/resource capacity to upstream admission instead of accumulating unbounded work.
nodes.nonExample: An unbounded queue that postpones overload until memory exhaustion.

nodes.title: Bounded async concurrency
nodes.summary: Limit admitted tasks or in-flight operations to a capacity justified by resources and service behavior.
nodes.definition: An explicit upper bound enforced by permits, queues, or structured admission rather than relying on workload luck.
nodes.nonExample: Spawning one task per untrusted input with no cap.

nodes.title: Async cancellation
nodes.summary: Stop future progress through dropping, aborting, or cooperative notification while accounting for owned resources and side effects.
nodes.definition: A lifecycle transition that prevents or requests further task progress and defines cleanup, observation, and externally visible partial work.
nodes.nonExample: Dropping a timeout wrapper and assuming every spawned child or external operation rolled back.

nodes.title: Selecting concurrent operations
nodes.summary: Wait on multiple futures within one task and define what happens to every non-selected branch.
nodes.definition: Single-task multiplexing that completes one ready branch and drops or resumes other branch futures according to explicit control flow.
nodes.nonExample: A guarantee that all branches run simultaneously or finish.

nodes.title: Async suitability
nodes.summary: Choose async for many independently waiting operations, not as a default speed or parallelism switch.
nodes.definition: A workload decision based on concurrent waiting, resource occupancy, latency, and integration constraints that justify cooperative asynchronous execution.
nodes.nonExample: Converting a CPU-bound loop to async solely to make it faster.

nodes.title: Async task lifecycle
nodes.summary: Track spawn, scheduling, completion, panic, cancellation, and handle ownership for every task.
nodes.definition: The state and ownership path from task creation through a terminal result that is observed or deliberately handled.
nodes.nonExample: Dropping every JoinHandle and assuming all background work is supervised.

nodes.title: Bindings and mutability
nodes.summary: Names bind values, with mutation requiring an explicit mutable binding and type-compatible assignments.
nodes.definition: A local name introduced by a pattern and associated with a typed value under Rust's mutability rules.
nodes.nonExample: A dynamically typed container whose operation set changes after assignment.

nodes.title: Blocking boundary
nodes.summary: Keep blocking or CPU-heavy work from occupying async executor threads needed to poll unrelated tasks.
nodes.definition: An explicit bridge that isolates synchronous/blocking work or exposes async work through a controlled runtime interface.
nodes.nonExample: Calling a long blocking function directly between await points on a runtime worker.

nodes.title: Bounded batch flow
nodes.summary: Limit row batches and in-flight query output so memory use and downstream waiting remain observable.
nodes.definition: A finite chunk and admission protocol connecting row ingest, columnar conversion, persistence, and query consumption.
nodes.nonExample: Collecting every RecordBatch into memory before consuming the first result.

nodes.title: Unique heap ownership with Box
nodes.summary: Box uniquely owns a heap allocation and gives recursive values a finite known representation size.
nodes.editionScope: Rust 2024 standard Box ownership and recursive representation
nodes.definition: An owning smart pointer for one heap allocation whose owner moves and drops with the Box.
nodes.nonExample: Using Box to create shared mutable ownership.

nodes.title: Cancellation safety
nodes.summary: Know whether an operation may be dropped at an await point and retried without losing data or violating protocol state.
nodes.definition: The documented invariant preserved when a pending future is dropped before producing its output.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming every async method is safe to abandon in select.

nodes.title: Channel closure protocol
nodes.summary: Use endpoint drop and send/receive errors as explicit completion or abandonment signals.
nodes.definition: The protocol state reached when senders or receiver are gone, causing later operations or receiver iteration to terminate with documented results.
nodes.nonExample: Keeping an unused sender alive while waiting for receiver iteration to finish.

nodes.title: Supported CI matrix
nodes.summary: Continuously verify only the promised toolchain, target, feature, and operating-system combinations plus deliberate forward checks.
nodes.definition: A finite executable support contract mapping each promised environment/configuration to required gates.
nodes.nonExample: A huge speculative matrix whose failures do not correspond to a support promise.

nodes.title: Closure capture
nodes.summary: Infer shared, mutable, or owned environment capture from how the closure body uses values and where the closure must live.
nodes.definition: The compiler-selected access mode for values a closure references from its defining environment, optionally forced toward ownership with move.
nodes.nonExample: An unconditional deep copy of every variable visible where the closure is written.

nodes.title: Fallible versus panicking collection access
nodes.summary: Choose optional access for expected absence and indexing only when an invalid index is an invariant violation.
nodes.definition: An explicit behavior choice between returning an absence value and panicking on invalid positional access.
nodes.nonExample: Treating get as always safer regardless of whether absence is possible or meaningful.

nodes.title: Standard collection selection
nodes.summary: Choose a standard collection from ordering, access, mutation, ownership, and text/key semantics before optimizing.
nodes.definition: A requirements-led choice among sequence, owned UTF-8 text, and key/value lookup structures for the bounded task.
nodes.nonExample: Selecting HashMap because it is assumed universally faster without a keyed lookup requirement.

nodes.title: Concurrency and parallelism
nodes.summary: Distinguish independently progressing work from work physically executing at the same time.
nodes.definition: Concurrency structures multiple in-progress activities; parallelism executes activities simultaneously and depends on runtime resources/scheduling.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming two spawned threads necessarily execute simultaneously or improve throughput.

nodes.title: Value-producing control flow
nodes.summary: Choose branches or repetition constructs from required behavior while accounting for expression values and termination.
nodes.definition: Rust expressions such as if, match, and loop direct evaluation and may produce values under their specific rules.
nodes.nonExample: Selecting match merely because it is considered more Rust-like than if.

nodes.title: Copy semantics
nodes.summary: Types implementing Copy duplicate their value implicitly so the source remains usable after assignment or passing.
nodes.definition: A type-level contract permitting implicit bitwise value duplication with no custom Drop behavior.
nodes.nonExample: Any value that happens to be physically stored on the stack.

nodes.title: Crate roots and targets
nodes.summary: Map Cargo target conventions to the root source file from which rustc builds each crate.
nodes.definition: A crate root such as src/lib.rs, src/main.rs, or a configured target root forms the root module and entry compilation unit for one Cargo target.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming every .rs file under src/bin is part of the default binary crate.

nodes.title: Explicit CSV ingest contract
nodes.summary: Declare dialect, headers, field count, byte/text handling, null/missing policy, and typed schema before reading.
nodes.definition: The complete configuration and schema assumptions required to interpret row bytes consistently and reject ambiguity.
nodes.nonExample: Calling a file CSV and accepting whatever the parser happens to infer.

nodes.title: Decode and domain validation
nodes.summary: Distinguish parse/type conversion errors from validly decoded values that violate domain rules.
nodes.definition: A two-stage boundary that first obtains a typed record and then checks cross-field, range, uniqueness, and business invariants.
nodes.nonExample: Treating every successfully deserialized numeric field as acceptable domain data.

nodes.title: DataFusion query boundary
nodes.summary: Register bounded sources, construct SQL/DataFrame queries, execute them, and validate resulting Arrow batches.
nodes.definition: The embeddable engine boundary from declared table/schema through logical query to streamed Arrow RecordBatch results.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming SQL execution makes an invalid upstream schema correct.

nodes.title: Lock-order deadlock
nodes.summary: Detect cycles where threads hold resources while waiting for one another and establish one global acquisition order or redesign.
nodes.definition: A wait-for cycle that prevents all involved work from making progress even though memory access is type-safe.
nodes.nonExample: Any momentary blocking on a mutex that another thread eventually releases.

nodes.title: Hypothesis-driven debugging loop
nodes.summary: Move from reproducible observation to one causal hypothesis, discriminating experiment, root-cause fix, regression test, and broad rerun.
nodes.definition: An evidence-preserving sequence that changes one relevant cause at a time and records why the final repair explains the original observation.
nodes.nonExample: Changing several lines until the symptom disappears without a regression oracle.

nodes.title: Delayed Rust recheck
nodes.summary: Reassess a fresh variant after time has passed before treating provisional performance as durable.
nodes.definition: A scheduled retrieval opportunity whose prompt/variant differs from practice and whose result updates the same outcome-specific evidence trail.
nodes.nonExample: Three immediate repetitions counted as long-term retention.

nodes.title: Schedule-independent concurrency test
nodes.summary: Assert protocol completion and invariants through explicit synchronization rather than sleeps or output ordering.
nodes.definition: A test that controls required happens-before relationships with joins/channels/hooks and remains valid under any allowed scheduler interleaving.
nodes.nonExample: Sleeping 10 ms and assuming the worker must have completed.

nodes.title: Deterministic test control
nodes.summary: Control shared state, ordering, time, randomness, environment, and concurrency so repeated runs produce explainable outcomes.
nodes.definition: Explicit control or injection of nondeterministic inputs and interference within the scope required by the test.
nodes.nonExample: Retrying a flaky test until it passes without identifying the changing input.

nodes.title: Compiler diagnostic evidence
nodes.summary: Extract primary span, code, notes, and applicability while treating suggested edits as hypotheses to validate against intent.
nodes.definition: Structured or human compiler observations that locate a violated language contract and provide bounded explanatory cues.
nodes.nonExample: Blindly applying every help suggestion because the compiler emitted it.

nodes.title: Documentation test boundary
nodes.summary: Compile or run documentation examples so public API guidance remains executable and current.
nodes.definition: A code block extracted by rustdoc and compiled/run under its declared documentation-test attributes.
nodes.nonExample: A prose example whose code is intentionally never checked but is presented as runnable.

nodes.title: Error handling boundary
nodes.summary: Handle, translate, retry, report, or terminate at the layer that owns the corresponding policy decision.
nodes.definition: A responsibility boundary where lower-level failure details become a domain, user, process, or invariant decision.
nodes.nonExample: Every helper independently logging, stringifying, and swallowing the same error.

nodes.title: Error context
nodes.summary: Add the failed operation and safe identifying details while preserving the underlying cause for diagnosis.
nodes.definition: Structured or display information that locates a failure in the current operation without destroying its source or leaking sensitive data.
nodes.nonExample: Replacing every lower-level error with the string something went wrong.

nodes.title: Explicit error classification
nodes.summary: Match Option/Result/error-kind variants when branches require materially different behavior.
nodes.definition: Pattern-based branching that distinguishes success, absence, and relevant failure variants at the layer responsible for the decision.
nodes.nonExample: Matching every error only to discard it and return an unrelated generic message.

nodes.title: Error propagation
nodes.summary: Return a failure to a caller with more responsibility or context instead of handling it prematurely.
nodes.definition: An early failure return that preserves or converts the error into the enclosing function's declared error contract.
nodes.nonExample: Ignoring the failure and continuing with fabricated success data.

nodes.title: Error source chain
nodes.summary: Link a higher-level error to the lower-level cause that produced it for layered diagnosis.
nodes.definition: A sequence exposed through Error::source in which each contextual error optionally identifies its underlying cause.
nodes.nonExample: Duplicating the same formatted text at every layer without a typed causal relationship.

nodes.title: Exclusive mutable borrowing
nodes.summary: Temporarily access and mutate a value through an exclusive mutable reference.
nodes.definition: A non-owning mutable reference whose live access excludes other live accesses that would conflict.
nodes.nonExample: Owning the referenced value or allowing arbitrary simultaneous readers and writers.

nodes.title: Executed Cargo tests
nodes.summary: Compile and run selected unit, integration, and documentation test targets.
nodes.definition: Behavioral evidence from cargo test under explicit package, target, feature, and harness rules.
nodes.nonExample: A successful cargo check with no test executable run.

nodes.title: Explicit Clone
nodes.summary: An explicit duplication operation that may run arbitrary code and incur nontrivial cost.
nodes.definition: A deliberate call to the Clone contract when independent duplicated ownership matches the program intent.
nodes.nonExample: A mandatory response to every borrow-checker diagnostic.

nodes.title: Failure-path fixture
nodes.summary: Construct an input or state that deterministically reaches a required error or invariant branch and asserts its observable contract.
nodes.definition: A controlled negative case whose expected error kind, message subset, state preservation, or panic invariant is explicit.
nodes.nonExample: A test that passes for any Err without checking which failure occurred.

nodes.title: FFI contract
nodes.summary: Define ABI, layout, ownership, allocation/free pairing, pointer validity, strings, errors, callbacks, threads, and unwind behavior at a foreign boundary.
nodes.definition: The complete cross-language agreement required to translate foreign calls/data into a narrow safe Rust wrapper.
nodes.nonExample: Declaring extern C and assuming Rust/C types and ownership automatically match.

nodes.title: Function contract
nodes.summary: Parameters and return type state the typed boundary while the body evaluates to the returned value or unit.
nodes.definition: A named callable boundary whose parameter and return types constrain valid calls and results.
nodes.nonExample: A comment describing inputs without an enforced signature.

nodes.title: Fuzz target and oracle
nodes.summary: Feed structured/unstructured generated input into a narrow target with assertions, differential checks, or sanitizer-detectable failures.
nodes.definition: A reproducible search harness whose input domain, failure oracle, corpus, minimized regressions, and resource bounds are explicit.
nodes.nonExample: Generating random bytes but asserting nothing beyond process completion.

nodes.title: Outcome-specific remediation routing
nodes.summary: Route failure to the smallest prerequisite, misconception, diagnostic, or practice cluster and preserve unrelated passed evidence.
nodes.definition: An explainable graph path from failed evidence to candidate root concepts and a fresh reassessment, with no opaque global demotion.
nodes.nonExample: Restarting the whole Rust course after one async shutdown failure.

nodes.title: Graceful async shutdown
nodes.summary: Detect shutdown, notify owned tasks, stop admission, drain or cancel bounded work, and await terminal results.
nodes.definition: A coordinated terminal protocol that closes producers, propagates cancellation, preserves required state, and observes task completion within a budget.
nodes.nonExample: Returning from main immediately after receiving Ctrl-C.

nodes.title: impl Trait positions
nodes.summary: Use bounded anonymous input types for convenience or hide one concrete return type behind a trait contract.
nodes.definition: Position-sensitive syntax whose argument form accepts an implementing type and whose return form denotes one hidden concrete implementing type.
nodes.nonExample: A return promise that may choose unrelated concrete types on different branches without indirection.

nodes.title: Fresh independent Rust transfer
nodes.summary: Solve an unseen problem in a changed context without tutor hints or generated solution while using allowed compiler/tests/docs workflow.
nodes.definition: Evidence that the learner can select and apply the underlying model beyond memorized surface structure with explicitly recorded support.
nodes.nonExample: Repeating the same exercise immediately after viewing its solution.

nodes.title: Integration test boundary
nodes.summary: Exercise a library as an external crate through its public API and realistic component collaboration.
nodes.definition: A separate tests/ crate that can reach only public items and therefore verifies consumer-visible contracts.
nodes.nonExample: An external test that depends on a private module path.

nodes.title: Item paths
nodes.summary: Name items from a crate root or current module with crate, self, super, crate names, and identifiers.
nodes.definition: A sequence of module/item segments whose resolution starts absolutely at a crate root or relatively in the current module.
nodes.nonExample: A filesystem path that bypasses the module tree and privacy rules.

nodes.title: Iteration ownership mode
nodes.summary: Predict whether traversal yields shared references, mutable references, or owned items and whether the collection remains usable.
nodes.definition: The relationship between the receiver's ownership/borrow mode, the iterator Item type, and post-iteration availability.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming every for loop copies elements and leaves every collection unchanged.

nodes.title: Iterator adapters
nodes.summary: Transform, filter, combine, or bound an iterator lazily while preserving a new iterator value.
nodes.definition: A method such as map or filter that consumes an iterator value and returns another iterator without fully traversing it.
nodes.nonExample: collect, which drives the iterator into a destination collection.

nodes.title: Iterator consumers
nodes.summary: Drive an iterator to produce a result, side effect, aggregate, search decision, or collection.
nodes.definition: A terminal or advancing operation that requests items through next, possibly stopping early according to its contract.
nodes.nonExample: A lazy map adapter stored without later iteration.

nodes.title: Lazy iterator evaluation
nodes.summary: Iterator values perform no element processing until a consumer drives next.
nodes.definition: Deferred element production in which adapters compose behavior and work occurs only when next is requested by a consumer.
nodes.nonExample: Expecting map to mutate or print every element before any consumer runs.

nodes.title: Explicit lifetime annotations
nodes.summary: Name reference lifetime relationships in signatures and borrowed data types when inference is insufficient or the API contract needs expression.
nodes.definition: Named lifetime parameters applied to references to express equality or outlives relationships the borrow checker must validate.
nodes.nonExample: A directive that changes when an owned value is dropped.

nodes.title: Lifetime elision
nodes.summary: Apply the defined input/output signature rules that allow common lifetime relationships to be omitted without changing their semantics.
nodes.definition: A limited set of compiler rules that assign omitted lifetimes in function and method signatures when output provenance is unambiguous.
nodes.nonExample: General inference that guesses which of multiple unrelated input references an output borrows.

nodes.title: Reference lifetime relationships
nodes.summary: Describe which input borrow a returned or stored reference is tied to and the overlap in which that reference may be used.
nodes.definition: A compile-time relationship among reference validity regions, constrained so no reference outlives the data it borrows.
nodes.nonExample: A timer controlling how long a heap allocation exists at runtime.

nodes.title: Lock scope and guard lifetime
nodes.summary: Hold a mutex guard only across the protected invariant transition and release it before unrelated blocking or expensive work.
nodes.definition: The lexical/control-flow region in which the guard retains exclusive access and unlocks on drop.
nodes.nonExample: Holding a lock while waiting for a channel message unrelated to the protected mutation.

nodes.title: Loom concurrency model
nodes.summary: Replace supported synchronization with Loom types and assert invariants across a bounded deterministic state space.
nodes.definition: A small concurrency abstraction/model whose explored interleavings can falsify synchronization assumptions within documented bounds.
nodes.nonExample: Running an entire network service under Loom and assuming all real executions are covered.

nodes.title: Language-server feedback
nodes.summary: Editor-time semantic assistance from rust-analyzer that accelerates navigation and completion without replacing compiler/evaluator evidence.
nodes.definition: Advisory LSP responses scoped to the loaded project and current analysis state.
nodes.nonExample: A passing build, test, or hidden evaluator result.

nodes.title: Macro activation
nodes.summary: Use declarative or procedural code generation only when repeated syntax or compile-time derivation is clearer than ordinary functions, traits, or derives.
nodes.definition: A reviewed compile-time generation boundary with explicit input syntax, expansion behavior, diagnostics, testing, and maintenance benefit.
nodes.nonExample: A macro replacing a readable function solely to reduce a few repeated tokens.

nodes.title: Message-passing concurrency
nodes.summary: Transfer owned data and protocol events through channel endpoints instead of exposing shared mutable state.
nodes.definition: A producer/consumer communication model in which sending transfers a message and receiving observes data or disconnection according to channel semantics.
nodes.nonExample: A guarantee of bounded memory or backpressure from the unbounded channel constructor.

nodes.title: Minimal reproducer
nodes.summary: Remove irrelevant code and state while preserving the failure, making causal hypotheses faster to discriminate.
nodes.definition: The smallest controlled program, test, input, and command that still demonstrates the observed failure.
nodes.nonExample: A rewritten toy that no longer exhibits the original failure mechanism.

nodes.title: Module declaration
nodes.summary: Attach an inline or conventionally located module body at one position in the crate's module tree.
nodes.definition: A mod declaration creates a module node and, when terminated by a semicolon, directs the compiler to the module body's conventional file.
nodes.nonExample: A C-style textual include repeated in every file that uses the module.

nodes.title: Module tree
nodes.summary: The nested namespace and privacy structure rooted at crate, independent of how module bodies are split across files.
nodes.definition: A hierarchy of modules and items attached beneath a crate root through declarations.
nodes.nonExample: A directory scan that automatically turns every file into a module.

nodes.title: Monomorphization
nodes.summary: Compile used generic definitions into concrete type-specific code for static dispatch.
nodes.definition: Compile-time specialization of a generic definition for the concrete substitutions used by the program.
nodes.nonExample: A universal runtime container that erases every concrete type.

nodes.title: Move semantics
nodes.summary: Assignment, argument passing, and returning may transfer ownership and invalidate the previous place for non-Copy values.
nodes.definition: A transfer of a value's ownership that makes the source place unusable unless it is reinitialized.
nodes.nonExample: An automatic deep copy of heap data.

nodes.title: Mutex poisoning
nodes.summary: Treat a panic while holding a mutex as advisory evidence that protected state may violate its invariant.
nodes.definition: A best-effort marker returned by lock acquisition after another thread panicked while holding the mutex, requiring explicit recovery or propagation policy.
nodes.nonExample: A soundness boundary that always detects and prevents every corrupted shared state.

nodes.title: Named generic relationships
nodes.summary: Use a named type parameter when multiple signature positions or bounds must refer to the same selected type.
nodes.definition: A declared generic name reused to express type identity or shared bounds across parameters, returns, fields, or impls.
nodes.nonExample: Two independent anonymous input parameters assumed to have the same concrete type.

nodes.title: Runtime operability contract
nodes.summary: Define configuration validation, health, version/provenance, logs, startup, shutdown, recovery, and baseline observations for a release.
nodes.definition: The externally observable behaviors operators need to start, inspect, stop, diagnose, and recover the built application safely.
nodes.nonExample: A release binary that compiles but has no documented configuration or shutdown behavior.

nodes.title: Ownership
nodes.summary: Rules that assign responsibility for a Rust value and trigger cleanup when its owner leaves scope.
nodes.definition: At a program point, each value has one owner; ownership can transfer, and an owned value is dropped when its owner leaves scope unless it was moved.
nodes.nonExample: Classifying every stack value as copied and every heap-backed value as moved without consulting its type.

nodes.title: Packages and crates
nodes.summary: Distinguish a Cargo package manifest from the library and binary compilation units it describes.
nodes.definition: A package is a Cargo-managed bundle described by Cargo.toml; a crate is one library or executable compilation unit rooted at a source file.
nodes.nonExample: Calling every Rust source file a separate crate.

nodes.title: Panic and violated invariants
nodes.summary: Stop normal execution when the program reaches a state its valid API contract says should be impossible or unsafe to continue from.
nodes.definition: A terminal failure path for bugs or broken invariants, with unwind or abort behavior selected by build/runtime policy.
nodes.nonExample: A default response to a missing user-selected file that the caller could report or retry.

nodes.title: Arrow/Parquet round trip
nodes.summary: Persist schema-conforming batches and verify schema, row count, nulls, and selected values after reading them back.
nodes.definition: A tested conversion between in-memory Arrow batches and Parquet storage with explicit compatibility and correctness oracles.
nodes.nonExample: A writer returning Ok without inspecting the produced file.

nodes.title: Pin activation for address sensitivity
nodes.summary: Reach for Pin internals only when a value's validity depends on its address remaining stable after entering a state.
nodes.definition: A justified use of Pin<Ptr> to uphold a no-move contract for an address-sensitive pointee through its drop lifecycle.
nodes.nonExample: Manually pinning every future merely because async is involved.

nodes.title: Poll and wake
nodes.summary: A future reports Ready or Pending and arranges a wakeup when it may make progress.
nodes.definition: The executor/future protocol where poll advances available work and a Waker schedules a later poll after readiness changes.
nodes.nonExample: Busy-loop polling every pending future continuously.

nodes.title: Project-stage Rust readiness
nodes.summary: Unlock a stage only when its named prerequisite outcomes have current evidence and the learner can explain why each is needed.
nodes.definition: A stage-specific decision combining prerequisite outcome state, relevant artifact/tests, support, delay, risks, and allowed remediation or diagnostic skip path.
nodes.nonExample: Unlocking QUAY because the learner reports high Rust confidence.

nodes.title: Public re-export
nodes.summary: Expose a reachable public item through a chosen public API path using pub use.
nodes.definition: A public use declaration that makes an existing public item reachable through the re-exporting module's API path.
nodes.nonExample: Making a private item externally usable without changing its effective visibility.

nodes.title: Rust quality gate
nodes.summary: Run the smallest explicit formatter, lint, check, test, and documentation command set that enforces supported behavior.
nodes.definition: A deterministic set of named checks whose failure blocks integration and whose scope/lint levels are repository policy.
nodes.nonExample: Installing every third-party quality tool before a concrete invariant needs it.

nodes.title: Evidence-based Rust readiness
nodes.summary: Promote readiness from a reviewable set of independent, delayed, and project evidence rather than course completion or confidence.
nodes.definition: A versioned decision over outcome-specific attempts, support, tests, artifacts, delay, reviewer, and unresolved gaps that can be explained and reversed.
nodes.nonExample: Marking ready because every lesson page was opened.

nodes.title: Rust readiness portfolio
nodes.summary: Retain code, tests, diagnostic/root-cause notes, design trade-offs, release provenance, and review results that stand without tutor narration.
nodes.definition: A small independently inspectable artifact set connecting claimed outcomes to source, commit/checksum, environment, executable evidence, reflection, and known limitations.
nodes.nonExample: A screenshot of a green checkmark with no source or tests.

nodes.title: Recoverability at a boundary
nodes.summary: Decide whether a caller can respond meaningfully to a failure without violating program invariants.
nodes.definition: A contextual classification based on responsibility, available alternatives, and whether normal execution can remain correct.
nodes.nonExample: Labeling every I/O failure recoverable and every programmer assertion unrecoverable without examining the boundary.

nodes.title: Regression test
nodes.summary: Encode the smallest behavior that failed so the original bug would fail again if its cause returns.
nodes.definition: A durable deterministic test whose fixture and oracle specifically distinguish the previously observed defect from correct behavior.
nodes.nonExample: A broad test that happened to pass after the fix but would also pass with the original bug.

nodes.title: Release package verification
nodes.summary: List, assemble, extract, and build the distributable package before publishing or deployment.
nodes.definition: A clean-room check of exactly which source, metadata, lock, license, and generated files enter a Cargo distribution artifact.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming the git worktree and packaged artifact contain identical files.

nodes.title: Representative Rust breadth
nodes.summary: Require observable capability from toolchain and ownership through APIs, collections, abstraction, errors, tests, concurrency/async, release, and data transfer.
nodes.definition: A finite set of representative outcome clusters covering the default Rust spine without requiring every fact or optional advanced branch.
nodes.nonExample: A checklist demanding unsafe, FFI, macros, and pinning before any real project needs them.

nodes.title: Reproducible Rust build evidence
nodes.summary: Pin resolution and toolchain inputs, build clean with locked dependencies, and record environment and output checksums.
nodes.definition: Evidence that the declared source, toolchain, target, dependency resolution, environment, and command reproduce the expected artifact or behavior.
nodes.nonExample: A successful incremental build on one dirty workstation.

nodes.title: Row error provenance
nodes.summary: Attach file/source, row/record, field, raw-safe excerpt, and error class to rejected input.
nodes.definition: Enough bounded non-secret origin context to reproduce, count, quarantine, and repair a row-level failure.
nodes.nonExample: Returning only 'invalid data' after discarding record position and cause chain.

nodes.title: Safe abstraction over unsafe internals
nodes.summary: Use privacy and validated constructors/methods so no safe caller can violate the internal unsafe invariant.
nodes.definition: A module/API boundary whose public safe surface preserves every invariant relied on by contained unsafe code for all safe inputs and call sequences.
nodes.nonExample: A public safe method that permits a caller to invalidate pointer or length invariants.

nodes.title: Scope and drop
nodes.summary: Trace when bindings are valid and when an owned value's cleanup occurs after replacement, move, or scope exit.
nodes.definition: The relationship among binding validity, ownership transfer, assignment replacement, and automatic destructor execution.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming every value is dropped at the brace where its original binding was declared even after a move.

nodes.title: Typed serialization boundary
nodes.summary: Keep domain Rust types separate from the format-specific serializer/deserializer that encodes them.
nodes.definition: A trait-based mapping where a Rust data model supplies Serialize/Deserialize and a format implementation supplies representation rules.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming Serde itself parses every file format or validates every domain invariant.

nodes.title: Shared borrowing
nodes.summary: Temporarily access a value through one or more immutable references without taking ownership.
nodes.definition: A non-owning immutable reference whose valid use cannot overlap a conflicting mutable borrow.
nodes.nonExample: A second owner responsible for dropping the referenced value.

nodes.title: Synchronized shared state
nodes.summary: Share ownership and serialize mutation when multiple threads must maintain one common invariant.
nodes.definition: A concurrency design where threads reach the same state through synchronization that protects every relevant invariant transition.
nodes.nonExample: Cloning an Arc and mutating its inner value without synchronization.

nodes.title: Spawned task ownership and Send bounds
nodes.summary: Move owned state into spawned tasks and keep non-Send values out of state held across await when required by the scheduler.
nodes.definition: The lifetime and thread-transfer constraints on a spawned future and every value retained across its suspension points.
nodes.nonExample: Interpreting a 'static bound as proof that the task lives forever.

nodes.title: Static package checking
nodes.summary: Compile enough of selected Cargo targets to report many errors without final code generation or executing tests.
nodes.definition: The evidence produced by cargo check for selected packages, targets, and features.
nodes.nonExample: Proof that runtime behavior and all code-generation paths are correct.

nodes.title: Streaming row pipeline
nodes.summary: Transform one record at a time or in bounded chunks without retaining the whole input by default.
nodes.definition: An iterator-driven read/decode/validate/transform/write flow with explicit error and allocation policy.
nodes.nonExample: Collecting all input rows before the first validation or output operation without need.

nodes.title: Support provenance
nodes.summary: Record compiler/docs/hint/solution/external-help use so evidence strength is transparent without policing or shaming tool use.
nodes.definition: Per-attempt metadata naming allowed support mode and transitions, used to interpret evidence and select a fresh follow-up rather than infer misconduct.
nodes.nonExample: Guessing whether the learner used AI from code style or paste behavior.

nodes.title: Bounded test evidence
nodes.summary: Interpret a test result only for the targets, inputs, environment, and assertions actually executed.
nodes.definition: Repeatable empirical evidence that selected behavior satisfied or violated a stated oracle under a recorded setup.
nodes.nonExample: Concluding that no bugs exist because cargo test returned zero.

nodes.title: Focused test execution
nodes.summary: Filter one failing test and expose its output or serialize threads to shorten the observation loop without narrowing final verification.
nodes.definition: A temporary execution selection used to reproduce and inspect one failure before rerunning the full relevant suite.
nodes.nonExample: Running only the repaired test and claiming the package is regression-free.

nodes.title: Behavioral test oracle
nodes.summary: State the observable output, state transition, error, or invariant that distinguishes correct behavior from a plausible wrong result.
nodes.definition: An assertion derived from the requirement rather than copied from the current implementation.
nodes.nonExample: Asserting only that a function returned without panicking when its result matters.

nodes.title: Thread lifecycle and join
nodes.summary: Retain completion handles, observe panics, and establish when parent work may safely continue or exit.
nodes.definition: The spawn-to-completion relationship in which JoinHandle or scope establishes waiting, result/panic observation, and resource lifetime.
nodes.nonExample: Dropping every handle and assuming background work finishes before main exits.

nodes.title: Thread closure ownership transfer
nodes.summary: Move captured values into spawned work when borrowed data cannot be proven to outlive the thread.
nodes.definition: Ownership transfer into the closure environment so the spawned thread owns values for its required lifetime.
nodes.nonExample: A way to keep using the moved value concurrently from the parent.

nodes.title: Timeout budget
nodes.summary: Treat a timeout as the caller's finite wait budget and specify the cancellation and cleanup consequences separately.
nodes.definition: A deadline or duration that bounds how long a caller waits while leaving operation termination and side-effect policy explicit.
nodes.nonExample: Equating a timeout error with proof that the remote or spawned work stopped.

nodes.title: Toolchain resolution
nodes.summary: Determine the rustup-selected toolchain from explicit overrides, directory context, toolchain files, and defaults.
