nodes.definition: The documented precedence by which rustup selects the binaries behind rustc, Cargo, and components.
nodes.nonExample: Assuming the nearest rust-toolchain.toml wins without checking higher-precedence command or environment overrides.

nodes.title: Trait bounds
nodes.summary: State the capabilities a generic parameter must provide so the body and callers are checked against one explicit contract.
nodes.definition: A constraint such as T: Trait, possibly in a where clause, that limits valid substitutions and authorizes trait operations in the generic definition.
nodes.nonExample: A runtime if-statement that discovers whether an arbitrary type has a method.

nodes.title: Trait implementation and coherence
nodes.summary: Provide a trait's behavior for a type only where Rust's locality/coherence rules permit one unambiguous implementation.
nodes.definition: An impl Trait for Type block satisfying the trait contract under rules that prevent conflicting external-trait/external-type implementations.
nodes.nonExample: Implementing a foreign trait for a foreign type in an unrelated crate.

nodes.title: Type-guided interpretation
nodes.summary: A value's type determines how its memory is interpreted and which operations are valid.
nodes.definition: Reasoning from the concrete or inferred Rust type to valid representation and operations.
nodes.nonExample: Choosing a type solely because its printed value looks similar.

nodes.title: Undefined-behavior falsification
nodes.summary: Run supported unsafe tests under Miri with varied seeds/targets while retaining code review and documented unsupported cases.
nodes.definition: Dynamic attempts to expose violations of unsafe contracts without mistaking unobserved UB for a proof of soundness.
nodes.nonExample: One clean Miri run used as a correctness certificate.

nodes.title: Unit test boundary
nodes.summary: Exercise a small behavior near its implementation, including private details only when that coupling is intentional.
nodes.definition: A test compiled within the crate/module context and optimized for local feedback and precise failure localization.
nodes.nonExample: A claim that every private helper must have a one-to-one test.

nodes.title: Unsafe safety obligation
nodes.summary: State each precondition, invariant, valid lifetime/layout/aliasing state, and caller/callee responsibility the type system cannot enforce.
nodes.definition: A documented proof obligation created by an unsafe declaration or required before an unsafe operation can be soundly performed.
nodes.nonExample: A SAFETY comment that only restates the operation without proving its preconditions.

nodes.title: use bindings
nodes.summary: Bring a reachable path into the current scope under its name or an explicit alias.
nodes.definition: A lexical name binding that shortens a reachable path without deciding whether the item is compiled or publicly exposed.
nodes.nonExample: An include directive that copies the target module's code into the current file.

nodes.title: Visibility and privacy
nodes.summary: Control which ancestors, descendants, sibling paths, or external crates may reach an item.
nodes.definition: Items are private by default; pub and restricted pub forms widen reachability only when every containing path segment is accessible.
nodes.nonExample: A public module that silently makes every nested item and struct field public.

nodes.title: Cargo workspace
nodes.summary: Coordinate related packages under shared resolution, lockfile, output, and inheritable workspace configuration.
nodes.definition: A Cargo workspace root and member set that coordinate multiple packages while each package retains its own targets.
nodes.nonExample: A requirement that every growing module become a separate crate.

nodes.title: Apache Arrow Rust
nodes.summary: Rust implementation of Arrow arrays, schemas, and RecordBatches.
nodes.versionScope: release family compatible with selected DataFusion, pinned by Cargo.lock

nodes.title: csv
nodes.summary: Streaming configurable CSV reader/writer with raw record and Serde support.
nodes.versionScope: 1.x, pinned by the future Cargo lockfile

nodes.title: Apache DataFusion
nodes.summary: Embeddable Arrow-native query engine with SQL and DataFrame APIs.
nodes.versionScope: release pinned by the future Cargo lockfile

nodes.title: Loom
nodes.summary: Permutation-testing crate for small deterministic models of concurrent Rust code.
nodes.versionScope: 0.7 family or reviewed successor, pinned only when a model exists

nodes.title: Apache Parquet Rust
nodes.summary: Parquet file APIs including Arrow RecordBatch readers and writers.
nodes.versionScope: same arrow-rs release family as Arrow, pinned by Cargo.lock

nodes.title: Serde
nodes.summary: Trait-based serialization and deserialization between Rust types and format implementations.
nodes.versionScope: 1.x, pinned by the future Cargo lockfile

nodes.title: Tokio
nodes.summary: An asynchronous runtime and I/O/concurrency toolkit used by the production Rust path.
nodes.versionScope: version pinned by the future Cargo lockfile; sources verified 2026-07-18

nodes.title: Validated Arrow batch construction
nodes.summary: Translate already validated domain rows into schema-matched builders, append nulls explicitly, and finish batches at a declared bound.
nodes.invariant: Each emitted batch has the approved schema, equal column lengths, one append decision per input row/field, and no implicit null/default conversion.
selectionCues: validated row/domain values enter a columnar boundary
schema and nullability are fixed
downstream accepts repeated RecordBatch units

nodes.title: Schema-checked null-aware Arrow kernel
nodes.summary: Validate input fields and concrete arrays, iterate validity-aware column values, and emit a length-preserving typed result.
nodes.invariant: Every output slot corresponds to the same input row; null and overflow policy is explicit; type mismatch returns an error before value access.
selectionCues: operation is column-wise
schema is known only at runtime
null propagation or filtering is specified

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(output rows) or O(1) for scalar reduction

nodes.title: Measured bounded async pipeline
nodes.summary: Place explicit item/byte/concurrency caps at admission and stages, propagate waiting, enforce overload/shutdown policy, and measure occupancy/age/service/drop/reject.
nodes.invariant: Total live work/memory is bounded by declared capacities; every admitted item is processed once or receives a visible policy outcome; sustained overload cannot silently grow state.
selectionCues: asynchronous stages have unequal/bursty rates
memory/latency/overload behavior must be bounded
upstream can wait or an explicit loss/reject policy exists

complexityBounds.time: O(items × stage work + waiting); throughput limited by bottleneck service rate
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(sum queue byte capacities + bounded per-stage/state/concurrency)

nodes.title: Bounded typed file snapshot
nodes.summary: Check/limit a small UTF-8 file, deserialize one wire value, validate into domain state, and return classified provenance-rich errors.
nodes.invariant: No domain value is published unless bytes satisfy the size/text/format/schema/domain contracts; every failure retains source and class without partial domain mutation.
selectionCues: one complete snapshot is required
maximum bytes safely fit memory
EOF is the document boundary

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(file bytes + decoded value), subject to explicit limit

nodes.title: Consistent checkpoint and replay-safe effects
nodes.summary: Snapshot state with source positions, durably publish completion, restore latest valid point, replay deterministically, and make sink effects idempotent/transactional.
nodes.invariant: After any modeled crash, recovered managed/final sink state equals one failure-free execution for the committed input prefix, within the explicitly claimed guarantee.
selectionCues: source can replay from durable positions
stateful computation must survive failure
sink offers stable idempotency or coordinated transactions for end-to-end exactly-once

complexityBounds.time: normal work + checkpoint serialization/I/O + replay after latest checkpoint
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(live state + in-progress/retained checkpoints + bounded in-flight data)

nodes.title: Bounded correlated telemetry investigation
nodes.summary: Start from an SLI symptom, pivot through an exemplar or validated context to traces/logs/run artifacts, compare dependency/resource evidence, preserve sampling gaps, and rank supported hypotheses without inventing causality.
nodes.invariant: Every correlation edge matches declared identity/resource context; every causal statement cites temporal plus mechanism/counterfactual evidence; metric series remain within budget; sensitive fields never enter output; sampling/missing evidence remains explicit.
selectionCues: aggregate SLO symptoms need per-operation evidence
trace/log/metric/run signals share context
high-cardinality detail must stay out of metrics
diagnosis must distinguish evidence from hypothesis

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(bounded series aggregates + retained sampled records + correlation edges)

nodes.title: Contract-first bounded DataFusion query
nodes.summary: Register typed sources, construct SQL/DataFrame intent, validate schema/plan, execute as finite streams, and compare results with an independent oracle.
nodes.invariant: All emitted batches satisfy the query schema/semantics and resource/cancellation limits; result correctness is independent of the chosen physical plan.
selectionCues: relational transforms over Arrow/file sources are required
input/output/null/order contracts are fixed
results may exceed safe collect size

complexityBounds.time: plan cost plus selected scan/operator work
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: bounded operator/runtime memory plus output batch, except explicitly spillable/blocking operators

nodes.title: Plan- and metric-guided query diagnosis
nodes.summary: Capture normalized logical/physical plans, execute controlled variants, compare exact results, and attribute work to scans, exchanges, and operators with metrics.
nodes.invariant: Baseline and candidate results are equivalent; every performance claim names a structural change and measured work under the same data/configuration.
selectionCues: query is correct but work/latency is unexplained
pushdown, partitions, or blocking operators may dominate
a reproducible dataset/configuration exists

complexityBounds.time: O(number of controlled executions × query work)

nodes.title: Deterministic keyed event-time window aggregation
nodes.summary: Validate timestamp/key, assign half-open windows, update bounded associative state, advance minimum active watermark, fire eligible windows, and clean at the lateness horizon.
nodes.invariant: Each admitted event contributes exactly once to every assigned key/window; watermarks never regress; state/output transitions follow only the explicit trace/policy.
selectionCues: unbounded events require time-bounded aggregation
event timestamps matter more than arrival time
out-of-order/lateness assumptions and state limits are known

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(active key-window aggregate/revision state + bounded late routing)

nodes.title: Bounded framed record decoding
nodes.summary: Read one limited newline-delimited byte/text record at a time, deserialize/validate independently, and apply explicit fail-fast or quarantine policy.
nodes.invariant: At each record boundary, memory is bounded, physical record identity is known, accepted outputs are domain-valid, and a rejected record cannot corrupt neighboring framing/state.
selectionCues: input contains repeated independently framed values
whole input need not fit memory
per-record reject/continue semantics are defined

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(max record bytes + one decoded record), subject to limits

nodes.title: Validated commit and reachability maintenance
nodes.summary: Stage immutable files, build candidate metadata, compare-and-swap after operation validation, retry from refreshed state when safe, then expire/rewrite/delete only under explicit retention and complete reachability evidence.
nodes.invariant: Every visible state is one complete committed metadata graph; rewrites preserve logical rows; no file reachable from any retained/in-progress valid root is deleted.
selectionCues: multiple writers publish immutable files
metadata pointer supports atomic conditional replacement
time travel creates retained roots
file/manifest overhead needs measured maintenance

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(candidate metadata + retained-root reachability set + staged files)

nodes.title: Snapshot-to-file scan planner
nodes.summary: Resolve a snapshot root, traverse manifest-list/manifests, project predicates through each partition spec, apply conservative metrics pruning, and return files plus residual predicates and provenance.
nodes.invariant: The selected file set contains every file that may satisfy the predicate in the chosen committed snapshot and no file outside that snapshot; residual evaluation preserves row truth across all active specs/schemas.
selectionCues: a table snapshot names immutable files through manifests
file/partition metrics can prune safely
schemas or partition specs evolve
time-travel reproducibility matters

complexityBounds.time: O(selected manifest metadata + candidate file entries), not directory listing size

nodes.title: Deterministic interval-scoped DAG runner
nodes.summary: Topologically schedule eligible task instances for pinned intervals/versions, cap active work, persist attempt state, atomically publish stable artifacts, retry safely, and reconcile catchup/backfill coverage.
nodes.invariant: Each required interval/task has at most one published logical artifact per declared version; every published artifact comes from satisfied dependencies and complete validation; retries/backfills do not silently change interval inputs or duplicate effects.
selectionCues: tasks form an acyclic artifact dependency graph
historical intervals must be reproducible
attempts may fail or repeat
backfill concurrency and publication need explicit bounds

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(active attempts + run/task state + artifact metadata)

nodes.title: Keyed late-result upsert/changelog
nodes.summary: Give each key/window result stable identity/version, emit main and admitted-late replacements or before/after changes, and finalize after cleanup.
nodes.invariant: Applying the emitted change log to an empty keyed sink yields exactly the current window state once; too-late events never silently mutate finalized results.
selectionCues: low-latency preliminary results are required
late events may revise prior output
downstream supports stable keys plus upsert or retraction semantics

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(active key-window last-emitted values/versions + sink state)

nodes.title: Identity-normalized lineage event graph
nodes.summary: Normalize producer events to job/run/dataset/artifact versions, deduplicate lifecycle claims, connect used/generated/derived relations, preserve partial/conflicting evidence, and answer upstream/downstream/root-cause/impact paths with confidence.
nodes.invariant: No lineage edge exists without a source claim or explicit reviewed inference; canonical identities do not collide; duplicate/out-of-order events do not multiply entities; missing/conflicting evidence remains visible.
selectionCues: multiple jobs/runs produce and consume versioned datasets
events arrive asynchronously and may repeat
impact and root-cause paths require data rather than control dependencies
provenance confidence must be auditable

nodes.title: Recoverable WAL–memtable–flush lifecycle
nodes.summary: Sequence and checksum each update, commit it to the WAL before ack, apply to a bounded memtable, install verified flush output, and recover by replay.
nodes.invariant: After any modeled crash, every acknowledged update appears exactly once in recovered version history and no unacknowledged/torn tail is reported as committed.
selectionCues: recent writes must survive restart
updates are buffered before immutable storage
sync/ack and recovery contracts are explicit

complexityBounds.time: amortized append plus O(log memtable entries) model update; recovery O(valid WAL records)
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(bounded memtable + WAL since installed coverage)

nodes.title: Versioned sorted-run merge and compaction
nodes.summary: Merge sorted run streams by key then descending sequence, emit newest required versions/tombstones, atomically install output, and delete inputs only afterward.
nodes.invariant: Before/after reads are equivalent for every retained snapshot; output is sorted, inputs remain valid until install, and obsolete data is dropped only with coverage proof.
selectionCues: overlapping immutable runs increase read/space cost
version/tombstone visibility is specified
temporary space and install/delete ordering are bounded

complexityBounds.time: O(total input entries log run count) with a heap, or O(total entries) for a fixed small run count
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(run count + output buffer/file + bounded metadata)

nodes.title: Finalized verified Parquet write
nodes.summary: Write compatible bounded Arrow batches into tuned row groups, flush under a memory policy, finish, reopen, validate, then publish.
nodes.invariant: Published artifacts have a complete footer, approved schema/properties, and reconciled row counts; no partial file is exposed as success.
selectionCues: durable analytical interchange is required
input is validated Arrow batches
schema, row-group, codec, memory, and publication contracts are fixed

complexityBounds.time: O(encoded input bytes + codec work + verification read)
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(in-progress row-group memory + one verification batch)

nodes.title: Projected and pruned Parquet scan
nodes.summary: Inspect metadata, project required columns, conservatively select candidate regions, decode bounded Arrow batches, and evaluate the exact predicate.
nodes.invariant: No matching row is discarded by metadata pruning; every emitted row satisfies the exact predicate and output schema/order contract.
selectionCues: only a subset of columns/rows is needed
metadata can rule out some regions
bounded Arrow output is consumed incrementally

complexityBounds.time: O(footer/index + selected compressed bytes + decoded candidate rows)
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(metadata + predicate cache limit + output batch)

nodes.title: Workload-aware partition and replica plan
nodes.summary: Assign a deterministic small key/token space from query and skew requirements, place distinct replicas across failure domains, and measure coverage, load, and topology-change movement.
nodes.invariant: Every key has exactly one primary and N distinct ordered physical replicas satisfying the declared domain policy; aggregate modeled load and movement are derived from the same deterministic ownership map.
selectionCues: keyed state must be distributed
query locality and skew can be modeled
replicas must survive named correlated failures
topology changes need bounded observable movement

complexityBounds.time: O(keys × routing cost + replicas) for an enumerated teaching workload

nodes.title: Threat-linked private-data lifecycle register
nodes.summary: Map each classified element/copy through purpose/flow/access/retention/deletion, attach threats and least controls, choose no-storage/minimization before encryption, map key/secret lifecycles, verify backups/derived/log copies, and review changes/residual risk.
nodes.invariant: Every collected sensitive element and derived/backup/log copy has a necessary purpose, owner, allowed principals, retention/deletion outcome and threat-linked control; expired/unneeded data becomes unreachable under policy; keys/secrets are separately lifecycle-managed and never recorded as data/audit content.
selectionCues: personal/confidential data enters multiple stores or artifacts
purpose/retention/deletion must be demonstrable
residual threats may justify encryption
secrets/keys and derived/log/backup copies need ownership

nodes.title: Bounded length-prefixed TCP session
nodes.summary: Incrementally decode fixed-header bounded frames, validate envelopes, dispatch one request ID once, queue full encoded responses, and close on unsafe framing/write state.
nodes.invariant: Every accepted byte belongs to exactly one validated frame in order; memory is bounded; each response retains request identity; partial/canceled output is never blindly replayed.
selectionCues: ordered reliable stream fits the protocol
messages need explicit framing
connection/resource/deadline limits are defined

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(max frame + bounded input/output queues) per connection

nodes.title: Bounded correlated UDP exchange
nodes.summary: Send one self-contained bounded request with an ID, retry under an overall deadline/backoff/rate policy, ignore malformed/unmatched duplicates, and make server handling idempotent or deduplicated.
nodes.invariant: Only a valid matching response completes the exchange; retries remain congestion-bounded and cannot multiply the command's logical effect.
selectionCues: one datagram can hold each self-contained message
loss/reorder/duplication semantics are acceptable and handled
custom retry burden is justified over TCP

complexityBounds.time: O(attempts × datagram bytes) within deadline/retry cap

nodes.title: Thresholded CSV quarantine ingestion
nodes.summary: Parse under a fixed dialect, accept independently valid rows, quarantine classified failures, and abort when a configured error budget is exceeded.
nodes.invariant: Every logical record becomes exactly one accepted domain row or one bounded redacted rejection; source counts reconcile and threshold crossing is deterministic.
selectionCues: row-level salvage is authorized
source identity/replay and quality threshold exist
partial acceptance is visible to downstream consumers

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(max record + bounded quarantine buffer + output streaming/staging)

nodes.title: Scheduled versioned replicated register
nodes.summary: Simulate one-key reads/writes over deterministic message/failure schedules, collect configured responders, reconcile versions, state the observed guarantee, retain hints, and repair divergence.
nodes.invariant: Every returned value is selected from recorded versions under the declared responder/conflict policy; acknowledged, missed, hinted, repaired, rejected, and timed-out effects remain auditable for every schedule.
selectionCues: single-key replicas can diverge
read/write response counts are tunable
concurrent versions need explicit reconciliation
partition and repair behavior must be demonstrated

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(replicas × retained versions + events + bounded hints)

nodes.title: Deterministic fixed-cluster Raft log model
nodes.summary: Drive persistent term/vote/log and volatile role/commit/apply state with an explicit message/crash/restart schedule; verify elections, conflict repair, current-term commit, ordered apply, deduplicated results, safety, and majority loss.
nodes.invariant: At most one leader is elected per term; equal index/term entries share a prefix; no two servers apply different commands at one index; committed entries survive future leaders; each request ID has at most one logical state-machine effect.
selectionCues: one deterministic state machine must survive non-Byzantine node/message failures
a fixed odd-size cluster and majority are explicit
safety must hold through divergent logs and elections
a logical scheduler can enumerate failure cuts

complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(cluster logs + queued events + client-result cache)

nodes.title: Exact event-window SLO evaluator
nodes.summary: Normalize valid/good events into explicit windows, apply late/missing/zero-traffic policy, compute weighted SLI, budget consumption/remaining and burn, and emit the exact contributing counts plus decision state.
nodes.invariant: For every window, good+bad equals valid after declared exclusions; budget arithmetic derives only from that population/target; late/missing/duplicate events have one visible policy outcome; zero denominator never becomes fake success.
selectionCues: a user journey has discrete validity and goodness criteria
an objective applies over a stated event/time window
late/missing data and low traffic need policy
budget state must drive a reviewed action

complexityBounds.time: O(events log windows) for sorted-window lookup or O(events) for one ordered window
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(active windows + dedupe identities + aggregate counters)

nodes.title: Strict typed CSV ingestion
nodes.summary: Parse one declared text dialect, validate the header/width, convert every row through wire and domain types, and fail before publishing partial output.
nodes.invariant: All emitted rows share the approved header/schema and are domain-valid; any rejected record aborts the batch with stable position and no partial commit.
selectionCues: producer contract is controlled
all-or-nothing correctness is required
UTF-8/header/width/schema are fixed

nodes.title: Complete transaction-history oracle
nodes.summary: Execute a small deterministic MVCC/lock-policy model, record versioned reads/writes/predicates/commit/abort, construct dependency evidence, test invariants and serial orders, and retry rejected transactions from the beginning.
nodes.invariant: Every committed result is classified from the complete history under the declared visibility/conflict policy; every aborted attempt contributes no database state and no unkeyed external effect.
selectionCues: multi-step invariants face concurrent access
isolation level behavior must be demonstrated
serialization/deadlock abort is possible
external effects must survive retry safely

complexityBounds.time: O(history events + transactions! × validation) for deliberately tiny serial-order fixtures
complexityBounds.auxiliarySpace: O(versions + predicates + history events + dependency edges)

nodes.title: Fail-closed validated identity/authorization gate
nodes.summary: At one shared boundary: parse/canonicalize/limit input, establish current identity/session, resolve tenant/object/action, evaluate deny-default least-privilege policy with sensitive-action freshness, invoke structured sinks, publish redacted audit, and test abuse variants.
nodes.invariant: No sensitive operation reaches its sink unless one canonical request is syntactically/semantically valid and the current authenticated subject is explicitly authorized for that tenant/object/action/context; all unmatched/error states deny; audit output contains outcome identity but no secret/sensitive payload.
selectionCues: untrusted input crosses into a data or execution sink
resources are scoped by owner/tenant/role/attributes
sessions and sensitive actions need current evidence
all paths must share one fail-closed policy point

nodes.title: Missing lifetime specifier
nodes.summary: Diagnostic family for reference-bearing types or signatures whose required lifetime relationship is absent or not elidable.

nodes.title: Trait bound not satisfied
nodes.summary: Diagnostic family for using a type where the required trait implementation or generic bound is absent.

nodes.title: Use of moved value
nodes.summary: Diagnostic family for using a place after its non-Copy value was moved.

nodes.title: Multiple mutable borrows
nodes.summary: Diagnostic family for overlapping mutable borrows that violate exclusivity.

nodes.title: Conflicting mutable and immutable borrow
nodes.summary: Diagnostic family for borrowing a value mutably while an incompatible immutable borrow remains relevant, or vice versa.

nodes.title: Private item used outside scope
nodes.summary: Diagnostic family for reaching an item through a path that its visibility does not permit.

nodes.title: Original practice: nearest catalog neighbors
nodes.summary: Given a validated strict-key BST and a query, return exact value or nearest lower and higher keys with one ordered descent.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official Rust docs allowed; candidate-invariant hint follows a full inorder baseline; reveal schedules a fresh bound query

nodes.title: Original practice: validate version-key tree
nodes.summary: Validate an owned optional tree under a declared duplicate-right policy using inherited lower/upper bounds and report the first invalid path.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official Rust docs allowed; ancestor-bound hint follows a local-child-only counterexample; reveal schedules a fresh bound-policy validator

nodes.title: Original practice: indivisible budget choices
nodes.summary: Choose each feature at most once under an integer budget, return maximum value plus stable selected IDs, and report the pseudo-polynomial resource bound.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official references allowed; item-plus-capacity/descending-update hint follows reuse; reveal schedules a fresh bounded-choice variant

nodes.title: Original practice: catalog probe
nodes.summary: Given a sorted unique identifier catalog, return either the matching record index or the position where a missing identifier belongs.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official Rust docs allowed; interval trace hint follows a non-shrinking or off-by-one trace; reveal schedules a fresh insertion-point variant

nodes.title: Original practice: closest ordered pair
nodes.summary: On sorted unique signed readings, return the index pair whose sum is closest to a target with lexicographic index tie-breaking.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official Rust docs allowed; discard-proof hint follows a written pair grid; reveal schedules a fresh ordered-pair objective

nodes.title: Original practice: credit-adjusted paths
nodes.summary: Compute source distances with signed credits or return a reachable negative-cycle witness using bounded edge passes.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official references allowed; pass-i invariant hint follows a negative-edge failure; reveal schedules a fresh signed graph

nodes.title: Original practice: dependency plan validator
nodes.summary: Return a stable valid build plan for all packages or a concrete directed cycle witness, including isolated packages.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official Rust docs allowed; active-versus-finished hint follows a false cycle/order; reveal schedules a fresh dependency graph

nodes.title: Original practice: stable duplicate counts
nodes.summary: Return each alias occurring more than once with its total count, ordered by first occurrence.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official Rust docs allowed; count/order hint follows a failed set-only explanation; solution reveal schedules a fresh frequency variant

nodes.title: Original practice: minimum-energy checkpoints
nodes.summary: Choose one- or two-step transitions through checkpoint costs, return minimum checked energy and a deterministic visited-index witness.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official references allowed; state/last-transition hint follows repeated recursion; reveal schedules a fresh transition graph

nodes.title: Original practice: checked expression-tree fold
nodes.summary: Evaluate a boxed integer expression tree postorder with checked arithmetic and return the first structural/arithmetic error by deterministic child order.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official Rust docs allowed; process-after-children hint follows a failed preorder trace; reveal schedules a fresh subtree fold

nodes.title: Original practice: fair bounded retry queue
nodes.summary: Process jobs FIFO; a first failure requeues once at the back, while success or second failure records a terminal result in processing order.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official Rust docs allowed; pending-order hint follows a written queue trace; reveal schedules a fresh bounded reenqueuing policy

nodes.title: Original practice: first threshold breach
nodes.summary: In nondecreasing timestamped cumulative readings, return the first index whose value is at least a threshold, including no-breach and duplicate plateaus.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official Rust docs allowed; monotone-predicate hint follows an incorrect exact-match claim; reveal schedules a fresh upper-bound variant

nodes.title: Original practice: fractional capacity allocation
nodes.summary: Allocate divisible supplies by exact value density under checked rational comparison, then exhibit why the same rule fails for indivisible supplies.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official references allowed; cut-and-paste density hint follows a failed proof; reveal schedules a fresh divisible-resource variant

nodes.title: Original practice: maximum maintenance visits
nodes.summary: Select the largest number of compatible half-open maintenance visits and provide an exchange/stays-ahead proof plus counterexamples to two tempting rules.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official references allowed; transformed-optimum finish hint follows an intuition-only answer; reveal schedules a fresh interval objective

nodes.title: Original practice: canonical maintenance windows
nodes.summary: Validate and coalesce half-open maintenance windows under an explicit merge-touching policy, preserving source-independent canonical order.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official Rust docs allowed; emitted/current invariant hint follows a failed unsorted bridge case; reveal schedules a fresh endpoint-policy variant

nodes.title: Original practice: earliest longest monotone run
nodes.summary: Given signed measurements, return the start and length of the earliest longest strictly increasing contiguous run and explain the scan invariant.
nodes.supportPolicy: attempt first; compiler/tests and official Rust docs allowed; invariant hint only after an explicit current-state trace; full solution marks assisted and schedules a fresh variant

nodes.title: Original practice: nested metric total
nodes.summary: Fold an owned recursive category/value tree with checked arithmetic while reporting maximum depth and rejecting excessive depth.

nodes.title: Amortized means average input
nodes.summary: Confusing a deterministic operation-sequence guarantee with expectation over random inputs or choices.
diagnosticCues: requires an input distribution for an amortized argument

nodes.title: Undo happens automatically
nodes.summary: Allowing shared mutable path/used state to leak across siblings or early returns.
diagnosticCues: used flag remains set after child

nodes.title: BFS marks visited on dequeue
nodes.summary: Allowing converging predecessors to enqueue duplicate vertices and assign unstable parents.

nodes.title: Big-O is exact worst-case time
nodes.summary: Treating an upper-bound notation as an exact count and silently assuming a case and cost model.

nodes.title: Binary search works on unsorted input
nodes.summary: Applying interval elimination without an ordering or monotone-predicate precondition.
diagnosticCues: eliminated half can still contain answer

nodes.title: BST operations are always logarithmic
nodes.summary: Replacing height h with log n without a maintained balance invariant.

nodes.title: BST validity is only local child order
nodes.summary: Checking parent-child comparisons without propagating ancestor bounds to descendants.
diagnosticCues: accepts a left-subtree key above root

nodes.title: Density greedy solves indivisible capacity
nodes.summary: Applying a fractional exchange to whole items that cannot be substituted proportionally.

nodes.title: DFS returns a shortest unweighted path
nodes.summary: Treating first depth-first discovery as minimum edge count.
diagnosticCues: long branch accepted before direct edge

nodes.title: Dijkstra tolerates negative edges
nodes.summary: Applying the settled-minimum proof when a later negative edge can reduce a finalized distance.

nodes.title: Caching any recursion makes it efficient DP
nodes.summary: Ignoring exponential/distinct state dimensions, cyclic dependencies, or expensive transition enumeration.
diagnosticCues: no dependency order or state count

nodes.title: In-place DP update direction is arbitrary
nodes.summary: Overwriting a dependency before it is consumed or reusing a 0/1 item within the same iteration.
diagnosticCues: rolling row reads newly written neighbor

nodes.title: Item index alone captures capacity feasibility
nodes.summary: Merging partial histories with different remaining capacity into one subproblem.
diagnosticCues: same suffix expected to serve all used amounts

nodes.title: Union-find returns graph paths
nodes.summary: Confusing equality of representatives with an ordered route or weighted distance.
diagnosticCues: parent forest emitted as input path

nodes.title: Exact binary search returns the first duplicate
nodes.summary: Reading any matching index as a lower bound and losing duplicate-range semantics.
diagnosticCues: uses Ok index as first equal

nodes.title: Hashing is ordered worst-case constant time
nodes.summary: Assuming stable iteration order and unconditional O(1) lookup without key/hash/collision/capacity assumptions.

nodes.title: BinaryHeap is a stable min-heap
nodes.summary: Forgetting max default and assuming equal-priority arrival order is guaranteed.
diagnosticCues: smallest expected from pop without Reverse
no tie field in observable output

nodes.title: Heap iteration is sorted
nodes.summary: Treating a local parent-child invariant as a total order over backing storage.

nodes.title: Inorder traversal is sorted for every binary tree
nodes.summary: Confusing structural visit order with BST semantic key order.
diagnosticCues: claims traversal itself sorts arbitrary keys

nodes.title: Interval endpoints and touching are implicit
nodes.summary: Switching between closed/half-open and merge/no-merge adjacency without a domain contract.

nodes.title: Earliest finish maximizes interval weight
nodes.summary: Reusing the maximum-cardinality proof after intervals acquire unequal values.
diagnosticCues: count proof cited for weight objective

nodes.title: Linked insertion is universally faster
nodes.summary: Counting only rewiring while omitting position traversal, allocation, indirection, and cache costs.

nodes.title: Every Rust list needs shared mutability
nodes.summary: Introducing Rc<RefCell<_>> before the topology requires aliases or multiple owners.
diagnosticCues: runtime borrow checks with no alias requirement

nodes.title: Local optimum implies global optimum
nodes.summary: Treating greedy choice as self-evident without exchange, dominance, or special structure.

nodes.title: Any graph negative cycle invalidates source paths
nodes.summary: Ignoring whether the negative cycle is reachable from the selected source and whether arithmetic starts from infinity.

nodes.title: Nested pointer loops are automatically quadratic
nodes.summary: Ignoring that each endpoint may advance only n times across the whole run.

nodes.title: Prefix indices mirror element indices
nodes.summary: Mixing inclusive and half-open definitions and subtracting the wrong two boundaries.
diagnosticCues: prefix has length n without a documented convention

nodes.title: A base case guarantees termination
nodes.summary: Ignoring a recursive path that does not strictly approach the base case.

nodes.title: Set and frequency map are interchangeable
nodes.summary: Using membership-only state when counts are required or storing dummy counts when only presence matters.
diagnosticCues: cannot answer total occurrences from set

nodes.title: Rust string offsets are character indices
nodes.summary: Treating byte length/offsets as Unicode scalar or grapheme positions.

nodes.title: Passing examples proves the invariant
nodes.summary: Replacing a general correctness argument with a finite set of observed cases.

nodes.title: Finish order topologically sorts cycles
nodes.summary: Reversing DFS finish times without rejecting an edge to an active vertex.

nodes.title: Every trie prefix is a key
nodes.summary: Confusing a traversable shared prefix with terminal membership and ignoring the chosen string unit.
diagnosticCues: prefix query used for exact membership

nodes.title: Unstable sorting preserves equal-key order
nodes.summary: Depending on incidental tie order from an API that may reorder equal elements.
diagnosticCues: sort_unstable used with visible input-order ties

nodes.title: Vec front removal is constant-time queueing
nodes.summary: Transferring O(1) indexing to remove(0) while ignoring element shifts.
diagnosticCues: claims total O(n) for n front removals

nodes.title: Sum windows remain monotone with negatives
nodes.summary: Shrinking or expanding based only on the current sum when signed contributions can reverse the expected effect.
diagnosticCues: uses nonnegative threshold logic on signed values

nodes.title: Cargo features are exclusive modes
nodes.summary: Designing features as mutually exclusive switches despite additive activation and unification.

nodes.title: Lockfile guarantees bit reproduction

nodes.title: Advanced syntax proves seniority
nodes.summary: Adding unsafe, FFI, macros, or pinning to appear sophisticated without a constraint they solve.
diagnosticCues: benefit is novelty or fewer tokens only

nodes.title: Arc alone synchronizes mutation
nodes.summary: Confusing atomic reference-count ownership with protected access to the inner value.
diagnosticCues: expects Arc<T> to permit mutable shared access

nodes.title: Assignment always copies
nodes.summary: Assuming the source remains valid after assignment or argument passing regardless of the type's Copy contract.

nodes.title: Assisted success equals independent transfer
nodes.summary: Ignoring hints, viewed solutions, or generated fixes when interpreting evidence strength.
diagnosticCues: same prompt reused after solution reveal

nodes.title: Async makes work faster
nodes.summary: Assuming async syntax creates CPU parallelism or reduces an operation's intrinsic cost.
diagnosticCues: converts CPU loop to async without measurement

nodes.title: Successful build equals production readiness
nodes.summary: Treating compilation as evidence for tests, package contents, configuration, operability, and shutdown.
diagnosticCues: release checklist contains only cargo build --release
cannot show packaged file list or shutdown result

nodes.title: cargo check proves runtime correctness
nodes.summary: Confusing fast static package checking with code generation and executed test evidence.
diagnosticCues: claims tests passed after cargo check

nodes.title: Clone is the universal ownership fix
nodes.summary: Duplicating data before identifying whether transfer, shared access, mutation, or restructuring is intended.
diagnosticCues: adds clone without cost or responsibility rationale
clone masks an incorrect API boundary

nodes.title: Columnar means load everything
nodes.summary: Assuming Arrow or DataFusion requires collecting an entire dataset in memory.

nodes.title: The first compiler suggestion is the fix
nodes.summary: Applying a diagnostic suggestion without checking the program's intended ownership, API, or behavior.
diagnosticCues: suggested edit compiles but changes behavior

nodes.title: Course completion equals Rust mastery
nodes.summary: Treating consumed lessons or passed immediate checks as durable independent capability.
diagnosticCues: cites completed pages instead of artifacts
cannot solve a fresh delayed variant

nodes.title: CSV has one implicit dialect
nodes.summary: Assuming delimiter, headers, quoting, width, encoding, and missing-value semantics need no contract.
diagnosticCues: uses default reader on unknown source
cannot explain empty versus missing field

nodes.title: Deserialization proves domain validity
nodes.summary: Confusing successful syntax/type conversion with acceptable business or cross-field semantics.
diagnosticCues: accepts impossible ranges or inconsistent fields

nodes.title: Flatten every error into one string
nodes.summary: Discarding typed cause and recovery information while repeatedly adding generic text at each layer.
diagnosticCues: same error is logged at multiple layers

nodes.title: An unbounded generic supports every operation
nodes.summary: Using methods or operators on T without expressing the capability in its bounds.
diagnosticCues: generic body assumes Display or ordering without a bound
adds a concrete type instead of the required capability

nodes.title: Green tests prove correctness
nodes.summary: Treating selected passing assertions as proof there are no bugs or uncovered behaviors.
diagnosticCues: equates zero exit with complete specification

nodes.title: Iteration always copies and preserves the source
nodes.summary: Ignoring whether traversal borrows, mutably borrows, or consumes the collection and its items.
diagnosticCues: uses a moved collection after consuming iteration
mutates a collection while element borrows remain live

nodes.title: A lifetime annotation extends the value
nodes.summary: Treating a lifetime name as a runtime command that keeps borrowed data alive.
diagnosticCues: adds 'static or a wider 'a to fix a dangling reference
cannot identify the returned reference's owner

nodes.title: rust-analyzer is the correctness oracle
nodes.summary: Treating editor feedback or absence of markers as equivalent to a compiler/evaluator result.
diagnosticCues: calls editor completion a passing result

nodes.title: Iterator map runs eagerly
nodes.summary: Expecting an adapter chain to process elements before a consumer drives it.
diagnosticCues: expects side effects from unused map

nodes.title: mod textually includes a file
nodes.summary: Treating mod as repeated textual inclusion rather than declaring one module at one tree location.
diagnosticCues: redeclares the same module in each consumer
expects file placement alone to create a module

nodes.title: One score captures Rust readiness
nodes.summary: Collapsing distinct strengths, gaps, support, decay, and project evidence into an opaque aggregate gate.

nodes.title: pub recursively exposes contents
nodes.summary: Assuming pub on a module or struct exposes all descendants or fields.
diagnosticCues: marks only an ancestor pub after E0603
cannot identify the first private path segment

nodes.title: Question mark swallows or logs the error
nodes.summary: Failing to trace the early return and compatible error conversion performed by question-mark propagation.
diagnosticCues: cannot name the enclosing error type

nodes.title: A reference becomes another owner
nodes.summary: Treating borrowed access as responsibility to retain or drop the referenced value.
diagnosticCues: describes shared reference as duplicating ownership

nodes.title: Safe Rust prevents every concurrency bug
nodes.summary: Assuming memory safety and data-race prevention also guarantee progress, fairness, deterministic order, or protocol correctness.
diagnosticCues: uses output order as guaranteed behavior

nodes.title: A trailing semicolon still returns the expression value
nodes.summary: Confusing a value-producing final expression with a statement that evaluates to unit in the surrounding block.
diagnosticCues: predicts identical block values with and without a trailing semicolon

nodes.title: Sleep establishes completion order
nodes.summary: Using elapsed time as proof that another thread reached a required state.
diagnosticCues: test passes only with longer sleep
no join/channel/barrier establishes the observed order

nodes.title: Spawn automatically supervises
nodes.summary: Assuming spawned work is joined, cancelled, and error-observed without retaining and managing ownership.

nodes.title: String integer indexing yields characters
nodes.summary: Assuming a UTF-8 String supports constant-width character access by integer index.
diagnosticCues: equates byte length with character count

nodes.title: Every test should mirror private implementation
nodes.summary: Coupling tests to helpers and internal steps even when only public behavior matters.
diagnosticCues: refactor breaks tests without behavior change

nodes.title: Timeout cancels all work
nodes.summary: Confusing the caller ceasing to wait with safe termination of spawned children or external side effects.
diagnosticCues: retries after timeout without idempotency or cleanup reasoning

nodes.title: Advanced tool proves correctness
nodes.summary: Treating a clean Miri, fuzz, or Loom run as exhaustive proof rather than bounded falsification evidence.
diagnosticCues: cannot list unsupported APIs or unexplored inputs/interleavings
removes code review after tool passes

nodes.title: A trait is class inheritance
nodes.summary: Assuming trait implementation copies state, creates a subtype hierarchy, or permits foreign-trait/foreign-type implementations.

nodes.title: Unsafe disables Rust's rules
nodes.summary: Believing an unsafe block permits arbitrary behavior rather than a small set of unchecked operations with stronger obligations.
diagnosticCues: cannot distinguish unsafe fn from unsafe block

nodes.title: unwrap handles recoverable failure
nodes.summary: Treating conversion of Err into panic as a recovery strategy at an external/input boundary.
diagnosticCues: unwraps user or I/O input without an invariant
cannot state why Err is impossible

nodes.title: use makes an item public
nodes.summary: Confusing a private scoped name binding with a public re-export.
diagnosticCues: expects private use to change external API
cannot distinguish use from pub use

nodes.title: A wildcard match arm is always the safest default
nodes.summary: Using `_` to satisfy exhaustiveness without considering whether variants require distinct behavior or future review.
diagnosticCues: wildcard hides a semantically distinct variant
cannot state which values the wildcard intentionally groups

nodes.title: Derive honest time and space bounds
nodes.summary: State input/cost/case assumptions and derive time plus auxiliary-space bounds for an implementation.
nodes.observableBehavior: Counts dominant operations from code, distinguishes worst/expected/amortized claims, includes hidden Rust collection/allocation work, and provides a tight bound when supported.

nodes.title: Analyze states, transitions, encoding, and space
nodes.summary: Count exact reachable state domains and choice work, flag pseudo-polynomial dimensions, and justify any rolling/in-place order.
nodes.observableBehavior: Includes initialization/reconstruction, separates value from bit length, handles overflow/sentinels, and does not compress before dependency proof.

nodes.title: Choose a sequence/string unit
nodes.summary: Define element semantics and implement boundary-safe iteration/indexing without accidental copies.
nodes.observableBehavior: States byte/char/token/grapheme semantics, uses valid UTF-8 offsets, handles empty/multibyte/combining cases, and accounts for ownership/allocation in complexity.

nodes.title: Define and implement a sort contract
nodes.summary: State permutation, order, tie stability, mutation, allocation, and comparator/key requirements before selecting a Rust method.
nodes.observableBehavior: Chooses stable or unstable sorting from an observable tie requirement, uses a consistent total order, preserves multiplicities, and states time/space plus key-extraction costs.

nodes.title: Design and prove a DP recurrence
nodes.summary: Define sufficient state/base/choices, prove both recurrence directions, order dependencies, and map the requested result.
nodes.observableBehavior: Repairs underspecified states, rejects cyclic dependencies, distinguishes memo/tab evaluation, and writes a subproblem meaning before code.

nodes.title: Design a greedy rule from an exact contract
nodes.summary: State objective/feasibility and local choice, then choose exchange or stays-ahead proof rather than intuition.
nodes.observableBehavior: Names the transformed optimum/prefix measure, preserves feasibility/objective, handles ties/base cases, and labels unproved rules heuristics.

nodes.title: Explain a minimal owned list
nodes.summary: Trace Box/Option ownership, moves, traversal, and drop for a bounded singly linked exercise without shared mutability or unsafe code.
nodes.observableBehavior: Implements push_front/pop_front/borrowed iteration safely, names allocation and sequential costs, and states why production should still prefer Vec/VecDeque absent a requirement.

nodes.title: Implement deterministic safe greedy selection
nodes.summary: Encode total ties/endpoints/rational comparisons and analyze sorting, scan, arithmetic, output, and mutation costs.
nodes.observableBehavior: Avoids floating density when cross multiplication is safe/checked, validates ranges/capacity, and tests objective/set validity independently.

nodes.title: Implement safe Rust range state
nodes.summary: Use one half-open convention, checked boundaries, valid window sizes, and explicit accumulator overflow behavior.
nodes.observableBehavior: Handles empty/short/zero-k contracts without accidental panic, prevents usize underflow, uses checked/widened totals, and tests l=0, r=n, duplicates, and extremes.

nodes.title: Model and prove frontier order
nodes.summary: State LIFO/FIFO behavior, pending-state invariant, empty behavior, progress, and total operation bounds.
nodes.observableBehavior: Traces interleaved operations, proves every live item appears exactly once unless bounded reenqueues are specified, and derives processing order from the invariant.

nodes.title: Prove restoration and pruning
nodes.summary: Show sibling isolation, sound pruning, duplicate policy, termination, and output-sensitive cost.
nodes.observableBehavior: Pairs every mutation with cleanup on all control-flow paths, proves each prune, handles repeated choices, and distinguishes first/all solution contracts.

nodes.title: Prove BFS discovery, distance, and path
nodes.summary: Show discover-on-enqueue uniqueness, layer order, minimum-edge distance, and parent reconstruction.
nodes.observableBehavior: Handles converging edges, unreachable targets, source-to-source path, self/parallel edges, and verifies parent chains independently.

nodes.title: Prove BST bounds and descent
nodes.summary: Validate inherited global bounds and justify each pruned subtree under a duplicate policy.
nodes.observableBehavior: Finds globally invalid/local-valid counterexamples, uses strict/inclusive bounds consistently, traces neighbor candidates, and states O(h) without assuming balance.

nodes.title: Prove DSU partition and amortized choices
nodes.summary: Show forest validity, representative equivalence, component-count updates, and why rank/size plus compression are paired.
nodes.observableBehavior: Handles invalid IDs, self/redundant unions, deterministic external output, long sequences, and distinguishes amortized from worst-case claims.

nodes.title: Prove a hash-state invariant
nodes.summary: Show set/map state exactly represents the processed prefix and yields the specified stable output.
nodes.observableBehavior: Writes initialization/maintenance/termination for membership or counts, proves key equality semantics, and explains why hash iteration order cannot affect the result.

nodes.title: Prove a priority frontier invariant
nodes.summary: Show every processed candidate is retained or safely dominated and the root is the exact eviction/next boundary.
nodes.observableBehavior: Writes initialization/update/termination, handles equal priority deterministically, and explains why arbitrary internal order cannot affect the result.

nodes.title: Define and prove an interval sweep
nodes.summary: State endpoint/touch policy, validate/sort input, and prove emitted/current union state.
nodes.observableBehavior: Handles empty/invalid/touching/contained/equal intervals, separates merge from scheduling objectives, and derives sorting plus sweep costs.

nodes.title: Prove a loop invariant
nodes.summary: Write initialization, maintenance, and termination arguments that imply the required postcondition.
nodes.observableBehavior: Names the processed region and state meaning at the loop boundary, proves one arbitrary update, handles empty/boundary cases, and derives the final answer at termination.

nodes.title: Prove an ordered search
nodes.summary: Write and trace a shrinking half-open interval proof for exact or boundary semantics.
nodes.observableBehavior: States sorted/partitioned precondition, interval invariant, progress, termination, duplicate semantics, and empty/all-side boundary behavior without unsafe midpoint arithmetic.

nodes.title: Prove pointer and window progress
nodes.summary: State endpoint meanings, safe discard rules, strict progress, termination, and total-move bounds.
nodes.observableBehavior: Traces [left,right), explains each move from ordering or monotonicity, proves no skipped candidate can win, and derives O(n) from total endpoint moves rather than nested-loop appearance.

nodes.title: Prove recursive progress and cost
nodes.summary: State base/progress/return contracts and derive call-tree work plus maximum live depth.
nodes.observableBehavior: Names a decreasing measure on every edge, handles empty/deep input, separates total calls from depth, and chooses iteration when depth safety is uncertain.

nodes.title: Prove relaxation-based shortest paths
nodes.summary: State finite-estimate/path witnesses, method preconditions, termination, parent reconstruction, and negative-cycle/overflow semantics.
nodes.observableBehavior: Proves Dijkstra settlement or Bellman pass bounds, skips stale/unreachable state, checks arithmetic, and validates every parent edge and path sum.

nodes.title: Return a topological order or cycle proof
nodes.summary: Maintain DFS state across all components and verify edge order or reconstruct a directed cycle.
nodes.observableBehavior: Distinguishes active from finished neighbors, rejects self-loops/cycles, includes isolated vertices, and validates every returned edge precedence.

nodes.title: Reconstruct and validate a DP witness
nodes.summary: Follow stored/recomputed optimal transitions under deterministic ties and independently verify feasibility and objective equality.
nodes.observableBehavior: Handles empty/equal-optimum cases, never follows unreachable state, and states when compression is incompatible with required witness output.

nodes.title: Refute an invalid greedy rule
nodes.summary: Generate and minimize a valid counterexample, identify the failed proof premise, and route the problem to another method.
nodes.observableBehavior: Separates counterexample falsification from proof, covers weighted/integral boundary changes, and does not patch a rule ad hoc without a new invariant.

nodes.title: Select connectivity or shortest-path machinery
nodes.summary: Choose union-find, BFS, Dijkstra, or Bellman-Ford from direction, weights, mutations, result, and failure contract.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects DSU for routes/deletions, BFS for unequal weights, Dijkstra for negative edges, and Bellman-Ford when simpler constraints suffice; states full costs.

nodes.title: Select BFS or DFS from the result contract
nodes.summary: Choose by shortest-hop/layer versus depth/finish/cycle needs and state direction, representation, disconnected coverage, and determinism.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects DFS for unweighted shortest hops, rejects BFS order as a dependency proof, and accounts for V+E plus sorting/stack choices.

nodes.title: Select set or map state
nodes.summary: Choose membership or per-key accumulation from the required query and preserve order separately when needed.
nodes.observableBehavior: Names key canonicalization/Eq/Hash, required associated state, expected-cost assumptions, distinct-key space, and output-order mechanism; rejects hashing when its guarantees do not fit.

nodes.title: Select and configure a heap
nodes.summary: Choose heap only for repeated extreme/top-k access and define max/min, ties, mutation, and complete method costs.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects FIFO/full-sort cases, uses BinaryHeap/Reverse correctly, creates deterministic Ord tuples, does not depend on iteration order, and analyzes n and k separately.

nodes.title: Select BTreeMap or an educational tree
nodes.summary: Use the standard ordered map for product work and custom boxed nodes only when traversal/invariant ownership is the learning target.
nodes.observableBehavior: Chooses BTreeMap for ordered keys/ranges, states Ord/key-stability requirements, and refuses a production custom BST absent a topology requirement.

nodes.title: Select pointer, window, prefix, or baseline
nodes.summary: Choose from ordering, contiguity, query count, updates, and monotonicity; reject a fashionable pattern when assumptions fail.
nodes.observableBehavior: Names pattern preconditions and total costs, distinguishes fixed/variable windows and static prefix queries, and chooses a scan/hash/other baseline for negatives or dynamic updates when needed.

nodes.title: Select the least sufficient Rust container
nodes.summary: Map required operations to Vec, VecDeque, or an evidenced linked representation and include amortization/traversal/contiguity costs.
nodes.observableBehavior: Uses Vec tail for stack and VecDeque back/front for queue, rejects Vec front shifts and speculative linked lists, and handles wrapped deque storage only when relevant.

nodes.title: Select or reject a single-pass state pattern
nodes.summary: Choose the pattern only when bounded state is sufficient for the processed prefix, otherwise explain what information prevents it.
nodes.observableBehavior: Starts from a correct baseline, states the necessary prefix summary, proves discarded history is irrelevant, and compares complexity with the baseline without overclaiming constants.

nodes.title: Select scan, exact search, or boundary search
nodes.summary: Choose from workload and result semantics, including preprocessing and updates rather than quoting only query cost.
nodes.observableBehavior: Distinguishes any-match, insertion-point, first/last boundary, and one-off scan needs; includes sorting/index maintenance in total complexity.

nodes.title: Select and prove traversal order
nodes.summary: Choose processing order from result dependencies and prove a subtree fold plus time/space bounds.
nodes.observableBehavior: States empty/leaf cases, child order, process timing, combine rule, O(n) work, and O(h) or O(width) frontier space; rejects a traversal whose timing cannot produce the result.

nodes.title: Select and model a trie
nodes.summary: Define exact/prefix behavior, terminal markers, key units, child layout, deterministic output, and measured alternatives.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects a trie for exact-only small workloads, handles prefix keys/empty keys/Unicode policy, and states time plus representation-dependent memory honestly.
