nodes.title: Design a bounded overload-aware pipeline
nodes.summary: Specify capacities in items/bytes/concurrency, propagation, overload/fairness/shutdown behavior, rate model, and observability.
nodes.observableBehavior: Finds hidden unbounded buffers, distinguishes bursts from sustained deficit, predicts queue age/memory, and handles slow/stopped/disconnected consumers.

nodes.title: Build valid bounded Arrow batches
nodes.summary: Append typed values and explicit nulls into equal-length columns and produce schema-matched repeated batches.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects wrong type/length/nullability, handles zero rows and batch boundaries, and accounts for variable-width bytes.

nodes.title: Reason from schedules to consistency claims
nodes.summary: Given N/R/W, versions, concurrency, delays, failures, and response policy, identify permitted client histories and CAP degraded behavior without slogan reasoning.
nodes.observableBehavior: Separates overlap from version selection and linearizability, constructs counterexamples, and states when operations respond, reject, or time out.

nodes.title: Contain and account for bad CSV records
nodes.summary: Choose all-or-nothing or quarantine, reconcile total/accepted/rejected counts, redact payloads, and enforce error thresholds.
nodes.observableBehavior: Produces stable replayable record errors, prevents silent partial success, and stops deterministically at count/rate/limit boundaries.

nodes.title: Design an Arrow schema and layout boundary
nodes.summary: Choose exact types, nullability, offset width, and batch shape from domain meaning and volume bounds.
nodes.observableBehavior: Explains buffers/offsets/validity, rejects name-only compatibility, and handles empty, Unicode, large-offset, and nested-value cases.

nodes.title: Design a CSV dialect and header contract
nodes.summary: Specify parsing, encoding, logical-record, header/width, trim, and empty/null behavior before typed conversion.
nodes.observableBehavior: Handles quoted delimiters/newlines/quotes, duplicate/reordered headers, invalid UTF-8, uneven records, and does not use split(',').

nodes.title: Design a Parquet layout and compatibility contract
nodes.summary: Choose supported schema mapping, row groups, pages/codecs, statistics/indexes, and version behavior from workloads and budgets.
nodes.observableBehavior: Separates Arrow from Parquet, explains hierarchy, rejects lossy types, and justifies row-group/codec/statistics choices with measurements.

nodes.title: Design a compatible Serde boundary
nodes.summary: Define wire representation, required/default/unknown fields, enum tagging, and fallible DTO-to-domain validation separately.
nodes.observableBehavior: Explains forward/backward compatibility cases, rejects semantically invalid decoded values, and does not expose raw DTOs as domain invariants.

nodes.title: Build a correct bounded DataFusion query
nodes.summary: Specify schemas/null/order/resource behavior, build relational intent, stream results, and verify with an independent oracle.
nodes.observableBehavior: Handles empty/null/duplicate/overflow/error inputs, avoids unproven collect, reconciles batches, and returns exact schema/order.

nodes.title: Diagnose DataFusion work with plans and metrics
nodes.summary: Compare equivalent plans/results under controlled data/configuration and support each improvement claim with normalized structure and runtime evidence.
nodes.observableBehavior: Explains selected files/columns, rows, partitions/exchanges, operator time/memory, and rejects brittle plan snapshots or timing-only conclusions.

nodes.title: Read logical and physical query plans
nodes.summary: Trace schema-aware intent into concrete scans/operators/partitions and identify pushdown, blocking, and exchange boundaries.
nodes.observableBehavior: Distinguishes logical/physical nodes, source pushdown from later filters, partial/final aggregation, and environment-dependent partitioning.

nodes.title: Diagnose and contain ingest failure
nodes.summary: Report stable source/record/class/cause context, redact payloads, and prove no partial invalid state crosses the boundary.
nodes.observableBehavior: Distinguishes I/O, UTF-8, framing, syntax, schema, domain, and limit errors and applies the declared fail-fast/quarantine policy deterministically.

nodes.title: Compute deterministic event-time windows
nodes.summary: Process an explicit event/watermark trace into correct main/late/cleanup transitions and bounded keyed aggregate state.
nodes.observableBehavior: Matches batch/reference windows for admitted events across arrival permutations and never closes from a faster partition alone.

nodes.title: Design an event-time/window contract
nodes.summary: Specify timestamp/key validation, window boundaries, watermark/idleness assumptions, triggers, lateness, output revisions, cleanup, state, and replay.
nodes.observableBehavior: Handles boundary timestamps, out-of-order partitions, idleness, late/too-late events, final watermark, state bounds, and append/upsert distinctions.

nodes.title: Emit and consume late window revisions safely
nodes.summary: Represent main/late results with stable identity/version and prove final sink state equals admitted-event aggregation.
nodes.observableBehavior: Avoids duplicate append totals, applies updates idempotently, routes too-late data, and finalizes/cleans at the declared horizon.

nodes.title: Prove bounded recovery with failure injection
nodes.summary: Run deterministic overload and crash cuts, compare failure-free/recovered final state/effects, and show capacity catches up within targets.
nodes.observableBehavior: Reconciles admitted/processed/rejected/dropped/replayed/effect counts, state/source positions, peak bytes/age, restore/replay time, and final equivalence.

nodes.title: Reason about concurrent table commits
nodes.summary: Distinguish staged files from visible state, select operation validation, refresh/retry safely, and produce serial committed snapshots or an explicit conflict.
nodes.observableBehavior: Merges compatible append metadata, rejects stale conflicting rewrites, explains atomic pointer visibility, and accounts for unreachable attempt files.

nodes.title: Design safe evidence-driven maintenance
nodes.summary: Set snapshot/in-progress retention, prove reference-safe deletion, and select data/manifest rewrites from measured overhead and logical-equivalence evidence.
nodes.observableBehavior: Protects retained snapshots and in-flight files, detects incomplete inventory risk, reports before/after costs, and preserves rows across compaction.

nodes.title: Reconstruct and prune a snapshot correctly
nodes.summary: Trace catalog→metadata→snapshot→manifest-list→manifest→file, honor schema/spec IDs, and prove conservative pruning plus residual evaluation.
nodes.observableBehavior: Ignores stray files, reproduces time travel, plans mixed specs, handles rename/reorder/null metrics, and never converts uncertain metadata into a false negative.

nodes.title: Build trustworthy run-to-artifact lineage
nodes.summary: Normalize exact dataset/job/run/artifact versions and lifecycle claims, preserve failures/unknowns/conflicts, and distinguish data derivation from scheduler order.
nodes.observableBehavior: Prevents namespace collisions, tolerates duplicate/out-of-order records, avoids invented edges, and explains every edge's producer evidence and confidence.

nodes.title: Answer impact and root-cause queries with uncertainty
nodes.summary: Trace version-specific upstream/downstream paths for a failed run, bad artifact, code/schema change, or proposed deletion and report missing evidence instead of guessing.
nodes.observableBehavior: Returns exact paths and boundary versions, separates control-only tasks, identifies incomplete/conflicting claims, and links affected rerun intervals.

nodes.title: Compact versioned runs without changing reads
nodes.summary: Merge sorted versions/tombstones under snapshot coverage, install atomically, and explain read/write/space amplification and stalls.
nodes.observableBehavior: Proves before/after point/range equivalence, preserves required deletes/versions, and accounts for bytes/files/temp space/pressure.

nodes.title: Design an LSM durability and visibility lifecycle
nodes.summary: Specify WAL/ack/sync, sequence, memtable, sorted-run, tombstone, flush/install, recovery, and pressure contracts.
nodes.observableBehavior: Orders every crash-sensitive step, resolves overlapping versions/deletes, bounds memory/WAL/disk, and distinguishes durability from application success.

nodes.title: Recover a miniature LSM at crash cut-points
nodes.summary: Replay valid committed WAL records over installed runs, reject torn/corrupt tails by policy, and reconcile acknowledged state.
nodes.observableBehavior: Passes before/after append/sync/apply/flush/install/retire cuts without losing acknowledged updates or double-applying visible state.

nodes.title: Investigate an SLO symptom with evidence
nodes.summary: Trace exact bad-event cohorts through correlated signals and dependencies, test hypotheses against baseline/failure/counterfactual evidence, and report cause confidence plus gaps.
nodes.observableBehavior: Does not equate correlation with causation, reports sampling/context loss, separates user symptom from resource clue, and identifies the next discriminating check.

nodes.title: Design deterministic retry and backfill
nodes.summary: Specify topology, intervals, versions, task states, atomic artifact identity, retry/reprocessing, concurrency, and reconciliation for fresh workflows.
nodes.observableBehavior: Finds now/latest reads, partial outputs, unstable keys, overlap races, gaps/duplicates, version drift, and unbounded backfill before execution.

nodes.title: Design a partition and replica topology
nodes.summary: Specify key/query locality, skew/cardinality/size, deterministic ownership, N, failure-domain placement, balance, and movement evidence.
nodes.observableBehavior: Finds hot keys and cross-partition queries, proves coverage/distinct placement, predicts correlated failures, and compares before/after ownership movement.

nodes.title: Prove minimized retention and deletion coverage
nodes.summary: Inventory element-level purposes/flows/copies/access/retention/deletion and demonstrate that expiry/deletion reaches primary, derived, cache, export, log and backup policy without overclaiming legal compliance.
nodes.observableBehavior: Removes unnecessary collection, finds hidden copies, distinguishes logical deletion/backup expiry, preserves required audit minimally, and reports unknown obligations to owners/legal review.

nodes.title: Process Arrow batches with checked typed access
nodes.summary: Check schema and downcasts, propagate nulls and arithmetic failures, preserve row alignment, and reason about slices.
nodes.observableBehavior: Returns typed errors instead of panics, never reads null storage, tests sliced offsets, and identifies retained-memory cost.

nodes.title: Design a bounded versioned transport protocol
nodes.summary: Specify transport guarantees, framing/envelope, size/resource limits, EOF/shutdown, deadlines, errors, correlation, evolution, and retry semantics.
nodes.observableBehavior: Chooses TCP/UDP deliberately, rejects implicit boundaries/liveness, caps every peer-controlled allocation/queue, and defines partial/canceled states.

nodes.title: Implement a chunking-invariant TCP codec/session
nodes.summary: Decode arbitrary fragments/coalescing, handle partial writes and clean/truncated EOF, correlate responses, and enforce deadlines/resources.
nodes.observableBehavior: Passes every byte split, multi-frame read, short-write, oversized/truncated, half-close, timeout, and slow-peer case without duplication/unbounded memory.

nodes.title: Implement a loss-tolerant bounded UDP exchange
nodes.summary: Correlate bounded datagrams and handle loss/duplicate/reorder/retry/idempotency/rate/deadline semantics explicitly.
nodes.observableBehavior: Completes only matching responses, never repeats logical side effects, stops under retry/deadline caps, and prefers TCP when custom reliability is unjustified.

nodes.title: State Raft client and liveness boundaries
nodes.summary: Distinguish durable log agreement from transaction isolation, physical execution from deduplicated logical effect, safety from majority-dependent progress, and core protocol from excluded extensions.
nodes.observableBehavior: Predicts timeout/retry after leader failure, uses stable request IDs, stops progress without majority, and refuses claims about transactions, Byzantine faults, membership, snapshots, or reads not modeled.

nodes.title: Prove Raft safety across schedules
nodes.summary: Trace persistent/volatile state and messages to justify election safety, log matching, leader completeness, current-term commitment, and state-machine safety.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects stale-term leaders and stale-log candidates, repairs only conflicting uncommitted suffixes, never directly commits old-term entries by replica count, and applies one command per committed index.

nodes.title: Design checkpoint/replay/sink guarantees
nodes.summary: Specify consistent state/position, durable completion, retention, restore/replay, effect IDs/transactions, guarantee scope, RPO/RTO, and catch-up.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects state-only offsets and blanket exactly-once claims, chooses idempotent effects, and handles incomplete/corrupt checkpoints plus replay duplicates.

nodes.title: Reconcile and prove replica convergence
nodes.summary: Detect concurrent/stale versions, apply an explicit merge policy, account for hints and anti-entropy, and prove all reachable replicas converge after healing within retention assumptions.
nodes.observableBehavior: Produces per-replica/version ledgers, handles failed/expired hints, measures repair debt, and compares the healed result with an independent history oracle.

nodes.title: Execute and explain a selective Parquet scan
nodes.summary: Project columns, prune only impossible regions, decode bounded batches, apply the exact predicate, and report read work.
nodes.observableBehavior: Produces a full-scan-equivalent result while reducing justified bytes/regions and handles missing/untrusted stats without false negatives.

nodes.title: Select and verify threat-matched controls
nodes.summary: From assets/actors/flows/threats choose standard validation/authz/minimization/crypto/key/secret/audit/dependency controls, negative tests, residual risk and change/review triggers.
nodes.observableBehavior: Prefers not storing data, standard libraries/native secret stores and shared guards, states encryption limits, tests rotation/compromise and feeds failures to root-cause prevention.

nodes.title: Prove a request fails closed across trust boundaries
nodes.summary: Given fresh request/resource/session/policy cases, show canonical validation, identity, tenant/object/action authorization, sensitive-action freshness, safe sink and redacted audit for every allow/deny/error path.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects client-only/denylist validation, IDOR/cross-tenant/stale-session/stale-role paths, default allow and secret/error leakage; locates one shared reference monitor.

nodes.title: Select bounded snapshot or framed ingestion
nodes.summary: Choose bytes/text, whole/buffered, EOF/delimiter, limits, and error/recovery behavior from source and workload contracts.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects unbounded whole reads and pseudo-streaming from_reader assumptions, handles invalid UTF-8/final records, and derives memory from limits.

nodes.title: Define and calculate a user-centered SLO
nodes.summary: Specify journey, valid/good events, target/window/exclusions/missing policy, budget/burn math and a proportionate decision for fresh workloads.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects convenient infrastructure proxies, handles zero/late/missing/duplicate traffic, reconciles exact counts, and distinguishes SLO/SLA/observed performance.

nodes.title: Design bounded safe cross-signal telemetry
nodes.summary: Choose metric types/units/labels/distributions, context propagation, structured log/span fields, sampling/redaction/retention and a series/storage budget.
nodes.observableBehavior: Predicts series cardinality, handles counter resets/units, preserves latency tails, correlates through context, and removes secrets/unneeded personal values.

nodes.title: Diagnose and prove transaction isolation
nodes.summary: From a fresh complete history, identify anomalies, construct a serial-order proof or counterexample, choose sufficient isolation/invariant protection, and scope rollback/durability/external effects.
nodes.observableBehavior: Finds write skew and predicate conflicts, rejects level-name folklore, discards aborted reads, retries the whole decision, and does not extend database atomicity to APIs/files/messages.

nodes.title: Stage CSV validation into domain data
nodes.summary: Separate structural, encoding, typed field, row-domain, and cross-row rules with checked conversion and exact location.
nodes.observableBehavior: Distinguishes absent/empty/null, rejects range/overflow/cross-field violations, validates uniqueness as a batch rule, and preserves raw versus normalized identity.

nodes.title: Write and verify finalized Parquet artifacts
nodes.summary: Encode bounded batches with explicit properties, control writer memory, finalize, reopen, reconcile, and publish safely.
nodes.observableBehavior: Handles zero/small/multi-group inputs, close failure, incompatible schema, memory thresholds, truncated output, and no partial publication.

nodes.title: Route attempt-first, consolidation, or direct instruction
nodes.summary: Use prerequisite evidence and one bounded attempt to decide whether to consolidate generated ideas, give targeted help, or teach directly without compulsory struggle.
nodes.observableBehavior: Preserves the attempt/error artifact, explains the route, and never treats time endured as evidence.

nodes.title: Interpret confidence separately from competence
nodes.summary: Commit confidence before feedback and explain raw calibration evidence across comparable immediate/delayed outcomes without using it to award mastery or label ability.
nodes.observableBehavior: Identifies insufficient samples, separates support/horizon, and distinguishes overconfidence, underconfidence, accuracy and resolution from competence state.

nodes.title: Discriminate among confusable strategies
nodes.summary: Select and justify the right strategy for fresh mixed items using structural cues, then execute it and explain why siblings do not fit.
nodes.observableBehavior: Commits before labels/feedback and distinguishes strategy-selection errors from implementation errors.

nodes.title: Interpret fresh delayed evidence
nodes.summary: Judge whether a later response supports retained independent performance from outcome alignment, freshness, actual lag, score and support provenance.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects immediate/copied/assisted evidence as sufficient while preserving it as useful practice history.

nodes.title: Read a Rust diagnostic before editing
nodes.summary: Identify code, primary span, relevant explanation, and the contradiction in the program model.
nodes.observableBehavior: The learner explains the diagnostic and predicts the next compile result before changing code.

nodes.title: Resolve a failure from compiler/tests and official docs
nodes.summary: Build an exact evidence packet, distinguish check/test/run scope, test one hypothesis at a time, and explain why the verified change addressed the cause.
nodes.observableBehavior: Reads spans/codes, writes a focused docs query, rejects an inapplicable suggestion, and reruns the correct evaluator.

nodes.title: Explain and verify a concrete error
nodes.summary: Trace evaluator evidence to a reviewable cause hypothesis, choose a minimal correction, verify it independently, and record a useful future cue/remediation.
nodes.observableBehavior: Separates symptom/category/cause, rejects vague trait labels, and cites artifacts before claiming resolution.

nodes.title: Detect recurrence or resolution on a fresh variant
nodes.summary: Use future cue/remediation on a changed item, classify same-versus-new cause from evidence, and append corrected/needs-confirmation/resolved or superseding state without erasing history.
nodes.observableBehavior: Does not close an error from reflection or one assisted rerun and distinguishes a new symptom from the same underlying cause.

nodes.title: Explain a worked solution's decisions and state
nodes.summary: Reconstruct why each consequential step follows from the goal, constraints, invariant and prior state, including non-examples and verification.
nodes.observableBehavior: Predicts a hidden next step and explains ownership/data flow or algorithm state without paraphrasing annotations.

nodes.title: Advance from completion to independent transfer
nodes.summary: Complete omitted steps, solve a fresh isomorphic item, select among confusable strategies, and transfer the outcome under a changed context without solution reveal.
nodes.observableBehavior: Produces independently evaluated artifacts at each stage and carries the invariant rather than copied surface form.

nodes.title: Place guidance from diagnostic evidence
nodes.summary: Choose or reopen the least redundant example/fading stage from fresh outcome evidence, errors, support and version, and explain the decision.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects biography/confidence placement and routes a later failure to a specific prerequisite or completion step.

nodes.title: Request and use proportionate help
nodes.summary: State the blocker, request the smallest useful level, perform a relevant new action, use bypass when needed, and accurately report how support changed the artifact.
nodes.observableBehavior: Does not click through unchanged, hide a reveal, or avoid needed help solely to protect a score.

nodes.title: Run an evidence-seeking debugging loop
nodes.summary: Given a failure, state an observation and hypothesis, choose a minimal test, and revise from the result.
nodes.observableBehavior: The attempt record contains observation, falsifiable hypothesis, expected result, action, and actual result in order.

nodes.title: Prove independence after supported work
nodes.summary: Declare tutor/external/AI support without shame, preserve the assisted artifact, and solve/explain a fresh delayed variant with no tutor help under the same outcome rubric.
nodes.observableBehavior: Does not equate assisted success with retained mastery or rely on surveillance claims to establish provenance.

nodes.title: Explain a mastery state from exact evidence
nodes.summary: Reconstruct the state/model/rule and cite qualifying/nonqualifying observations, variants, delay, support, transfer and unresolved misconceptions for a fresh outcome history.
nodes.observableBehavior: Rejects visits/completions/confidence/hints as promotion evidence and explains needs_confirmation without erasing prior learning.

nodes.title: Rebuild learner projections deterministically
nodes.summary: Validate idempotent append events, replay a declared event/observation/model version, and produce equal mastery/review snapshots and retained-coverage distribution with full provenance.
nodes.observableBehavior: Handles duplicate/out-of-order/invalid events transactionally and never repairs history by mutation.

nodes.title: Produce an answer before reveal
nodes.summary: Commit an outcome-aligned response before feedback and distinguish what was retrieved, inferred, guessed, or supplied by support.
nodes.observableBehavior: Leaves a timestamped pre-feedback artifact and accurately labels hints/resources/reveals rather than reconstructing independence afterward.

nodes.title: Recommend the next proof with a transparent reason
nodes.summary: Choose a fresh retention/transfer/confirmation/remediation/project-prerequisite item from due state and evidence, and show the exact calculation and nonpromotion boundary.
nodes.observableBehavior: Prioritizes later failure/critical misconception appropriately and does not recommend work for streaks, visits or hidden score optimization.

nodes.title: Calculate and explain a review schedule
nodes.summary: Derive due state from qualifying evidence, interval index, policy version and actual timing, including early, late, missed, failed and reopened cases.
nodes.observableBehavior: Reconciles event times and never advances mastery from a due date or silently rewrites a missed review.

nodes.title: Prove outcome transfer under declared changes
nodes.summary: Carry the invariant into an isomorphic, near, or far item and justify the transfer label from the transformation matrix and independent artifact.
nodes.observableBehavior: Names preserved structure and material changes instead of relying on novelty, topic name, or cosmetic edits.

nodes.title: Annotate a reference relationship
nodes.summary: Draw input/output borrow provenance and add only the lifetime parameters required to express the valid relationship.
nodes.observableBehavior: Identifies the referent for every returned/stored reference, predicts the usable overlap, applies elision when valid, and rejects annotations that pretend to extend data lifetime.

nodes.title: Audit an unsafe or FFI boundary
nodes.summary: Trace every unsafe operation to its documented obligation and prove the safe wrapper preserves it for all public safe calls.
nodes.observableBehavior: Enumerates aliasing, lifetime, layout, initialization, ownership, unwind, thread, and error invariants and identifies at least one safe-code mutation that would break a flawed wrapper.

nodes.title: Build a bounded columnar pipeline
nodes.summary: Convert validated records into schema-correct bounded Arrow batches and Parquet without whole-input collection.
nodes.observableBehavior: Explains ownership and allocation, enforces equal column lengths/schema/nullability, bounds batch size, writes Parquet, and passes a read-back oracle.

nodes.title: Build and explain an iterator pipeline
nodes.summary: Compose ownership-correct adapters and a consumer, predicting laziness, order, short-circuiting, and closure capture.
nodes.observableBehavior: Names when each closure runs, what it captures, which consumer drives the pipeline, and the resulting value without using collect reflexively.

nodes.title: Choose the async boundary
nodes.summary: Select sequential, native-thread, async-task, or isolated blocking execution from workload behavior.
nodes.observableBehavior: Names waiting versus CPU work, ownership, resource limits, runtime boundary, expected benefit, and failure behavior before introducing async.

nodes.title: Choose and access a standard collection
nodes.summary: Select Vec, String/&str, or HashMap and justify access/update behavior from the task's data contract.
nodes.observableBehavior: States ordering/key/text needs, chooses an absence/panic contract, and handles ownership without unnecessary cloning.

nodes.title: Choose a native concurrency model
nodes.summary: Select sequential execution, ownership transfer, message passing, or synchronized shared state from workload and invariant needs.
nodes.observableBehavior: Names the shared/owned data, communication topology, completion protocol, expected benefit, and remaining logical risks before adding threads.

nodes.title: Choose module versus crate boundary
nodes.summary: Keep related implementation in modules unless independent build, reuse, release, or dependency needs justify a package boundary.
nodes.observableBehavior: Given a small design, names the ownership/dependency reason for a module or crate split and rejects workspace complexity without such evidence.

nodes.title: Classify a failure path
nodes.summary: Choose Option, Result, or panic from the caller's recovery options and the invariant being protected.
nodes.observableBehavior: Names the responsible caller, available alternate action, lost information, and invariant before selecting absence, recoverable error, or panic.

nodes.title: Repair and prove a root cause
nodes.summary: Use diagnostics and experiments to identify the cause, make the smallest behavior-preserving fix, and add a regression test.
nodes.observableBehavior: States the hypothesis before editing, predicts the experiment, explains why the fix addresses the cause, and reruns both focused and full relevant verification.

nodes.title: Design bounded async work
nodes.summary: Define task ownership, admission limits, queue capacity, and backpressure for an asynchronous workflow.
nodes.observableBehavior: Draws task/channel ownership and demonstrates that overload reaches a specified wait, rejection, or shedding path without unbounded growth.

nodes.title: Design an error boundary
nodes.summary: Place handling and translation where domain or user policy is known and keep lower layers composable.
nodes.observableBehavior: Assigns each layer one responsibility, defines safe user and diagnostic outputs, and proves expected failures do not panic or disappear.

nodes.title: Design a minimally bounded generic API
nodes.summary: Remove real type duplication while expressing only the capabilities and type relationships the implementation needs.
nodes.observableBehavior: Identifies duplicated type structure, names required operations, chooses named generics or impl Trait deliberately, and rejects unused/speculative bounds.

nodes.title: Design a narrow public API
nodes.summary: Expose the smallest stable surface while keeping implementation modules and fields private.
nodes.observableBehavior: Chooses pub, restricted visibility, or pub use for each required consumer and demonstrates that unintended paths remain inaccessible.

nodes.title: Design a discriminating test oracle
nodes.summary: Translate a requirement into positive, boundary, and failure assertions at the smallest useful test layer.
nodes.observableBehavior: Explains why the assertion would fail for a plausible wrong implementation and selects unit, integration, or documentation scope from the observed contract.

nodes.title: Design completion and communication
nodes.summary: Define thread ownership, message/lock protocol, closure, join, panic, and disconnection behavior without assuming execution order.
nodes.observableBehavior: Draws ownership and wait-for edges, identifies every endpoint/handle drop, and proves no required work is abandoned or waits forever in the nominal/error paths.

nodes.title: Diagnose unfamiliar Rust independently
nodes.summary: Observe a compiler/test/runtime failure, form and test hypotheses, consult official docs precisely, and explain the root cause without generated fixes.
nodes.observableBehavior: Produces an observation/hypothesis/experiment log, identifies the minimal causal code or invariant, applies a focused fix, and preserves a regression test with support mode recorded.

nodes.title: Implement and use a trait contract
nodes.summary: Define behavior at the consumer boundary, implement it on valid local types, and call it through a correctly bounded API.
nodes.observableBehavior: States the behavior contract, checks coherence locality, implements required methods, and explains an E0277 failure without adding unrelated bounds.

nodes.title: Implement a Rust vertical slice
nodes.summary: Take an unseen typed requirement through API/data-flow design, error behavior, tests, concurrency/resource bounds where relevant, and clean integration.
nodes.observableBehavior: Delivers the smallest working path, names ownership/invariants/failure semantics, handles meaningful boundaries, and passes focused plus regression checks without speculative architecture.

nodes.title: Ingest and validate typed data
nodes.summary: Configure a row format, decode typed records, enforce domain rules, and preserve actionable rejection provenance.
nodes.observableBehavior: Processes valid, missing, malformed, extra-field, invalid-domain, and non-UTF-8 fixtures with a documented accept/reject/quarantine result for every row.

nodes.title: Isolate a deterministic failure
nodes.summary: Reproduce a failure with one command, control changing inputs, and reduce it without losing the causal mechanism.
nodes.observableBehavior: Records command, seed/environment/state, observed output, minimal fixture, and proof that the reduced case still fails for the same reason.

nodes.title: Justify or reject an advanced mechanism
nodes.summary: Compare safe/native alternatives and approve the smallest advanced boundary only from a concrete constraint and evidence plan.
nodes.observableBehavior: Writes the trigger, alternatives, benefit, new unchecked invariant, containment boundary, test/tool limits, rollback, and decision; rejecting the mechanism can fully satisfy the outcome.

nodes.title: Model bounded domain data
nodes.summary: Choose primitive, tuple, struct, and enum representations that make valid states and operations explicit.
nodes.observableBehavior: Defines types for a small domain and explains the invalid states prevented or still representable.

nodes.title: Operate a local production-shaped release
nodes.summary: Configure, start, health-check, observe, stop, restart, and diagnose a packaged service without hidden global state.
nodes.observableBehavior: Demonstrates validated configuration, provenance/version reporting, bounded logs, graceful shutdown, restart persistence expectations, and a recorded cold-start/size baseline.

nodes.title: Propagate with useful context
nodes.summary: Use match/combinators/question-mark deliberately while preserving cause and adding operation-specific context once.
nodes.observableBehavior: Traces the early return/conversion, identifies the source chain, and produces a diagnostic that locates the operation without duplicate logging or lost causes.

nodes.title: Prove cancellation and shutdown
nodes.summary: Test success, error, timeout, cancellation, and shutdown completion with controlled async time and observed task results.
nodes.observableBehavior: Shows no admitted task is silently detached, all terminal paths are observable, and the test reaches them without wall-clock sleeps as its oracle.

nodes.title: Prove a clean Rust release
nodes.summary: Run locked quality gates and package verification from a clean environment with recorded inputs and results.
nodes.observableBehavior: Produces a reviewable command/result manifest covering toolchain, lockfile, supported features/targets, checks, package list, artifact checksum, and known non-reproducible inputs.

nodes.title: Query and verify Arrow results
nodes.summary: Execute a DataFusion query over fixture data and compare schema/rows/nulls/order assumptions with an independent oracle.
nodes.observableBehavior: States ordering and null semantics, inspects output batches, handles execution errors, and proves expected aggregates/filters against a small independent result.

nodes.title: Repair a borrow conflict at its cause
nodes.summary: Explain overlapping uses and change ownership, borrow duration, or operation order while preserving behavior.
nodes.observableBehavior: Identifies conflicting accesses and their last uses, predicts the accepted repair, and rejects unnecessary clone/leak workarounds.

nodes.title: Select complementary advanced evidence
nodes.summary: Choose review, deterministic tests, Miri, fuzzing, or Loom from the failure class and state each tool's residual blind spots.
nodes.observableBehavior: Builds a failure-to-evidence matrix, demonstrates a seeded defect found by the selected tool, preserves a regression, and records what was not explored.

nodes.title: Select control flow from data shape
nodes.summary: Choose if, match, loop, while, or for from the data and termination contract and justify the choice.
nodes.observableBehavior: States branch coverage, exhaustiveness/termination behavior, and result type before implementation.

nodes.title: Choose ownership or borrowing at a function boundary
nodes.summary: Select owned, shared-reference, mutable-reference, or returned ownership from the function's responsibility and caller needs.
nodes.observableBehavior: States whether the callee must retain, read, mutate, or return the value and justifies the signature without reflexive cloning.

nodes.title: Select the smallest valid Rust quality command
nodes.summary: Choose check, test, Clippy, or a combination from the evidence required rather than habit.
nodes.observableBehavior: Names the desired evidence, command scope, expected output, and what a success would not prove.

nodes.title: Ship an operable Rust artifact
nodes.summary: Produce a clean locked package and demonstrate configuration, version/provenance, health, bounded output, shutdown, restart, and limitations.
nodes.observableBehavior: A reviewer follows documented commands from clean source to package, starts/stops/restarts it, verifies its acceptance behavior, and resolves all evidence to exact source and checksums.

nodes.title: Structure an inspectable workspace
nodes.summary: Create minimal package boundaries and prove membership, dependencies, features, lints, and profiles through Cargo metadata and commands.
nodes.observableBehavior: Explains every member and shared setting, emits format-versioned metadata, and removes a speculative package or feature without losing required behavior.

nodes.title: Test a concurrency invariant deterministically
nodes.summary: Construct a schedule-independent test that observes completion, shared-state invariants, disconnection, panic, or deadlock risk.
nodes.observableBehavior: Uses explicit synchronization or controlled hooks, repeats under varied interleavings, and fails for a deliberate protocol defect without using timing as the oracle.

nodes.title: Trace expression values
nodes.summary: Predict the type and value produced by blocks, branches, function bodies, and statement boundaries before compilation.
nodes.observableBehavior: Annotates evaluation order, branch choice, final expression, semicolon effect, and resulting type for a small program.

nodes.title: Trace iteration ownership
nodes.summary: Predict Item values and post-loop availability for borrowed, mutable, and consuming collection traversal.
nodes.observableBehavior: Annotates receiver mode, yielded Item shape, live borrows, moves, mutations, and whether the source remains usable before compiling.

nodes.title: Trace a module path
nodes.summary: Draw the crate/module tree and determine whether a concrete absolute or relative path resolves.
nodes.observableBehavior: Identifies the target crate root, module declarations, starting scope, path segments, and first inaccessible or missing segment before compiling.

nodes.title: Trace ownership and drop
nodes.summary: Mark owner, move/copy/clone operations, valid places, and cleanup for every relevant value in a small program.
nodes.observableBehavior: Produces a correct line-by-line ownership/drop trace before compilation and revises it from compiler evidence.

nodes.title: Transfer Rust models into a flagship stage
nodes.summary: Apply ownership, error, testing, concurrency/async, data, and release models selectively in PULSE, QUAY, or TESSERA and justify omissions.
nodes.observableBehavior: Maps the stage contract to prerequisite outcomes, builds the artifact independently, passes project-specific tests, records trade-offs/rejected alternatives, and identifies the next evidence gap.

nodes.title: Verify the active Rust toolchain
nodes.summary: Explain the winning override and record exact rustc, Cargo, and component availability before debugging version behavior.
nodes.observableBehavior: Runs rustup show and version/component checks from the project directory, then identifies the precedence source.

nodes.title: DP state, order, witness, and scale fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic empty/equal/unreachable/overflow and wrong-state/update-direction/pseudo-polynomial cases with exhaustive small search and witness oracles.
nodes.evaluatorKind: Rust unit/property fixtures with fixed seeds, exhaustive recursion/subset/edit oracle on small inputs, recurrence-table assertions, witness validator, update-direction trap, and capacity/resource ceilings
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible base/transition examples plus hidden missing-state, equal-tie, empty sequence, unreachable sentinel, ascending-0/1, overflow, and large-capacity cases; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: state meaning, operation/item order, tie/witness policy, string unit, numeric type, and value-only versus witness output are explicit

nodes.title: Partition, weighted-path, and failure fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic redundant-union/long-chain and equal-route/stale/unreachable/negative-edge/cycle/overflow cases with independent component and simple-path oracles.
nodes.evaluatorKind: Rust unit/property fixtures with fixed seeds, explicit component-set oracle, exhaustive small simple-path oracle, path/cycle-witness validators, heap stale-pop counters, and checked numeric boundaries
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible redundant-union and small route examples plus hidden invalid IDs, long sequences, equal ties, unreachable cycles, stale heap entries, and overflow boundaries; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: ID mapping, edge direction, weight type, tie/path policy, failure precedence, and component output order are explicit

nodes.title: Graph direction, discovery, and cycle fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic isolated/disconnected/converging/self/parallel/directed/undirected cases with shortest-hop and edge-precedence/cycle-witness oracles.
nodes.evaluatorKind: Rust unit/property fixtures with fixed seeds, exhaustive small-graph distance oracle, independent edge-order validator, cycle-witness validator, and enqueue-count instrumentation
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible layer/DAG examples plus hidden converging queues, disconnected vertices, multiple valid topological orders, self-loops, and directed-versus-undirected traps; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: graph direction, duplicate policy, vertex/start/neighbor order, and order-versus-property scoring are explicit

nodes.title: Greedy proof and counterexample fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic equal-tie/touch/weighted and fractional/integral/capacity-boundary cases with exhaustive optimum and rational-comparison oracles.
nodes.evaluatorKind: Rust unit/property fixtures with fixed seeds, exhaustive subset optimum for small intervals/items, exact rational comparison, feasibility/objective validators, and minimal-counterexample shrinking
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible earliest-finish and fractional examples plus hidden weighted intervals, indivisible density failures, equal ties, zero capacity/value, endpoint policies, and overflow boundaries; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: objective, divisibility, endpoint/tie policy, rational ordering, selected-set order, and property-versus-snapshot scoring are explicit

nodes.title: Priority and interval boundary fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic empty/equal/min-max/top-k and invalid/touching/contained/bridging interval cases with independent sort/filter/point-set oracles.
nodes.evaluatorKind: Rust unit/property fixtures with fixed seeds, full-sort top-k oracle, exhaustive small-domain union oracle, and heap-size/operation ceilings
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible empty/tie/touch examples plus hidden arbitrary heap layouts, priority mutation traps, bridge intervals, and policy variants; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: full priority tuple, endpoint convention, touch policy, and output order are explicit

nodes.title: Monotone run correctness and complexity fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic cases for empty/single/equal/decreasing/increasing/multiple-run inputs plus operation-count instrumentation.
nodes.evaluatorKind: deterministic Rust unit/property fixtures with independent O(n^2) oracle on small arrays
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible examples plus hidden fresh values and operation-count ceiling; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: fixed seeds and exact tie policy; no wall-clock benchmark as correctness evidence

nodes.title: Pointer, window, and prefix fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic empty/boundary/duplicate/negative/overflow cases with independent quadratic or linear oracles and endpoint-move counters.
nodes.evaluatorKind: Rust unit/property fixtures with fixed seeds, exhaustive small-range enumeration, independent nested-loop oracles, and exact endpoint-operation ceilings
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible boundary examples plus hidden negatives, extreme totals, zero/oversized windows, tie cases, and invalid ranges; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: tie rules and overflow outcomes are explicit; no wall-clock timing is used as complexity evidence

nodes.title: Recursive, restoration, and prefix-boundary fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic empty/deep/branching, early-exit/repeated-choice, prefix/terminal/Unicode-unit cases with independent iterative or exhaustive oracles.
nodes.evaluatorKind: Rust unit/property fixtures with fixed seeds, iterative structural oracle, exhaustive small-assignment oracle, sorted-vector prefix oracle, and restoration/depth instrumentation
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible empty/base/prefix examples plus hidden non-progress, early return, duplicates, prefix-as-key, empty-key, and byte/scalar cases; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: choice order, duplicate policy, key unit, normalization assumption, and result order are explicit

nodes.title: Ordering and search boundary fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic permutation/tie/duplicate/empty/extreme-index cases with independent linear scan and multiset oracles.
nodes.evaluatorKind: Rust unit/property fixtures with fixed seeds, stable decorated-reference sort, multiset equality, and linear exact/boundary oracles
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible empty/tie examples plus hidden fresh duplicates, all-side partitions, inconsistent-order traps, and workload choices; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: comparison keys and tie policy are explicit; assertions never depend on an allowed arbitrary duplicate match

nodes.title: Frontier order and owned-list fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic empty/interleaved/wrapped/retry/ownership cases with Vec-based reference models and exact operation ceilings.
nodes.evaluatorKind: Rust unit/property fixtures with fixed seeds, simple Vec reference traces, bounded retry oracle, and compile-time ownership tests
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible empty/order examples plus hidden wraparound, duplicate-value, retry-bound, and move/borrow cases; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: logical order is asserted independently of VecDeque physical split and retries are explicitly bounded

nodes.title: Stable string membership/count fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic ASCII/UTF-8/duplicate/order/empty cases plus independent sorting/count oracles on small inputs.
nodes.evaluatorKind: Rust unit/property fixtures with fixed seeds and independent canonical-vector oracle
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible boundary examples plus hidden fresh Unicode and order cases; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: expected output order is specified independently of randomized hash iteration

nodes.title: Tree order, bounds, and height fixtures
nodes.summary: Original deterministic empty/skewed/balanced/duplicate/global-invalid cases with independent recursive sequence and exhaustive-key oracles.
nodes.evaluatorKind: Rust unit/property fixtures with fixed seeds, explicit traversal reference vectors, bound-validation oracle, sorted-vector neighbor oracle, and visit/path counters
nodes.disclosurePolicy: visible empty/order examples plus hidden local-valid/global-invalid, skewed, duplicate-policy, and Ord-stability cases; no service-only solution
nodes.determinismRule: child order, duplicate policy, and predecessor/successor tie semantics are explicit

edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: A growth bound is meaningful only for a resource function derived from stated operation costs.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: The same code can have different best, worst, average, or expected resource functions.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: Amortized analysis must be distinguished from expected/average input analysis before it can be applied.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: Space analysis requires explicit treatment of input, output, recursion, allocation, copies, and working state.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: Initialization, maintenance, and termination operate on one precise loop-boundary predicate.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: Concrete Rust cost depends on whether iteration borrows, mutates, moves, clones, or allocates collection elements.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: Implementation measurement must retain the documented operation semantics and allocation/capacity assumptions used by analysis.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: A Rust single-pass scan consumes items lazily while carrying only the prefix summary state.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: The pattern is defined by a prefix-summary predicate preserved by each item update.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: The outcome requires deriving rather than naming time/space growth from code and assumptions.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: The learner must connect initialization, an arbitrary transition, and termination to the specification.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: Selection requires proving the state summarizes all relevant prefix information and discarded history is unnecessary.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: Notation instruction must expose omitted input, cost, case, and tightness assumptions.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: Sequence-total arguments must be distinguished from input distributions and randomized expectation.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: Finite examples cannot replace the arbitrary-iteration maintenance argument.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: The original problem requires maintaining current-run and best-run summaries over the processed prefix.

edges.rationale: The learner compares the quadratic oracle and linear scan with Rust operation/space assumptions.

edges.rationale: The tie-breaking and boundary cases require a precise current/best prefix invariant and termination argument.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: Deterministic edge cases and an independent small-input quadratic oracle check behavior while operation counts reject disguised quadratic scans.

edges.rationale: The mixed checkpoint requires a complete input/cost/case/time/space derivation on unseen code.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: The learner writes a general proof rather than citing the passing fixture set.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: Interleaved distractors require selecting the prefix-state pattern only where past information can be summarized safely.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: The delayed checkpoint changes surface context and includes non-matching distractors to test pattern selection rather than recall.
edges.author: Codex

edges.rationale: PULSE transformations and rollups require explicit prefix/batch invariants and resource bounds before performance claims are trusted.

edges.rationale: Array indexing and insertion costs depend on the represented element unit and shifts/copies counted.

edges.rationale: Hash performance and correctness assume stable equal-key hashing before collision/order costs are interpreted.
